full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 27-4-98 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge. Daudkandi, Comilla in allowing Miscellaneous Case No.7 of 1998 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was preferred against the ex parte decree dated 10-6-97 passed in Title Suit No. 4 of 1995 should not be set aside. 

 2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.4 of 1994 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge Sadar. Comilla for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession alleging, inter alia, that the opposite party who is a tenant under him has no title and possession. It was alleged that the opposite party has been serving in the police department and taking this advantage the opposite party in spite of ex parte decree obtained by him in Title Suit No. 4 of 1995 stood in the way of recovery of Khas possession for which he preferred Civil Revision No. 916 of 1997 before this Court against the order of the learned Assistant Judge, rejecting the prayer for striking out the name of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 i.e., the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police, Comilla, It was further alleged that the civil revision was allowed and the name of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 i.e. the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police. Comilla were struck off and, subsequently a date was fixed for ex parte disposal and accordingly, it was decreed ex parte on 10-6-97. The opposite party thereafter filed Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1998 under Order 9 rule 13 for setting aside the ex parte decree dated 10-6-97 and for restoration of the original suit to its file and number and the learned Assistant Judge allowed the Miscellaneous Case setting aside the ex parte decree and restoring the original suit to its file and number. 

 3. Mr. Mokhlesur Rahman, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the opposite party has no title and interest in the suit land and as such, Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1998 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure should have been dismissed by the learned Assistant Judge as not being maintainable. He submits that the learned Assistant Judge committed an illegality in allowing the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure setting aside the exparte decree dated 10-6-97 and restoring the original suit being No. 4 of 1995 to its file and number and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the learned Assistant Judge should be set aside. 

 5. Heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and perused the revisional application along with affidavit-in-opposition filed by the opposite party and counter affidavit with its Annexures. It appears that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.4 of 1995 before the Court of Assistant Judge, Comilla wherein he filed an application for striking out the name of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 i.e., the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police, Comilla from the plaint which was rejected by the learned Assistant Judge. It further appears that against this order of the learned Assistant Judge, the petitioner filed Civil Revision No. 916 of 1997 which was allowed striking out the name of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 from the plaint leaving only the petitioner as defendant. It also appears that after the order of the. High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 916 of 1997, the Title Suit No. 4 of 1995 was fixed for ex parte hearing on 10-6-97 on which date it was decreed ex parte. The learned Advocate for the opposite party contends that he has been in possession of the suit premises as a tenant under the Government as the same was declared vested and non-resident property. He further contends that he did not get any opportunity in filling written statement in Title Suit No. 4 of 1995 after the name of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 i.e. Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police, Comilla was struck off and that the suit was decreed ex parte to his prejudice for which the opposite party filed Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1995 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex parte order and for restoration of the original suit to its file and number and the learned Assistant Judge after due consideration allowed the miscellaneous case and restored the original title suit to its file and number subject to payment of compensatory cost of Taka 2000.00 and, as such, learned Assistant Judge did not commit any illegality in allowing the Miscellaneous Case. He also submits that the learned Assistant Judge by the impugned order dated 27-4-98 allowed the Miscellaneous Case with compensatory cost of Taka 2000.00 which was made condition precedent and that on being deposited the same by the petitioner, the opposite party withdrew the same and thereafter the learned Assistant Judge restored the original suit to its file and number and, as such, the petitioner cannot assail the order of the learned Assistant Judge after receipt of the compensatory cost. The petitioner as it appears, himself withdrew the compensatory cost of Taka 2000.00 by granting a receipt and that after such payment the learned Assistant Judge restored the suit to its file and number after setting aside the ex parte decree dated 10-7-97. The learned Advocate for the opposite party in support of his contention has cited the case of Purvada Satyanarayan Amurthy vs Gadepalli Sundara Rao, reported in AIR 1938 (Madras) 603 wherein it was held that the decree holder after accepting cost without protest cannot subsequently attack the court's order setting aside the ex parte decree. In the instant case the petitioner has accepted the compensatory cost of Taka 2000.00 awarded-by the learned Assistant Judge who after payment of compensatory cost set aside the ex parte decree and restored the original suit to its original file and number. In view of this admitted fact and the principle as enunciated in the above ruling, I am also constrained to hold the view that since the decree holder petitioner accepted the cost so he cannot attack the court's order for setting aside the ex parte decree as the petitioner cannot approbate and reprobate at the same time. It further appears that the learned Assistant Judge set aside the impugned order for ends of justice and also to give the opposite party an opportunity to contest the original suit after the names of the defendant Nos. 2-3 i.e., the Deputy Commissioner and Superintendent of Police, Comilla were struck off from the plaint. In this view of the fact and circumstances of the case, I do not find that the learned Assistant Judge committed any illegality in allowing the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The petitioner is, therefore, not entitled to the relief as prayed for. So, this revision must fail.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Md. Ali Asgar Khan

parties:
Kashem Sardar ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Afsaruddin Mia ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
D.M. Ansaruddin Ahmed, J.: This Rule, issued on an application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff, is directed against the judgment and decree passed on 7.8.1990 in Title Appeal No. 153 or 1986 by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna, affirming those passed on 19.7.1986 by the Munsif, Batiagatha Upazilla, District Khulna dismising Title Suit No.143 of 1984 (Originally Title suit No.393 of 1979 of the court of Munsif, Khulna.) 

 3. Briefly stated, the plaintiffs' case is that the suit properties originally belongs to Rajani, Nimchand and Dharmachand in equal shares. Rajani's interest ultimately devolved upon defendant Nos.22 to 24 and this is not relevant for the purpose of the suit. Nimchand was succeeded by 2 sons named Santosh and Moniram. The interest of Santosh devolved upon his only son Hazari Lal (defendant No.1) and Moniram died leaving issueless widow named Kumudini. On the other hand, Dharmachand died leaving 4 sons namely Kalicharan, Behari, Swarup and Baburam. Baburam died ummarried, and Behari and Swarup died leaving issueless widows named Sharathi and Sourabhi respectively. All the 3 widows Patta settled their interest in favour of Benode, Nirode and Mohesh (defendant No.12), who knowing fully well that their interest in the property extinguished with the death of the widows, transferred the same in favour of defendant No.13 to 19. It is stated that on the death of the 3 widows, their life interest reverted to defendant No.1 who thus became owner in possession of 9-annas share in the properties (including that inherited from his father), out of which he transferred 3.30 acres of lands to the plaintiffs by a registered kabala dated 6.5.1969 (Ext.1). Since then the plaintiffs are in possession thereof by getting their names mutated. On 19.11.1979, however, defendants Nos. 14 to 19 threatened to dispossess them from the suit lands. It may be mentioned, however, that on 15.7.1985 48 plaintiffs filed a petition without serving any copy on the other side for amendment of the plaint schedule adding as follows: 

 5. At the trial, including the second plaintiffs son 6 P.Ws. and including the contesting defendant 2 D.Ws. had been examined and the parties put into evidence certain documents in support of their respective claims. The learned Munsif, on consideration of the only evidence of P.W.4 to the effect that before the plaintiffs the suit lands were possessed by the pattadars of the 3 widows, held that since defendant No.1 had no possession in the suit lands, the plaintiffs could not be held to have any possession therein. He accordingly dismissed the suit. In the appeal preferred by the plaintiffs against the decree of dismissal, the learned Subordinate Judge has held that the suit lands are not properly defined and specified and since the parties are in joint possession of the properties, the plaintiffs are not entitled to permanent injunction without partition by metes and bounds. He has accordingly dismissed the appeal. It is against this appellate judgment and decree of affirmance that the plaintiffs have obtained the instant Rule. 

 6. It has been urged by Mr. Latifur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioner-plaintiffs, that the learned Subordinate Judge has erred in law in not considering the amendment petition and also not discussing the evidence on possession adduced on the plaintiffs side. He submits that the suit lands have been clearly defined with boundaries in the proposed amendment and that non-consideration of the material evidence on the exclusive possession of the plaintiffs in the suit lands has resulted in error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Sk. Matlub Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No.19, on the other hand submits that the amendment petition having not been pressed and disposed of, may be dermed to have been rejected by implication and as such the injunction has been rightly refused in respect of the unspecified lands. He further submits that there are complicated questions of title to the suit properties involved and as such the plaintiffs cannot get the relief except in a properly framed suit for title. According to him, in view of the defective frame of the suit, there was no necessity for discussion of the evidence on possession. 

 7. It appears from the judgment of the trial Judge that he framed and took up for consideration some unnecessary issues such as the issues on limitation, defect of parties at the plaintiffs' right, title and interest in the suit lands and also simply reproduced the arguments advanced by the learned advocates of the parties but without making any observation or comment thereon. The only discussion and finding which have been made the basis of his decision is that P.W.4 Dhirendra stated that Mohesh, Nerode and Benode possessed the suit lands before the plaintiffs and as such defendant No.1 Hazari Lal never possessed the lands and consequently assertion of the plaintiffs as their possession of the lands is false. On the other hand, the learned Subordinate Judge has not taken notice of the reason given by the learned Munsif in arriving at his decision. The learned Subordinate Judge has held that the suit lands as described in the schedule to the plaint are unspecified and the properties being in joint possession of the parties, no injunction could be granted without partition. Neither of the courts below has given any finding on the defence plea of maintainability of the suit on which a specific issue was framed and taken up by the trial court in its judgment. 

 8. As to the vagueness in the description of the suit lands in the original plaint schedule, Mr. Rahman has nothing to say. He represents that the trial court or the appellate court ought to have taken into consideration the amendment petition in which, according to him, the suit lands have been clearly described. He could not however lay his hands upon anything on record to show that the amendment petition was ever moved or pressed by the plaintiffs. It is true that the petition still remains undisposed of. But the question is whose responsibility it was to get an order passed thereon. The petition was filed without serving on the other side a copy thereof which was actually received by the other side after a period of 6 months. It was the plaintiffs responsibility to press the petition in time and get an order thereon. If a petition is filed but not moved or pressed and ultimately remains unnoticed by the court and indisposed of. It cannot but is held to have been not pressed and as such rejected by implication. The result, therefore, is that the suit lands as described in the plaint schedule is vague, indefinite and unspecified and no injunction can issue in respect of such, properties. 

 9. Even if, for the sake of the argument, the amendment petition is taken into consideration, the nature of evidence adduced on the plaintiffs' side regarding the description of the suit lands does not, in any manner, improve the plaintiffs' case, in the amendment petition the suit land has seen stated to be in a compact block bound on the north by Nagen and Upen and on the cast by Haripada and Monorangan whereas according to P.W.2 Hazari Lal, one Afsar Mia is the eastern boundary man and according to P.W.4 Dhirendra he holds lands on eastern and northern boundaries of the suit land and yet P.W.6 Golam Rahman says to east of the suit land are Dhiren(P.W.4) and Niren. In the amendment petition, the names of the eastern boundary-men are given as Haripada and Monoranjan and those of the northern boundary-man as Nagen and upon. It is, therefore, clear that the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs on the exact identity and location of the suit land are not in conformity with the description given in the amendment petition. It may be noted that no sketch map has been added with the plaint schedule and none knows how much land is there within the stated boundaries. Thus, even if the amendment petition is taken into consideration, the plaintiff's case remains exactly where it was in the original plaint. The learned Subordinate in the original plaint. The learned Subordinate Judge cannot, therefore, be said to have taken any erroneous view when he observes that the suit land is vague and unspecified. 

 10. As to maintainability of the suit which has not been considered by either of the courts below it appears that serious complicated question of title are involved in the suit. There in nothing on record to show as to how defendant no. I Hazarilal acquired the life-interest of Sarathi and Shouravi, or in other words, 9-annas interest in the suit properties as claimed in the plaint. The plaint itself is silent as to how Hazarilal and after him the plaintiffs got or entered into possession of the suit properties; in order so make up the deficiency, a new case beyond pleading has been attempted to be made out by introducing from the mouth of Hazarilal a story of frocible ouster by him of the transfers from the 3 widows. Further, the more, the plaintiffs' Kabala Ext. I shows that they purchased Hazari's interest as inherited by him from his father and also devolved upon him as reversioner from Kumudini, whereas the plaintiffs have claimed the interest enjoyed by the other 2 widows as life interest and transferred by them to Nerode and Mohesh. The question of legal necessity behind the transfers by the widows is yet a complicated question of title involved. Again, the plaintiffs Kabala Ext.1 speaks of transfer in their favour of 3.30 acres out of 10.97 acres of lands, where the area described in the plaint schedule in 9.97 acres. It may be mentioned, however, that the total area of the holding belonging to the original holders named Rajani, Nimchand and Dharmachand as recorded in C.S. Khatian No.19 comprising 2 plots No. 453(75) and No. 454(10.04) was 10.79 acres. During S.A. operations, the entire plot No.453 and 9.04 acres out of plot No.454 with a total area of 9.79 acres have been recorded in S.A. Khatain No.19/1 and the remaining 1100 acre out of plot No.454 remains unexplained. Having purchased from the entire 10.79 acres of the properties, i.e., the 2 entire plots, the plaintiffs have brought the suit leaving aside the aforesaid 1.00 acre of land. I cannot but, therefore agree with Mr. Matlub Ahmed. Serious complicated question of title are involved in the suit. It has been clearly laid down in the case of Rafizuddin Ahmad Vs. Mongla Barmon & ors reported in 43 DLR (AD) 215 that if the dispute involved complicated question of title the plaintiff must establish hid title, by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. Simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing device for ascertainment of title. In this case the plaintiffs alleged title is not clear and they do not appear to have prima facie title to the lands claimed in the suit. True, the courts below have not properly discussed the evidence adduced by the parties on possession of the land; but in view of the findings I have arrived at, the discussion of evidence on possession is simply redundant. Because, if the suit lands are allowed to remain vague and unspecified and the plaintiffs fail to prove their prima facie title there to, the suit itself fails for non-maintainability. 

 11. On a careful consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to hold that the courts below has not committed any error of law in finding that the suit lands are vague and not properly specified. In addition, there is a further finding that the plaintiffs cannot maintain the suit without selling their title established to the properties. The appellate court is well justified in affirming the judgment of the trail court dismissing the suit. In such view of the matter, the impugned judgment and decree is not to be interfered with in revision.

parties:
Baby and others  -------- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioners
vs
Md. Chand Miah and others ------ Defendant- Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
"Records be called for. Let a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-12 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 4-1-2021 (decree being drawn on 11-1-2021) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 377 of 2012 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 29-8-2012 (decree being drawn on 2-9-2012) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 114 of 2010 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are, inter alia, that the petitioners and the opposite party Nos. 70-71 filed Title Suit No. 05 of 1993 in the 4th Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka for partition of the suit property stating, inter alma, that the suit property originally belonged to Maghu Chowkider and his name was correctly recorded in CS Khatian. Thereafter, Meghu Chowkider died leaving behind two sons, namely-Sheikh Yeasin and Kalimuddin. The property appertaining to schedule Nos. 4 and 5 of the plaint belonged to Sheikh Yeasin. Sheikh Yeasin died in the year 1946 leaving 3 sons, namely-Momtazuddin, Sultan and Magrab Ali, 3 daughters, namely Sharifunnessa, Uttam Nessa and Joytunnessa who possessed the property left by Sheikh Yeasin in ejmali. Thereafter, Momtazuddin died in the year 1968 leaving behind one son, namely Abdul Awal, wife Moti Bibi and 5 daughters Anwara, Fulbanu, Afatunnessa, Sademunnessa and Saleha Khatun. Abdul Awal died in the year 1970 leaving behind mother Moti Bibi, wife Shamsunnahar, 3 sons Montu, Reazuddin and Jashimuddin and 4 daughters Farida, Arjuda, Parul and Kuna. Magrab Ali also died in the year 1962 leaving behind wife Dona Bibi, 3 sons, namely Abdul Matin, Salahuddin and Chand Miah and 4 daughters, namely Nazia Khatun, Razia Khatun, Hamida Khatun and Sufia Khatun. Kalimuddin transferred his share to Salimuddin by way of gift. Salimuddin died in the year 1974 leaving behind wife Talemunnessa, 2 sons, namely Nasir Uddin and Abdul Majid and 7 daughters, namely Akter Banu, Nur Banu, Pari Banu, Angura, Hosne Bibi, Shamsunrkahar, Nurunnahar, Abdul Karim and Abdur Rahim. Thereafter, Abdur Rahim died in the year 1965 leaving behind wife Kadbanu, two sons, namely Zaman Mollah and Hasan Mollah and four daughters, namely Madina, Kulsum, Nazma, Hanufa. Abdul Karim died in the year 1970 leaving behind wife Mabia, and 4 sons, namely Mohsin, Shafiullah, Md. Anis and Md. Yunus. The defendant Nos. 23-45 inherited 11 annas share of Salimuddin. Joytunnssa and the daughter of Yeasin died leaving behind 3 sons, namely Ramizuddin, Rafizuddin, Tafizuddin and 3 daughters, namely Falani, Rahimon, Anna Bibi and Debjan Bibi inherited from Joytunnessa. The defendant Nos. 52-67 are reported to have purchased a portion of the said property and, as such, they have been made as party. The plaintiffs are the successive heirs of the 3 daughters of Sheikh Yeasin and they are entitled to get 1 anna 15 gonda 2 kara 2/3 kranti share from the property. The plaintiffs have been possessing the property by way of ejmali share. The plaintiffs requested the defendants for partition of their shares, but the defendants did not agree with the prayer of the plaintiffs and, as such, they filed the suit for partition of the suit property against the defendants. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 15-18, 19, 68-71 and 73 contested the suit by filing a written statement stating, inter alia, that the Meghu Chowkider was the original owner of the suit property and died leaving behind 2 sons, namely Sheikh Yeasin and Kalimuddin. They claimed to have purchased 29 decimals of land from the suit land from the heirs of 3 sons of Magrab Ali by the registered deeds dated 4-10-1978 and 6-11-1978 from the suit plot No. 1433. At the time of the trial, the plaintiffs examined two witnesses, namely Sanaullah (PW1) and Md. Siraj Miah (PW2). The defendant Nos. 15-18 and 72-73 examined three witnesses including the defendant No. 16 on behalf of the defendant Nos. 68-71 and 73 and the defendant No. 68 himself and they were cross-examined by the plaintiff. After conclusion of the trial, the Trial Court dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 25-11-1999. 

 5. Impugning the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred First Appeal No. 156 of 2000 before the High Court Division. After hearing, the High Court Division was pleased to allow the appeal and accordingly sent back the suit on remand with a direction to dispose of the original Suit as per the observation made in the body of the judgment. After hearing the parties, the Trial Court dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 19-4-2012. 

 6. Challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiffs again preferred Title Appeal No. 377 of 2012 before the Court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka. After admitting the appeal and observing all other formalities, the learned District Judge was pleased to transmit the record to the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Dhaka for disposal. Upon hearing, the learned Additional District Judge was pleased to dismiss the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 4-1-2021. Being aggrieved by and highly dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiff-petitioners moved this Court and obtained the aforesaid Rule and status quo thereto. 

 10. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman (Helal), the learned Advocate with Mr. Mintu Kumar Mondal appearing for the opposite party Nos.73-109 submits that both the Courts below correctly found that Sheikh Yeasin was the predecessor of the plaintiffs and contesting defendants gifted the suit land to his three sons by means of three heba-bil-ewaz deeds and his three daughters got ornaments and cattle heads and, as such, after the sad demise of Sheikh Yeasin, the three daughters did not claim their shares before filing the present suit and therefore, there is no apparent reason to interfere with the concurrent finding of the facts as there is no misreading, non-consideration of evidence and non-interpretation of law critically involved in this case. In this respect, he has referred to the case reported in 15 BLD (AD) 82. He further submits that the opposite party Nos. 73-101 claimed their title through Kalim Uddin and not Sheikh Yeasin and the plaintiffs claimed their portion of land from Sheikh Yeasin and, as such, the suit is decreed and they are entitled to get saham of 0.1323 acre of land since the predecessor of the added opposite parties Abdul Latif was not made party and the observation is required to be given in the judgment. In this connection, the predecessor of the added opposite party Nos. 73-101 became the owners of 0.15 acre of land by way of purchase as well as exchange in the year, 1990-94 and accordingly, separate city survey khatian being No. 5685/1 was duly prepared and published in his name but the plaintiff filed the suit without impleading him as defendant and, as such, the suit is bad for defect of party. 

 "When the terms of any such contract, grant or other disposition of property or any matter required by law to be reduced to the form of a document, have been proved according to the last section, no evidence of any oral agreement or statement shall be admitted, as between the parties to any such instrument or their representatives in interest, for the purpose of contradicting, varying, adding to, or subtracting from, its terms; Proviso (1). Any fact may be proved which would invalidate any document, or which would entitle any person to any decree or order relating thereto; such as fraud, intimidation, illegality, want of due execution, want of capacity in any contracting party, want or failure of consideration, or mistake in fact or law. 

 17. On perusal of the recital of impugned deeds, it appears that the executant transferred the land as mentioned in the three heba-bil-ewaz deeds upon receiving the Holy Quran and the jainamaz, therefore, it cannot be held that the aforesaid deeds were not genuine and the Courts below considering the facts and circumstances of the case rightly held that the aforesaid three deeds are genuine but the Courts below wrongly held that the rest of the property of Yeasin was transferred by the oral gift. To be a valid oral gift under the Muslim Law, there must be an offer, acceptance and delivery of possession. The defendants by adducing cogent and reliable evidence hopelessly failed to prove the story of the oral gift that Yeasin transferred his rest of the land to his aforesaid three sons. The contention of the defendants is that the three heba-bil-ewaz deeds were registered on 23-11-1945 and the oral gift was made on 31-12-1945. It is preposterous to believe on the facts and circumstances of the case that after one month of registered heba-bil-ewaz deed, Yeasin transferred the rest of his property depriving his three daughters but the Courts below without any valid reason accepted the contention of the oral gift made by Yeasin. The DW-1 in his evidence stated that in lieu of the property, Yeasin paid money, ornaments and cattle heads to his three daughters but it is not supported by any evidence. The Courts below failed to consider that being daughters of Sheikh Yeasin, they have every right to inherit the properties of their father. Unless it is proved by cogent and reliable evidence that they gave up their claim to their right of inheritance or they were totally ousted by Sheikh Yeasin by legal means. The possession of the co-sharers cannot be adverse to other co-sharers is a well-established principle of law but the Courts below hopelessly failed to consider the same. In our society, it is common phenomenon that after marriage the female co-sharers live separately with their husbands' abodes and they exercise their right of possession through their brothers and others. The Trial Court wrongly held that since SA and RS records were not prepared in the names of the plaintiff-petitioners, they were not entitled to get any share from Sheikh Yeasin. The record of right does not confer any title and it will in no way disentitle the co-sharers to have their shares through the intervention of the Court. 

 18. The opposite party Nos. 73-101 claimed their title through Kalimudddin; the full brother of Yeasin and therefore, they are entitled to get saham in respect of 0.1323 acre of land as successive purchaser and exchanged deed. The said land was duly recorded in the city survey; therefore, the defendant Nos. 73-101 may continue their construction work because the plaintiff-petitioners have got no right to interfere with the construction work started by the aforesaid defendants in the afore noted land admittedly belonged to Kalimuddin. 

 19. The facts and circumstances of the instant case are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the cases referred to by the learned Advocate for the petitioners. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, my penultimate conclusion is that the land belonging to the three heba bil ewaz deeds shall not be included in the saham of the three daughters of Sheikh Yeasin. In respect of the rest of the land, the sons shall be entitled to get saham in respect of 6/9 share and the daughters shall entitle to get saham in respect of 3/9 share. 

 20. In the result, the Rule is made absolute in part. The impugned judgment and decree of the Court below is hereby set-aside in part. Accordingly, the Title Suit No. 1145 of 2010 (original Title Suit No. 129 of 1978) is decreed in part in preliminary form. The plaintiffs shall get '5/9 shares in respect of the suit land belonging to Sheikh Yeasin excluding the land apper-taining to registered heba-bil-ewaj deeds being Nos. 4250/1945, 4251/1945 and 4252/1945 (Exhibits-Ga, Gha, Uma). The parties are directed to effect partition amicably by metes and bounds within 60(sixty) days from the date of receipt of this judgment by the Trial Court failing which, the parties may get their shares on partition through the intervention of the court by appointing an Advocate Commissioner. The defendants may pray for their saham before the trial court after submitting requisite court fees, if so advised. The Advocate Commissioner shall consider the possession, convenience and inconvenience of the parties and value of the land in distributing the saham among the parties to the suit. The earlier order of status quo granted by this Court, thus, stands recalled and vacated.

parties:
Md. Meraj Miah ----Plaintiff-appellant-petitioner.
Versus
Mossammat Alufa Khatun and others ---Defendant-respondent-opposite parties.
full_judgment:
Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder J: On an application under Section 115(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule, at the instance of the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner, was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 31.05.2010 (decree signed on 07.06.2010) passed by learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Habiganj in Title Appeal No.09 of 2007 affirming the impugned judgment and decree dated 27.08.2006 (decree signed on 07.09.2006) passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Lakhai, Habiganj in Title Suit No.09 of 2001, should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts of the plaintiff’s suit relevant to disposal of the Rule, in nutshell, is that the plaintiff instituted the suit seeking declaration of title to the suit land described in the 1st schedule to the plaint as well as for a further declaration that the exparte decree passed in the Title Suit No.35 of 1995 is illegal, collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff. It is stated in the plaint that the suit land measuring .39 acre of land of plot Nos. 6395, 6412 and 6413 appertaining to Khatian Nos. 2416 and 2416/1 along with many other lands belonged to one Luda Miah, the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-9 and Arjat Ali, the defendant No. 10. The S.A. Khatian No. 2416 was prepared accordingly. Thereafter, Luda Miah died leaving behind his one wife Kulsum alias Kulsuma, two sons Lakindar and Lukandar and a daughter Alufa Khatun. Lukhandar died leaving behind a wife Rejia Khatun and a daughter Nigara Khatun. The plaintiff got .13 acre of land in plot No. 6412 through exchange vide deed No. 1216 dated 15.09.1994 from the heirs of Lakinder. The plaintiff purchased .28 acre of land of plot Nos. 6412, 6413 and 6395 from the heirs of Lukander by virtue of a registered kabla deed No. 2518 dated 07.12.1995. After obtaining permission of the court, the defendant No. 8 sold out her share as well as the share of her daughter i.e. the defendant No. 9, to the plaintiff. The plaintiff erected two houses on the suit plot No. 6412 within the knowledge of the defendant No. 1 and has been living there with his family. The plaintiff mutated the suit land in his name under the mutation case No. 496/94-95 and got the mutation khatian No. 2416/1. The plaintiff has been owning and possessing the suit property by paying rents to the Government. During R.S. operation, the attested khatian has also been prepared in the name of the plaintiff within the full knowledge of the defendants. The defendant No. 1, in collusion with other cunning defendants, managed to get an ex-parte decree in respect of 10.5 acres of land in the Title Suit No. 35/95. The plaintiff was a necessary party to that suit but he was not impleaded therein. It is also stated that Luda Miah alias Ekram Hossain being the owner and possessor of the suit land of Title Suit No. 35/95, during his lifetime, transferred the land of plot Nos. 6412 and 6413 to his two sons Lakindar and Lukandar by registered deed of gift and handed over possession of the same to them. As such, the daughter of Luda Miah is not entitled to get any share in plot Nos. 6412 and 6413 mentioned in Title Suit No. 35 of 1995. So the exparte decree is collusive, illegal, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff came to know about the Title suit No.35 of 1995 on 01.04.2001. Hence, the suit. 

 3. On the other hand, the defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the statements made in the plaint. The case of the defendant No. 1, in brief, is that Luda Miah i.e. the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-9 was the owner of the 1st scheduled land with other land by way of inheritance and was possessing the same. He died leaving behind a wife Kulsuma, a daughter Alufa Khatun and two sons namely Lakindar i.e. the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 3-7 and Lukandar i.e. the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 8 and 9. It is further stated that as an heir of Luda Miah, the defendant No. 1 has duly got a separate share measuring 10.5 decimals of land in Title Suit No. 35/95. The documents of the plaintiff are false and fabricated and those are not binding upon the defendant No. 1. The plaintiff was not a necessary party to Title Suit No. 35/95. The plaintiff has brought the suit on a false statement with an ulterior motive to deprive the defendant No. 1 from her paternal property. Hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 2. Has the plaintiff any title and possession over the suit land? 

 3. Is the plaintiff bound by the expartee decree passed in Title suit No.35 of 1995 dated 07/03/1996? 

 4. Is the plaintiff entitled to get a decree as prayed for? 

 5. Is the plaintiff entitled to any further relief? ” 

 6. Upon hearing both the parties, the learned trial judge dismissed the suit against which the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 91/2003 before the District Judge, Habiganj. The learned judge of the Appellate court, after hearing the parties sent the suit on remand. At that stage, the plaint was amended on 17.10.2005 and the defendant No. 1 filed additional written statement on 24.01.2006. PW1 and DW1 were re-examined on 23.07.2006. The plaintiff produced the gift deed No. 5284 dated 07.08.1963 as exhibit No. 4. However, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff did not give proper legal advice to the plaintiff-petitioner for exhibiting and proving the registered sale deed No. 2518 dated 07.12.1995, exchange deed No. 1216 dated 15.09.1994 and other necessary documents although the same were produced and then kept with the record. 

 iv) Whether the plaintiffs have title and possession over the suit property? 

 v). Whether the plaintiffs are entitled to get decree as prayed for? 

 8. After hearing both the parties and on perusal of the evidence on record, the learned Assistant Judge, Lakhai, Habiganj dismissed Title Suit No. 09/2001. 

 11. At the very outset, Mr. Mohiuddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner, submits that the petitioner is claiming the suit land on the basis of registered exchange deed being No. 1216 dated 15.09.1994 and registered sale deed being No. 2518 dated 07.12.1995 from the legal heirs of Luda Miah, the S.A. recorded owner as such the petitioner is a cosharer in the suit holding; more so, during the last revised settlement operation, the attested Khatian was also prepared in the name of the petitioner and the petitioner has been in possession of the suit property by erecting two houses and has been living therein with his family; Moreover, DW 1 in cross-examination very clearly stated that “মেরাজ মিয়াকে মামলার পক্ষ করি নাই।......... এখানে মেরাজের ২টা ঘর আছে।” the learned trial judge also came to a positive finding to this effect; since the opposite party No. 1 inserted the suit property in the schedule to the plaint of Title Suit No. 35/95, the petitioner is a necessary party as co-sharer in the said suit and the opposite party ought to have impleaded the petitioner as the defendant in the suit; therefore, the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 35/95 is illegal, collusive and not binding upon the petitioner as such without considering the same, the learned judges of the courts below dismissed the suit and appeal causing serious miscarriage of justice. 

 12. He next submits that Luda Miah being the original owner of the suit property gifted the entire land of the suit plot Nos. 6412, 6413 measuring 3 Poua equivalent to .26 acre of land to his sons Lukandar and Lakindar vide registered gift deed being No. 5284 dated 07.08.1963 marked as exhibit No. 4 and delivered possession of the same in favour of them; the petitioner got the suit property by registered deed of exchange and sale deed from the heirs of Lukandar and Lakindar; thereafter, the opposite party No. 1 being a daughter of Luda Miah had nothing to inherit from suit plot Nos. 6412 and 6413; in spite of that, these two plots were included in Title Suit No. 35/95 and the opposite party No. 1 had been allotted saham in the aforesaid plots; however, the learned judges of both the courts below failed to consider the gift deed marked as exhibit 4 as such the impugned judgments and decrees passed by the learned judges of the courts below are based on non-reading and non-consideration of the documents on record. 

 14. He candidly submits that the plaintiff-petitioner filed all the documents in support of his title and possession in respect of the suit property and deposed categorically in his deposition that “২৫২৮নং দলিলের মূলকপি দাখিল করেছি। এই দলিলের তারিখ ৭-২-৯৫ ইং ১২১৬/৯৪ নং দলিলের সহি মোহরী নকল দাখিল করেছি। ২৪১৬ নং খতিয়ানের কপি (নামজারী) যাহা রাজস্ব অফিসার কর্তৃক সত্যায়িত দাখিল করেছি। বর্তমান জরিপের ডিপি খতিয়ান নং-১৫৫৭ এর সহি মোহরী দাখিল করেছি। ২৪১৬ খতিয়ানের মূলকপি দাখিল করেছি। এই সেই মূলকপি। ইহা প্রদ: ১। ডিসিআর প্রদ: ২। খাজনা আদায়ের রশিদ ২। খানা প্রদ: ৩ সিরিজ।” The mode of proving of documentary evidence is a question of law and a litigant public like the petitioner does not know by whom and in what manner a document should be formally proved; the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner did not provide proper legal advice to the petitioner to take proper steps for proving formally the aforesaid registered sale deed and deed of exchange in accordance with law; the learned Advocate for the plaintiff did not take any step in this regard even after sending back the suit on remand; the petitioner had no negligence or laches on his part in his regard; rather, it was a gross negligence and laches of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff; the learned judges of the courts below did not consider the facts that all the documents of the plaintiff with regard to title and possession of suit land were produced and kept with the record but those were not properly exhibited due to the negligence, laches and want of proper legal advice of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff and for the negligence and want of proper legal advice of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner, the plaintiff-petitioner should not suffer for the wrongs committed by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner; but the learned judges of the courts below without considering the same dismissed the suit and appeal and thus have committed serious miscarriage of justice. 

 16. I have gone through the revisional application, examined and perused the judgments and decrees passed by the learned Judges of the Courts below and the evidence available on record. On perusal of the revisional application and other materials/evidence on record, it is evident that the petitioner being plaintiff instituted a suit for declaration of title to the land mentioned in the schedule to the plaint. In order to prove the title over the suit land, the learned trial judge recorded evidence of 3 witnesses of the plaintiff and also recorded evidence of 3 witnesses of the defendants. 

 17. The pertinent question raised by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner is that the plaintiff in order to prove his title over the suit land produced original registered sale deed being No.2528 dated 07.02.1995 and the certified copy of the sale deed No.1216/94 dated 15.09.1994 before the trial Court but those were not marked as exhibits for want of proper legal advice of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner during trial of the suit as a result of which neither the learned judge of the trial court nor the learned Judge of the appellate court took the same into consideration. 

 “On perusal of the record, it is seen that plaintiff did not submit any scrap of original paper or documentary evidence in support of his claim nor examine any witness to prove his claim. It is seen that a certified copy of the said exchange deed has been kept on the record but the plaintiff did not take any step to prove the document properly.” 

 “On perusal of the documents submitted by the plaintiff, it is found that the plaintiff filed the said original deed which is kept on the record, but it is neither exhibited nor has the execution of the deed been proud by the testimony of the competent persons properly.” 

 21. As per submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, the plaintiff in order to prove his title over the suit land produced original registered sale deed being No.2528 dated 07.02.1995 and the certified copy of the sale deed No.1216/94 dated 15.09.1994 before the trial Court but those were not marked as exhibits for want of proper legal advice of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner during trial of the suit as a result of which neither the learned judge of the trial court nor the learned Judge of the appellate court took the same into consideration and for this reason, both the learned judges of the courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 22. From the above evidence, it is clear that the plaintiff produced the original deeds of title before the trial court to prove his title over the suit land but since those documents were not marked as exhibits, those were not taken into consideration by none of the learned judges of the courts below. 

 24. It is now well settled that for the laches, negligence and want of proper legal advice of the learned advocate for the plaintiff to prove the deeds of title, the plaintiff as litigant public cannot suffer for the wrongs which were committed by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff. In the decision taken in the case of Jobeda Khatun and others Vs. Md. Hamid Ali being dead his heirs Taherun Nessa and others, reported in 40DLR(AD)(1988)101, it was held as under:- 

 31. In consequence thereof, the impugned judgment and decree dated 31.05.2010 (decree signed on 07.06.2010) passed by learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Habiganj, in Title Appeal No.09 of 2007 affirming the impugned judgment and decree dated 27.08.2006 (decree signed on 07.09.2006) passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Lakhai, Habiganj in Title Suit No.09 of 2001 are set aside and the suit is sent on remand to the trial Court for exhibiting, proving and examining the witnesses if required to prove deed No.2528 dated 07.02.1995 and the certified copy of the deed No.1216/1994 and other documents already produced by the plaintiff which are kept with the record giving an opportunity to the defendants to cross-examine the witnesses if any in this regard if so advised.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Md. Nazrul Islam Talukder

parties:
Arun Chandra Debnath and others -------- Plaintiff-Respondent-Petitioners
VS
Narayan Nath and others -------- Defendant-Respondent-Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 17-4-2005 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge and Special District Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No.34 of 2004 reversing the judgment and decree dated 17-3-1996 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gournadi, Barisal in Title Suit No. 37 of 1993 decreeing the suit should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original suit for Partition being Title Suit No. 37 of 1993 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Gournadi against the defendant-opposite parties contending inter alia, that the suit jote appertaining to Mouza Horohoro under JL No. 176 corresponding to SA khatian No. 274 in plots No. 856/857 comprising an area of 82 decimals of land originally belonged to one Moti Lal and Sarda Sundari Debi in 04 annas and 12 annas share each. The land described in paragraph No. 1 of the plaint comprising an area of 201/2 decimals was correctly recorded in the name of Matilal Debnath, which was owned and possessed by Motilal and in the year 1958 he died leaving behind one daughter having son Laxmi Rani Debi. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that Laxmi Rani as owner of the land mutated her name in a mutation proceeding and paid rent therein. Thereafter; on 23-9-1985 she gifted the suit land in favour of her three sons the plaintiffs No. 1-3. The plaintiff-petitioners after acquiring title in the suit land by virtue of that deed of gift from their mother, in the Mutation Case being No. 1376(1X-11) 85-86 mutated their names and possessing the same after payment of rent. The plaintiffs are possessing their portion of land in ejmali with other co-sharers of the holding and facing difficulty in ejmali possession and for that; they requested the defendants to make amicable partition in respect of their 201/2 decimals of land, but the defendants denied after claiming the suit property; on the basis of a forged sub-kabala deed executed by Matilal Debnath in favour of the defendant's predecessor, which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit for partition. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendant No.1 in short is thus, that the plaintiffs instituted the original suit on false and fabricated claim to grab the properties which is barred by limitation, bad for defect of parties and not maintainable contending inter alia that the suit jote in fact; originally belonged to Matilal Debnath and Saroda Sunduri Debi in 04 annas and 12 annas share each and the record of right was correctly prepared in their names. Saroda Sunduri was issueless and after her demise her entire property was inherited by the defendant No. 1. The further case of the defendant-opposite parties is such that Motilal for want of money on 01.01.1963 A.D. transferred his share in favour of the defendant's father by a registered sub-kabala deed and after the death of their father; the defendant-opposite party become the owner of that land and in the recent field survey; the entire 82 decimals of the suit jote has been recorded in the name of the defendant No.1. The plaintiffs knowing about the field record filed an appeal case in the office of the Zonal settlement Officer, Barisal and the Zonal Settlement Officer analyzing of the oral and documentary evidence produced before him; dismissed the appeal on 15-5-1993 AD. Thereafter, the plaintiffs only to harass the defendants filed the original suit for partition on false allegations and in fact Motilal Debnath not died without son and he had two sons namely Krishna Kanta Debnath and Bijoy Krishna Debnath who are residing in India with their family members as Indian nationals. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after framing 08 different issues decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiffs and thereafter by his judgment a and decree dated 17-3-1996 decreed the suit on contest against the contesting defendant No.1 and ex-parte against the rest. 

 5. Being aggrieved the defendant No.1 preferred an appeal being Civil Appeal No. 34 of 2004 in the court of learned District Judge, Barisal which was transmitted to the Court of learned Divisional Special Judge and Special District Judge, Barisal for hearing and disposal and the learned appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-4-2005 allowed the civil appeal and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and also dismissed the original suit for partition. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that, the learned lower appellate court during passing the impugned judgment and order committed illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that, the deed of gift marked as Exhibit-3 was not a valid deed of transfer in favour of the plaintiff-petitioners by their mother Laxmi Rani Debi, but as reversionary the plaintiff-petitioners are entitled the suit land inasmuch as the admitted owner Motilal Debnath had no son and daughter excepting the only daughter Laxmi Rani having son the plaintiffs to the suit and under the 'Hindu Diavaga Law' at the demise of Laxmi Rani Debi the plaintiffs as reversioners have right, title, interest and possession in the suit land measuring 201/2 decimals of land. The learned Advocate also submits that the appellate court below failed to consider the factual aspect of the case and the principle of law in its true perspective. The learned counsel during his submissions argued that in the plaint, it was positive case of the plaintiffs that the mother of the plaintiffs Laxmi Rani was the only daughter having son of Matilal Debnath and for that reason Laxmi Rani Debi became the owner of the land left behind her father Motilal. The learned Advocate submits that by way of .reversionary right under 'Hindu Doyavaga Law' the claim of the plaintiffs has been established by sufficient, cogent' evidence which has been ignored by the appellate court and thereby the court of appeal committed misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate argued that although there is a counter positive case from the side of the defendant-opposite parties that Motilal Debnath excepting his daughter Laxmi Rani had two other sons, in their pleading, but it is decided, by the learned appellate court below conclusively after proper sifting of evidence that the defendants have failed to prove the existence of two sons of Motilal Debnath namely Krishna Kanta Debnath and 'Bijoy Kanta Debnath. Under section 102 of the Evidence act the onus of proof in this regard lies upon the defendant-opposite party since they have brought a specific case, but they have hopelessly failed to prove that case by any tangible evidence. The defendant's witnesses in different stage stated different things and number of the sons of Motilal Debnath which is inconsistent with the pleading of the defendants. The learned Advocate in support of his contention referred some decisions of Indian Jurisdiction and those are: AIR 1987 (SC) 1242:which was under the provision laid down in Order VI, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, AIR 1977 (SC) 1158 on the provision laid down in Order VI, rule 2 of Code of Civil Procedure and AIR 1961 Calcutta 620, on the provisions laid down in Order VI, rule 6 and Order VIII, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure and besides this; the learned Advocate Mr Saha referred a decision of this court in the case of Zamir Uddin Ahmed vs Ziaul Huq, 49 DLR 622 under the provision laid down in Order VI, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Referring the cited decisions the learned Advocate for the petitioners lastly submits that the litigant people should not suffer for poor drafting of the pleadings and despite there is no specific mention in the plaint of the plaintiff-petitioners that their mother Laxmi Rani Debi became the owner of the land left behind her father Motilal Debnath on the basis of her reversionary right, even then; the court is empowered under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to consider the petitioner's submissions given by him in his arguments at present. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned senior Advocate Mr Debdas Samaddar appearing on behalf of the opposite party No.1 opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that, the law is blind and nobody is above law. The learned Advocate further submits that it is decided by the learned court below that the title document of the plaintiff-petitioners is not a legal document by which the land can be transferred by Laxmi Rani in favour of her sons the plaintiffs. Furthermore; there is no evidence and pleading of the plaintiffs that Laxmi Rani had reversionary right from the admitted owner Motilal Debnath inasmuch as; she was the only daughter of Motilal having son at the time of death of Motilal Debnath. The title document of the plaintiffs i.e. the deed of gift as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs in their plaint has been decided a value less document under law having no legal force and realizing that fact; the plaintiff-petitioners rare now taking a new device to grab the property, bringing a new case without their pleadings and evidence on ,records that as reversioner they are entitled the suit land measuring 201/2 decimals of land in SA khatian No. 274 which stands recorded in the name of Motilal Debnath. The learned Advocate also submits that the judgment and decree of the learned lower appellate court is not perverse and the learned appellate court rightly after proper assessment of evidence, and appreciation of law decided the merit of the suit against the plaintiffs and in passing the impugned judgment and decree no such misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice has done by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned counsel argued that it is a decided matter that the' court cannot consider anything beyond the pleadings of the parties. The learned Advocate in support of his contention have referred some decisions of our Apex Court passed in the case of Shamsul Huda (Md) being dead his heirs Hafez Md Ismail vs Bangladesh, 5 BLC (AD) 108, on the provision laid down in Order VI, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the case of Tara Mia vs Babru Mia, 12 BLC (AD) 222 on the provision laid down under Order VI, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and finally in the case of Md Hazrat Ali vs Joynal Abedin, 1986 BLD (AD) 45, on the inherent power of the Court. 

 12. On perusal of the case records it transpires that the plaintiff-petitioners instituted the original suit for partition for getting a separate saham in respect of the land described in schedule-'ka' of the plaint comprising an area of 201/2 decimals of land appertaining to J.L. No 176 under police station-Gournadi of. Bakerganj District in Mouza-176 Horohoro corresponding to plot No.856/857 under SA. khatian No. 274 comprising total area 82 decimals of land, out of which; claiming 04 annas share in the land of suit the holding the plaintiffs filed the original suit for partition along with a specific pleading that the suit land had been owning and possessing by the recorded tenant Motilal and in the year 1958 AD he died leaving behind his only daughter Laxmi Rani Debi who at the demise of her father Motilal inherited the suit land and thereafter transferred the suit land by a deed of gift dated 23-9-1985 in favour of her sons the present plaintiff-petitioners and thus the- plaintiffs have acquired title and interest in the suit land claimed by them. 

 13. Vis-à-vis; the contesting defendant-opposite party No.1 brought out a specific case in his pleading that the recorded tenant Motilal Debnath died leaving behind not only Laxmi Rani but also two sons namely Krishna Kanta and Bijoy Krishna. The contesting defendant challenged the right, title, interest of the plaintiffs; on the basis of their deed of gift from Laxmi Rani. He has brought out a case in the pleading that Motilal transferred the `ka' schedule land along with non-suited 3 decimals of land in favour of his father by a registered kabala deed dated 1-1-1963 and after the death of his father the defendant-opposite party acquired the same by way of inheritance. 

 17. PW 3 Abdur Rob is a man of suit village Horohoro. This witness has stated about the possession of the plaintiffs and he stated nothing about the son or daughter of Motilal or about the original owner of the suit land. 

 22. During cross-examination in reply to a question from the side for the plaintiffs, the defendant No. 1 as DW 1 frankly admitted that, they did not file the original title deed. He also testified that he is not able to submit 2nd certified copy of their title document (kabala deed). This witness expressed his inability to show any paper showing the existence of 3rd son of Motilal Debnath. 

 30. Be that as it may; the provisions laid down in Order VI, rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure is definitely a legal embargo in getting the relief as prayed for from the side of the plaintiffs. Despite; the defendant-opposite party by producing cogent tangible evidence could not prove their respective case, even then; it is the incumbent duty upon the plaintiffs to discharge their onus of proof in proving their acquisition of title. If it is found that the plaintiffs have failed to discharge their onus in proving their case, they are not in a position to get the Rule absolute. In the instant case; as I have already spelt out that, Rule 7 of Order VI of the Code of Civil Procedure is a legal bar in granting the relief as prayed for in the instant suit inasmuch as "no pleading shall, except by way of amendment, raise any new ground of claim or contain any allegation of fact inconsistent with the previous pleadings of the parties pleading the same." 

 31. The provision of law is such that, firstly; the pleading of the plaintiff must contain those facts that have given right to one or more rights of relief. The plaintiff must alleged a cause of action describing particular instance which substantive law entitles him to relief or in other words, he must alleged facts showing defendant's duty towards him. 

 There may be thousands of defects in the documents of the defence as well as their case but that does not entitle, the plaintiff to get a decree. The plaintiff is to prove his case • irrespective of the defence version of the case. 

 38. In the result, the Rule having no merit be discharged. The impugned judgment and decree dated 17-4-2005 passed by the learned Divisional Special Judge and Special District Judge, Barisal in Title Appeal No.34 of 2004 reversing the judgment and decree dated 17-3-1996 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gournadi, Barisal in Title Suit No. 37 of 1993 is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Syed Amir Ali alias Syed ----- Faizul Islam
Vs.
Syed Asaddar Ali and others ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker J: This appeal is directed at the instance of the plaintiff-appellant against the judgment and decree dated 18-4-2010 and 21-4-2010 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj, in Title Suit No. 15 of 2006 rejecting the plaint. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the appeal in a nut shell can be stated thus the present appellant as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit being No. 15 of 2006 in the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Sunamganj against the present respondents who were defendants to the original suit for Specific Performance of Contract of sale in respect of the suit property and further declaration that the kabala deed being No. 1100 of 2005 dated 24-5-2005 is illegal, void, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff with a prayer for confirmation of possession. After service of summons notice upon the defendants therein the defendant-respondents appeared, and filed a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the contents of the plaint among which there was a contention from the side of the defendants that the suit as has been filed is not maintainable. While the suit was ready for pre emptory hearing the defendant-respondents again on 3-2-2010 filed an application under Order VII, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the plaint would be rejected under section 21A(b) of the Specific Relief Act. The learned trial Judge by his order dated 18-4-2010 rejected the plaint of. Title Suit No. 15 of 2006 and thereby dismissing the suit. 

 5. The teamed Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the learned trial Judge i.e. the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj during passing the impugned order committed illegality and during pre-emptory hearing stage of the original suit the defendant-respondents filed an application for rejection of the plaint along with dis-missal of the original suit. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Joint District Judge in rejecting the plaint failed to consider that the plaintiff has been in possession of the suit land on the basis of a contract dated 12-8-2004.The learned Advocate also submits that the learned court below misdirected himself in the question of law and facts. The relief sought for in the original plaint was not properly considered by the learned court below. The learned trial court ought to have found that the plaintiff filed the suit for acquisition of title by adverse possession from the father of the executant of bainapatra dated 24-7-2004 and lastly the learned Advocate submits, that the court below erroneously held that the suit is not maintainable under section 21A(b) of the Specific Relief Act and the trial Judge with-out going through the contents of the plaint being failed to consider the materials on record on surmise and conjecture passed the impugned order which is liable to be set aside. 

 6. As against the aforesaid submissions of the teamed Advocate of the appellant the teamed Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents opposing the grounds of the-appeal-memo controverted the argument advanced from the side of the teamed counsel of the appellant and submits that the learned trial Judge was quite justified and legal in passing the impugned order dated 18-4-2010 inasmuch as violating the provisions laid down in section 21A(b) of the Specific Relief Act (Act XVI of 1908) without depositing the balance amount of consideration of the contract the suit for specific of contract has been filed by the plaintiff. The teamed Advocate further submits that from the very beginning of filing of the written statement it was alleged from the side of the defendants that the suit as instituted is not maintainable. During pendency of the suit the defendants to the original suit again filed an application under Order VII, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure and brought a definite cause for which the suit is liable to be dismissed as the plaint would be rejected under the provisions of law and the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj vide his order dated 184-2010 rightly held that the bainapatra which was submitted from the side of the plain-tiff is shown to have executed on 12-8-2004 and in that bainapatra there is a recital that the consideration amount is Taka 5,25,000 (Taka Five lac and twenty five thousand). Out of that total amount of consideration money only Taka 4,00,000 (Taka Four lac) was paid m favour of the executant and Taka 1,25,000 Taka One lac and twenty five thousand) was due. The learned Advocate lastly submits that it is apparent MM the face of the record that the plaintiff to the suit at the time of filling of the original suit not deposited the balance consideration amount and, .as such, the suit was not maintainable. The learned trial Judge rightly under the provision of law rejected" the plaint and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and order. 

 7. I have considered the submissions of the teamed Advocates and have gone through the relevant papers including the plaint itself and the impugned order of the teamed Joint District fudge, 1st Court, Sunamganj dated 18-4-2010 and 21-4-2010 in Title Suit No. 15of2006. 

 8. On perusal of the papers it transpires that the plaintiff-appellant instituted the original suit for specific performance of contract and cancellation of a sub-kabala deed being No. 1100 dated 24-5-2005 with confirmation of possession in the suit property appertaining to Mouza Syedpur corresponding to JL, No.133 of settlement khatian No.1505 and 1669 and present khatian No. 4046 in plot No. 4567:11 is also apparent from the case records that in the suit for specific performance of contract the bainanama deed upon which the plaintiff banked upon was for consideration amount of Taka 5,25,000 (Taka :Five lac and twenty five thousand) and it was contended by the plaintiff that out of the total consideration amount the defendant No. 1 who was the executant of the deed accepted Taka 4,00,000 (Taka Four lac) and executed the bainanama but subsequently denying to takes the balance consideration amount of Taka 1,25,000 (Taka One lac and  twenty five thousand) the defendant-ago/8 jj dents on 16-12-2005 refused to execudroister the kabala deed in favour of which is the cause of action of the original suit. 

 9. It further transpires from the case records that the defendants during pendency of the original suit on 3-2-2010 filed an application for rejection of the plaint under Order VII, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure staling that the suit is barred by law as the plaintiff have failed to deposit the balance consideration amount of Taka Taka 1,25,000 (Taka One lac and twenty five thousand) at the time of institution of the original suit. 

 14. Iry the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 18-4-2010 and 21-4-2010 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj, in Title Suit No. 15 of 2006 is hereby upheld and con-firmed.
