parties:
Md. Hanif Miah being dead his legal heirs 1(a) Md. Zamal and others ----- Respondent-Petitioners. 
Versus
Dukhu Miah being dead his legal heirs: I (a) Mosammat Asura Begum and others ----- Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. I(a)-I(b) to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.02.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 8'h Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No, 250 of 1997 and 249 of 1997 analogously reversing the judgment and decree dated 17.08.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Keraniganj, Dhaka in analogous disposal of Title Suit Nos. 113 of 1995 and 132 of 1994 respectively should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 3. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rules in a nutshell can be stated thus. the present petitioners being plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 132 of 1994 in the court of learned Assistant Judge, Keraniganj, Dhaka for declaration of title in the suit property and Title Suit No. 113 of 1995 for eviction of the permissive possessors from the disputed land contending inter ahu that the suit land measuring .07 acres along with 0.14 acres of land originally belonged to one Dhana bibi which was owned and possessed by her the C.S. recorded tenant. Dhana bibi died leaving behind her only brother Hazi Miah Kha Hazi Miah Kha while possessing the suit land by way of inheritance died leaving only son Moharamad Yasin who sold out 0.07 acres of land in favour of one Hawa bibi, wife of Ashraf uddin in the year 1956 A.D. by an unregistered deed. Mohammad Yasin delivered possession therein in favour of Hawa Bibi. The further case of the plaintiff-petitioners is such that the said unregistered deed was lost during the war of liberation. Mohammad Yasin died leaving behind four sons namely Abdur Rahim, Abdur Rashid, Abdul Mazid and Abdul Monnaf Kha who possess 14 decimals of land in the suit plot. The S.A. record of right was correctly prepared in their names. Abdul Mazid died leaving his daughter Nafisa Khatun and her brother Monnaf Kha as his heirs. Nafisa Khatun transferred her share in favour of one Nazir Ahmed orally. Abdul Monnaf, Nazir Ahmed and Abdul Hamid Khan by way of a registered sub-kabla deed dated 08.04.1976 transferred their 14 decimals of land in favour of one Hanif Miah. The R.S. record was prepared in the name of Hawa Bibi and Hanif Miah for that portion of land. Subsequently, Hawa Bibi at the request of her brother Dukhu Miah handed over 7(seven) decimals of land in which Dukhu Miah is a permissive possessor with a condition to hand over the same. In the year 1984 Dukhu Miah obtained that permission. Hawa Bibi by way of transfer deed dated 18.11.1985 transferred 7(seven) decimals of land in favour of Md. Hanif Miah by a registered sub-kabla deed. At the time of purchase the purchaser Hanif Miah permitted Dukhu Mia to reside in the land with a condition to handover the same in his favour in future. Hawa Bibi died at her 67 years of age. Hanif Miah after mutating his name possessing the land of the suit plot after payment of rent and died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 1-7 as his legal heirs. The plaintiffs for their necessity on 10.07.1995 asked the defendants to surrender possession in their favour for the suit land but they refused which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suits. 

 4. The contrary case of the defendant-opposite parties in short is thus that the land of C.S. khatian No.14 had been owned and possessed by the C.S. recorded tenant Dhana. Bibi Dhana Bibi died leaving behind one son Ashraf uddin and she had no brother namely Nazi Mia Kha. Ashraf uddin during his life time transferred the entire land in favour of his wife Hawa Bibi and accordingly S.A. khatian was prepared in the name of Hawa Bibi. Hawa Bibi was partially insane and she allowed her brother Dukhu Miah to reside in her residence. Thereafter, she died on 02.07.1984 A.D. and she was buried in Azimpur graveyard. The defendants as legal heirs of his sister possess the suit land and since the death of Hawa Bibi the defendants are possessing without any interruption. The R.S. record in respect of the suit land was wrongly prepared and the plaintiffs to grab the property on false allegation filed the original suits which are liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The learned trial court after hearing the suit decreed Title Suit No. 113 of 1995 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 132 of 1994. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred two appeals being Title Appeal No. 249 of 1997 and 250 of 1997 respectively in the court of learned District Judge, Dhaka. The appeals were transmitted to the learned Additional District Judge, 8'5 Court. Dhaka for hearing and disposal and the learned lower appellate court hearing the appeals analogously allowed the appeals reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28.02.2005 and 06.03.2005 respectively. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court below during disposal of the appeals committed illegality in deciding the merit of the appeals and not assessed the evidence on records properly resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Additional District Judge did not consider the exhibited documents which were produced from the sides of the respective parties anti failed to appreciate that the plaintiff was able to prove that the defendant was permissive possessor of the suit land. The learned Advocate also submits that admittedly the original C.S. khatian which has been marked as exhibit-`E' stands recorded in the name of Dhana Bibi. The superior landlord of Dhana Bibi as it appears is one Misrash Hazi Miah Kha who is the brother of the present petitioners. The learned lower appellate court illegally held that Mirsah Hazi Miah Kha is not the brother of the petitioners but in deciding this; no reason was given and as such the learned appellate court erroneously held that the superior landlord is not the brother of the present petitioners. The learned Advocate submits that the opposite parties during trial of the original suits failed to produce any evidence to show that the father of Mirash Hazi Miah Kha is a different individual with that of the present petitioner's father. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the certificate issued showing the death of Hawa Bibi and allegedly buried in Azimpur graveyard is not correct which is a manipulated paper but the learned lower appellate court illegally held that the certificate is genuine. The learned trial court was justified in disbelieving the said paper for want of proof. The independent disinterested persons present in the graveyard were not examined and the very circumstantial evidence conclusively proved that Hawa Bibi was not buried in Azimpur graveyard. The learned lower appellate court without rebutting the findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records illegally decided the fate of the appeals in favour of the appellants and thereafter passed the impugned judgment and decree which deserve interference of this Court. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rules controverter the argument advanced from the side of the petitioners and submits that the learned lower appellate court during passing the impugned judgment and decree committed no illegality or irregularity. All the evidence adduced both oral and documentary were properly evaluated as well as assessed in its true perspective by the learned Additional District Judge before deciding the merit of the appeals. The learned Advocate further submits that incompliance of the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure the learned lower appellate court which is the final court of facts decided the fate of the appeals in favour of the appellants and there is no misreading or non-wading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate also submits that Dukhu Khalifa being the father of admitted owner Disana. Bibi obtained settlement of 21 decimals of land which is the disputed property from the superior landlord Mirash Hazi Mia Kha and this factual aspect was duly considered by the lower appellate court in consultation with the evidence on records. The relevant C.S. khatian no.14 marked as exhibit-`E' makes it clear that Dukhu Khalifa is the 'rayoti' tenant under the landlord Hazi Mia Kha and in this context; rebutting the findings of the trial court rightly the appellate court below arrived at a correct decision which is supported by both the oral and documentary evidence. The learned Advocate submits that the S.A. and R.S. khatian do not confirm the title of the petitioners as because the said khatians are not the documents of title. Secondly; the present petitioners during trial of the original suits utterly failed to prove their basic documents under section 67 of the Evidence Act inasmuch as those are the certified copies which are required to be proved under the purview of law after calling the volume book. But the plaintiff-petitioners failed to discharge their onus in proving their respective case which has been properly appreciated and addressed by the leaned appellate court below. Mere preparation of S.A. and R.S. khatian and payment of rent does not create any title and most empathetically the defendant-opposite parties have challenged the said S.A. khatian which was prepared in the name of some fictitious persons. The plaintiff-petitioner did not produce any evidence to prove the existence of those persons in whose name the khatian was prepared. Lastly for unspecified land the plaintiffs sought for their relief which is not in accordance with law and for such vague and indefinite land there cannot be any decree of eviction and the learned appellate court adverting evidence on records in his findings rightly held that the boundaries allegedly given is vague and indefinite. 

 11. On perusal of the case records it transpires that the disputed property comprising an area of 21 decimals of land originally belonged to the C.S. recorded tenants Dhana Bibi. It is the pleadings of the plaintiffs that the original owner Dhana Bibi - died leaving behind her brother Hazi Mia Kha who inherited the property left behind his sister the C.S. recorded tenant. Dhana Bibi. Subsequently: Hazi Miah Kha died leaving behind only son Md. Yasin Kha who transferred 07(seven) decimals of land in favour of one Hawa Bibi. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that at the demise of Yasin Kha his four sons became the heirs and the S.A. record of right was correctly prepared in their names. The predecessor of the plaintiffs Hanif Miah after purchasing 14 decimals of land mutated his name and paid rent and Hanif Mia also purchased 07(seven) decimals of land from Hama Bibi and in this way he became the owner of the entire 21 decimals of land. 

 13. Scrutinizing the relevant papers on record it farther appears that the only heir of Hawa Bibi the present opposite party Dukhu Mia as plaintiff instituted a Civil Suit being No. 132 of 1994 against the plaintiff Md. Hanif Miah challenging the deed which was allegedly taken by Md. Hanif Mia from Hawa Bibi. It is the case of the defendant that after the death of Hawa Bibi the deed was created which is a spurious document. After the institution of that suit the plaintiffs instituted the Civil Suit No. 113 of 1995 against the defendant-appellants alleging that they being permissive possessors are liable to be evicted from the suit property. In this regard; the teamed appellate court below scanning the evidence on record held that the plaintiffs with malice instituted the suit having no valid document and title in the disputed land. The relevant C.S. khatian No:14 has been properly evaluated by the leaned lower appellate- court and it is from exhibit-IF' that Mirash Haji Miah Kha was the superior landlord and the 'rayoti tenant under Dhana Bibi was Dukhu Khaln. The documentary evidence go to show that the C.S. recorded tenant Dhana Bibi had no brother Hazi Minh Kha by name rather Nazi. Miah Kha was a superior landlord and the observation which is transpired within the contents of the findings is supported by evidence on records. Furthermore: having gone through the relevant papers on records 1 find that during trial of the original suit the plaintiffs adduced six witnesses while the defendants examined three: witnesses in support of their respective cases. 

 15. The submissions cited from the side of the teamed Advocate for the opposite parties as to the documentary evidence which is the basis of the suits i.e. the C.S. khatian No.14 appears to be consistent which have got every nexus within the contents of the document. The fact remains that the trial court during disposal of the original suits failed to assess the evidence on records in its true perspective and also failed to appreciate the actual position of law. It is the plaintiffs who are to prove their case by credible, competent evidence and they cannot bank upon their adversary. The weakness of the defendants do not play any role in getting relief of the plaintiffs in absence of tangible evidence from their side. The learned appellate court in this regard rightly held that the certified copy of the title paper which was produced from the side of the plaintiffs requires to be proved under the purview of Evidence Act and the onus of proof under sections 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act entirely lies upon the plaintiffs to establish their case after adducing sufficient tangible evidence. But apparently during disposal of the original suits it transpires that the plaintiffs were not able to discharge their onus in proving their ease which is not escaped the notice of the appellate court. The appellate court below with regard to the factual aspect being a final court of facts decided the material facts for adjudication of the matter in dispute in its right approach and I find no ambiguity or violation of law in deciding the merit of the appeals. 

 17. In the result, the Rules are discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 28.02.2005 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 8"1 Court, Dhaka. in Title Appeal No. 250 of 1997 and 249 of 1997 analogously reversing the judgment and decree dated 17.08.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Keraniganj, Dhaka in analogous disposal of Title Suit No. 113 of 1995 and 132 of 1994 is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Wahida Khanam ----- Plaintiff-respondent-Petitioner.
1(a) Most. Laila and others, ------ Co-Petitioners.
Versus
Md. Abrahim @ Ibrahim and Another ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party nos. 1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 01.06.2010 and 07.06.2010 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge. 2nd Court. Chapai Nawabganj, in Title Appeal No. 135 of 2006 allowing the appeal reversing the judgment and decree dated 20.08.2006 and 23.08.2006 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Nachol, Chapai Nawabganj in Title Suit No. 10 of 2002. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit No. 10 of 2002 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Nachol, Chapai Nawabganj for declaration of title in respect of the suit properties contending inter alia, that the disputed property appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 217 measuring an area of .50 acres of land in C.S. plot No.1013 originally belonged to one Makhon Chandra Das. During S.A. operation the land has been recorded in S.A. khatian No. 262. The original owner of the land Makhon Chandra for want of money tried to dispose of the land and one Habibur Rahman agreed to purchase. Accordingly by a registered Sub-kabla deed dated 29.08.1960 Habibur Rahman purchased the suit land in his name. it is the case of Habibur Rahman that at the time of aforesaid deed he Was minor and his guardian paid the consideration money which was obtained by the purchaser Habibur Rahman in the occasion of his Khatna and the gift money with golden ornaments given by his relations in favour of Him. After attaining majority the purchaser Habibur cultivated the land and erected house in some portion of the suit land. He used to reside therein. Subsequently he transferred the same by a sub-kabla deed dated 03.04.1983 in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor. After purchasing the land the purchaser went into possession and after the death of plaintiffs predecessor the plaintiff is possessing the same for more than 20 years. The defendants having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit properties trying to disturb the peaceful possession of the plaintiff disclosing that their father purchased the land in the benami of Habibur Rahman and after the death of their father they acquired title and interest over the disputed property. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after examining witnesses from the sides of the respective parties consulting the oral and documentary evidence on record decreed the suit on contest vide judgment and decree dated 20.08.2006. Being aggrieved the defendants preferred a Title Appeal No. 135 of 2006 in the court of learned District Judge, Chapai Nawabganj which was transmitted to the 2' Court of learned Joint District Judge. Chapai Nawabganj and the learned lower appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 01.06.2010 allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Joint. District Jude, 2nd Court during disposal of the appeal without assessment of evidence and appreciation of law in its true perspective decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the defendant-appellant arbitrarily. The conclusive positive findings and decision of the trial court on the issues framed therein specially on the pertinent matter in dispute between the parties which is on alleged benami transaction not at all rebutted by the lower appellate court adverting evidence on records and thereby committed illegality resulting in an error in - the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that practically the appellate court utterly failed to discharge his duty in evaluating the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties before arrival at a decision on the merit of the appeal which is violative to the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the trial court during disposal of the original suit while after proper sifting of evidence and proper appreciation of law relying upon the principle of law and guideline of the Apex Court decided each and every issue in favour of the plaintiff, the lower appellate court without rebutting the findings and decision of the trial court reversed the judgment and decree on surmise and conjecture which is an error of law resulting in an error in the decision. There has been glaring misconception of law and non-reading and misreading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision in passing the impugned judgment and decree and as such the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law and facts and is liable to be interfered with. 

 9. On perusal of the case records it transpires that it is an admitted position that the schedule property measuring an area of -.50 acres of land originally belonged to one Makhon Chandra Das in C.S. plot No. 1013. The owner Makhon Chandra admittedly transferred the land in dispute in favour of Habibur Rahman by a sub-kabla deed dated 29.06.1960. It is the positive assertion of the plaintiff that the transaction in favour of Habibur Rahman is not a benami transaction and there is no ingredient of benami transaction in the aforesaid transfer. 

 10. Vis-a-vis; the contrary case of the contesting defendants is such that at the relevant time the purchaser Habibur Rahman was a minor and he had no money to purchase the land and as a result of that his father Abdur Rahman purchased the property in the benami of his minor son Habibur Rahman. Therefore, obviously the pertinent question which is transpired from the pleadings of the parties is such as to whether the transaction was benami. The learned trial court during disposal of the original suit relying upon two decisions of our Apex Court rightly held that there shall have to the existence of seven criteria’s before judging an instrument as benami transaction and the criteria’s are incorporated in the provisions laid down as under: 

 (v) The custody of the title deed and the conduct of the parties concerned in dealing with the property after the purchase. 

 14. In the result, the Rule having sufficient merit is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 01.06.2010 and 07.06.2010 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chapai Nawabganj, in Title Appeal No. 135 of 2006 allowing the appeal reversing the judgment  and decree dated 20.08.2006 and 23.08.2006 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Nachol, Chapai Nawabganj in Title Suit No. 10 of 2002 is hereby set aside.

parties:
Md. Iman Ali Sarder and 79 Others.
Vs.
Md. Ibrahim Sarder and 20 Others.
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party Nos.1-2 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 07.07.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Court, Satkhira in Title. Appeal No.167 of 1987 allowing the application for additional written statement filed by the defendants under order 6 Rule 5 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs filed the original Title Suit being No. 55 of 1982 in the court of the then Munsif, 2nd Court, Satkhira which was subsequently transferred to the court of Assistant Judge, Shyamnagor, Satkhira and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 86 of 1984 for declaration that the certificate sale held on 19.01.1961 is illegal, void & is of no legal effect and also for setting aside the same. The learned Assistant Judge, Shyamnagor, Satkhira after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest on 22.06.1987. 

 3. Being aggrieved the defendant Nos.1-4 preferred Title Appeal No.167 of 1987 in the Court of learned District Judge, Satkhira which was transferred for hearing and disposal to the court of learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Satkhira. In the said Appeal the defendant-appellants i.e. the present opposite party Nos.1-21 filed an application for accepting the additional written statement contending inter alia that at the time of filing of their written statement earlier; some important facts were left out so as to one Golam Mostofa, son of the defendant No.3, Amzad Hossain, son of the defendant No.1, Asraf & Abul Basar steps sons of the defendant No.3, Abdul Goffer, son of the defendant No. 4 and one Khalilur Rahman kabla purchased some lands from the defendant No. 2 and the purchasers have their huts, chowshed, kitchen on the land of plot Nos. 3723, 2730, 3834 and 3835 wherein they are residing with their family and the plaintiffs do not reside there. The learned court of appeal below vide it's order dated 07.07.2008 allowed the said application with cost. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners during hearing of this Rule submits that the learned Additional District Judge i.e. the lower appellate court committed illegality in allowing the application for additional written statement inasmuch as the contents of the application is amounts to total contradiction of their earlier pleading which was given in their written statement during pendency of the original Suit. The learned Advocate further submits that the amendment sought for would change the nature and character of the earlier pleading and such amendment has prejudiced the plaintiffs in getting justice. The learned Advocate also submits that it was the case of the defendants that the plaintiffs do possess some portion of the suit land in which the plaintiffs have their homestead. The learned trial court decreed the suit on a findings that the plaintiffs have homestead in the suit land and the defendants are not in possession. By the amendment in the appellate stage the defendants in the form of additional written statement have brought a new story that they have also homestead on the suit land which amounts to change of the character of their earlier pleading. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the lower appellate court without proper appreciation of law and facts passed an erroneous order which is liable to be interfered with. 

 7. As against the aforesaid submissions of the teamed acme of the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned appellate court in allowing the application filed under order 6 Rule 5 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure committed no illegality since the nature and character of the defendant's original pleading is not changed at all by the said amendment which is in accordance with law. The learned Advocate further submits that during drafting of the original written statement concerned engaged lawyer of the defendants was not properly instructed by his clients as the defendants are illiterate village lay man. Some important facts were left out from the original written statement and subsequently while the matter was brought into the notice of the learned Advocate, he filed an application under order 6 Rule 5 along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for additional written statement to clarify the pleading which is already on record. The learned Advocate lastly submits that by the said additional written statement nothing new or contradictory fact was brought in by which the nature and character of the original written statement can be changed and as such there is nothing to interfere with the impugned order of the learned lower appellate court. 

 9. On perusal of the application it appears that the defendants in their prayer tried to bring such a fact that the kabla purchaser Khalilur Rahman with his other family members after acquiring land from the original defendants residing in some portion of the suit land after erecting huts therein. The kabla purchasers also have their cowshed, kitchen on the land of plot Nos. 3723, 3729, 3730, 3834 and 3835. It is also noticed on perusal of the said application that the defendants by the said additional written statement tried to deny the existence of the plaintiffs in the suit plot Nos.3723, 3729, 3730, 3834 and 3835 and they also tried to bring such case in their pleading in the form of additional written statement that save and except the defendants and their relations none have any dwelling but therein and the plaintiffs do not possess the land of the aforesaid plots. 

 10. In this regard scrutinizing the relevant papers it is apparent that the defendants in their original written statement and the defendant No.1, Jobed Ali Molla in his deposition before the trial court during trial of the original suit contended that the plaintiffs have dwelling huts in some portion of the suit land and after obtaining permission from the defendants they are possessing the same. Therefore; obviously it can be held that the statement of the defendants in Paragraph-2 of their application under order VI Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure is contradictory to their earlier case (pleading). Such amendment or change in the form of additional written statement is not permissible in the eye of law. Order VI Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure contemplates, "only a further and better statement of the nature of the claim or defence, or further and better particulars of any matter stated in any pleading, may in all cases be ordered, upon such terms, as to costs and otherwise, as may be just". 

 11. The aforesaid better statement or particular must be consistent with the original pleading of the parties. Further and better statement does not permit introduction of new material or new case which is contrary to earlier case of the party concern.

parties:
Sabruddin @ Shafiuddin and others ------ Defendant Nos. 21-23 Appellant-Petitioners
Vs
Kafiluddin Dewan and 4 others ------ Plaintiff-Respondent -Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker,  J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj, in Title Appeal No.91 of 2005 affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.04.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 173 of 2002 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party Nos. 1-5 being plaintiffs filed the original Title Suit being No. 173 of 2002 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Singair, District-Manikganj against the defendant-petitioners praying for partition of the land described in the schedule and also for a declaration of title and recovery of possession with a further declaration that the S.A. and R.S. Khatian in respect of the land described in the schedule Nos.' and 2 of the plaint are illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia, that the land described in schedule no.1 of the plaint belonged to one Babor Ali and his brother Buchai Sheikh. The land of schedule Nos. 2 and 3 was recorded in the name of Buchai Sheikh. Babor Ali died before publication of D.S. record leaving behind his wife Tamasha Bewa. Buchai Sheikh died leaving behind his wife Meher Jan Bewa. The land described in schedule 1 was recorded in the name of Meherjan Bewa and Tamasha Bewa correctly. Tamasha Bewa and Meherjan Bewa granted korfa pattan of the land described in schedule nos. 1 and 2 in favour of one Saber Dewan and his wife Firoza Begum on 8th Srabon, 1328 B.S. Tamasha Bewa gave korfa pattan of the land described in schedule-3 in favour of Saber Dewan and Feroza Begum on 14th Aswin, 1329 B.S. Thereafter, getting the land by way of korfa pattan the pattan holders Saber Dewan and Feroza possessed the same described in schedule nos. 1-3. Saber Dewan died leaving behind his wife Feroza Begum, two sons Karim and Moksed and one daughter Hatunnessa. During the life time of Saber Dewan his one son Md. Ashraf Ali died leaving behind daughter Ayatunnessa and Ayatunnessa died leaving behind the plaintiffs as her heirs. The S.A. record was prepared in the name of Ayatunnessa and thus the plaintiffs after acquiring the suit land measuring 1.25 acres by way of inheritance and purchase sold 07 (seven) decimals of land in favour of the defendant No.2 and the rest land measuring I. I8 acres are being possessed by them with the defendants in ejmali. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the land of schedule-I of the plaint has been wrongly recorded in the names of the predecessor of the defendant nos. 21-23. Prior to the filing of the original suit the plaintiff nos. 1-4 along with others filed a Title Suit being No. 132 of 1994 in the court of Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj, which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 94 of 2000. The suit was dismissed and against that order of dismissal the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 18 of 2001 which was also dismissed and the learned appellate court vide his judgment and decree dated. 13.06.2002 observed that the plaintiffs may prefer partition suit in a competent court of law. Therefore, the plaintiffs filed the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants is such that the suit as it was framed is not maintainable and there is no cause of action. The suit is bad for defect of the parties and hotchpotch defect. The further case of the defendants to that suit is such that the plaintiffs have no right, title interest and possession in the disputed land and the suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata. The disputed 2.56 acres of land belonged to Babor Ali and Buchai Sheikh. The D.S. record was prepared in their names but in the dakhalker column of the D.S. record the names of one Tamasha Bewa and Meherjan Bewa were inserted, who are the wives of Babar Ali and Buchai Sheikh. The share of Tamasha was transferred to Meherjan and Meherjan become the owner of entire 2.56 acres of land. The positive case of the defendants is such that during the life time of Tamasha Bewa and Meheijan they never gave any korfa pattan in favour of Saber Dewan and Feroza Begum. Saber Dewan along with his wife Feroza Begum were in fact not the owners of the land described in the schedule of the plaint by virtue of korfa pattan. The R.S. Khatian no. 199 of Mouza Kashimnagar and R.S. Khatian No. 226 of Mouza Barabaka were recorded in the name of Shamsuddin alone which was correct. Shamsuddin owned and possessed 1.28 acres of land and constructed huts therein. He also planted various trees there and that he was not the permissive possessor in the land described in the schedule of plaint. Shamsuddin died leaving behind one son the defendant no. 21 and two daughters the defendant nos. 22 and 23. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs to this suit filed a Title Suit being No. 132 of 1999 which was renumbered as 94 of 2000. That suit was dismissed on contest. Against that judgment and decree plaintiffs preferred a Title Appeal being No. 18 of 2001 and that appeal was also dismissed on contest. The statements made by the plaintiffs with regard to their alleged title are totally contrary to the statement made by them in their previous Title Suit No. 132 of 1999. 

 4. The learned trial court after examining the witnesses from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit in the preliminary form by his judgment and decree dated 25.04.2005. Being aggrieved the present defendant-petitioners preferred a title appeal in the court of learned District Judge. Manikganj being Title Appeal No. 91 of 2005 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj and the leaned lower appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity and without considering the material evidence on record they committed error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the lower appellate court without discussing and considering the evidence of the witnesses decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiffs on surmise and conjecture and without discussions upon the issues framed upheld the findings of the trial court which is violative of the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Both the courts below failed to consider that the plaintiffs are claiming title and partition on the basis of kabla deeds marked as exhibit-3 series and same private documents of koda pattan exhibits-2, 2(ka). Having failed to prove these documents under sections 67 and 68 of the Evidence Act and in absence of proof of its execution the documents does not create any presumption of its genuineness and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the courts below were totally failed to assess the material exhibits of the defendants marked as Exhibits-`Ka' and gala' series. They also failed to evaluate Exhibit-'1Ca' properly. The learned lower appellate court acted illegally in affirming the decree of the trial court ignoring the oral and documentary evidence of the defendants by resorting to hypothetical assumption and both the courts below erred in law in not considering the respective cases of the parties in jaxta position with same yardstick weightment and rejected the defendant's case as regard title without proper application of judicial mind and the same has caused miscarriage of justice. The learned Advocate lastly submits that in the impugned judgment and decree there has been apparent misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be interfered with. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. As regard the basis of the plaintiff-opposite parties case in respect of the disputed property on korfa pattan, the koda pattan papers has already been marked exhibits after formal proof according to law and at this stage the defendants are stopped from challenging the said basis of claim of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate. further submits that in the original suit the plaintiffs prayed for three separate relief but the court below granted only one relief in favour of the plaintiffs without debarring the plaintiff from getting subsequent relief which were sought for by the plaintiff-opposite parties. No relief was granted on the prayer for recovery of khash possession in respect of 17 decimals of land in which admittedly the plaintiffs are ousted from their possession by the defendants illegally. Furthermore; no relief was given by the courts below on the prayer of declaration that the khatian in respect of 49 decimals of land is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Apart from this; the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its appeal failed to consider that the plaintiffs to the suit. who are the present opposite parties prayed for separate saham in respect of 1.18 acres of land. The trial court without assigning any reason only gave 1.02 acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs and there is no explanation on the remaining 16 decimals of land. Beside this no courts during their judgment and findings gave any observation on the plaintiff's specific contention of giving oral permission to the defendants to posses 17 decimals of land in the disputed holding and as a result the plaintiffs are not also happy with the judgments. 

 10. It appears from the case record that the plaintiffs to the suit in their pleading asserts that the land described in schedule 1 of the plaint originally belonged to Babar Ali and Buchai Sheikh and the land of schedule nos. 2 and 3 were recorded in the D.S. khatian which stands recorded in the name of Buchai Sheikh only. It was further contended that Babar Ali died before the publication of D.S. record leaving behind his wife Tamasha Bibi. Buchai Sheikh died leaving behind his wife Meherjan and in this way after the death of Babar Ali and Buchai Sheikh their wives by way of inheritance acquired the land in dispute. The land described in schedule nos. 1 and 2 of the plaint was recorded in the names of Meherunnessa and Tamasha Bewa and the land described in schedule 3 was recorded in the name of Tamasha Bewa only. The basis of claim from the side of the plaintiffs in respect of their schedule property is koda pattan in the year 1328 and in the year 1329 respectively. Their specific contention as it appears is such that the land of schedule Nos. 1 and 2 were transferred by Tamasha and Meherjan in favour of Saber Dewan and his wife Feroza Begum on 8th Srabon, 1328 B.S. Subsequently Tamasha Bewa on 14th Aswin of 1329 B.S. transferred the land of schedule no.3 in favour of Saber Dewan and Feroza Begum by way of korfa pattan at a salami of Taka 100/-. The said korfa pattan has been categorically challenged from the side of the contesting defendants and in this context it is the specific assertion of the defendant-appellant-petitioners that the basis of claim of the plaintiffs, i.e. the korfa settlement in the name of their predecessor in interest not at all proved under the purview of sections 67 and 68 of the Evidence Act. In this regard sections 67 and 68 of the Evidence Act contemplates that the documents alleged to have been executed by a person after putting signature or left thumb impression is required to be proved wholly or partly by the person, who is directly involved in its execution. Mere production of the documents is not at all sufficient for proof. The proof would be in compliance of provisions and the aforesaid sections. Therefore, a document which is not proved as required by this section; is inadmissible in evidence. 

 11. On careful scrutiny over the impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below it is obvious to note that both the courts below have hopelessly failed to appreciate the actual position of law in taking cognizance of the document produced which is the basis of claim of the plaintiffs. Furthermore, apparently the impugned judgment and decree is not passed in compliance of the provisions laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and it is also apparent from the face of the Records that the trial court during disposal of the original suit failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of law as provided in Order XX, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure in stating decision on each issue. Gross illegality was done during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal and it is an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Apart from this; in view of the argument advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the opposite parties in consultation with the original case record I have every reason to appreciate the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties and it is most unfortunate that the trial court as well as the appellate court without going into the merit of the suit and materials on record including the prayer portion of the plaint in a evasive manner disposed of the suit and its subsequent appeal which is arbitrary and not desirable. There is no explanation even from the side of the trial court as to why the relief which were sought for was not granted or refused. There is no findings in respect of the quantum of land for which the share allegedly was given in favour of the plaintiffs out of the total land. Despite 16 decimals of land has been left out the reason for which that portion of land was not given not at all cited within the four corners of the findings and decision. During arguments the learned counsel on behalf of the defendant-petitioners referred a decision of this court reported in 43 DLR 221 which is most appropriate here and have got every nexus in the instant case. In the case of Dewan Mohammad Safare Ali & others —vs.-People's Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 43 DLR(1991)221 it was held that the object of rule 31 of Or. XLI of the Code of Civil Procedure is such that the Appellate Court must consider independently the relevant salient points which arose for adjudication and to discuss evidence led by the parties as well as point of law. In the instant case the Appellate Court obviously did not discuss each issue separately nor gave any independent findings on each issue after proper assessment and preponderance of evidence and thereby the impugned judgment and decree suffers from patent illegality and material irregularity which was violative of the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Our Apex Court in the case of Hajarilal Mondal and others —vs.- Md. Mozajfor Bepari and others, reported in 8 BLC (AD) 77 held that "it is a settled principle of law that the lower appellate court being final court of fact will discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the finding of the trial Court." 

 13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj, in Title Appeal No. 91 of 2005 and the judgment and decree dated 25.04.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 173 of 2002 are hereby set aside. 

 14. The order of stay granted earlier by this court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. The original suit be send back on remand for fresh trial within 02(two) months from the date of receipt of the Records.

parties:
Bangladesh, represented by the DC, Sylhet ------ Defendant-Respondent-Petitioners
vs. 
Md. Abdul Aziz Chowdhury and others. ------ Plaintiff-Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-1998 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No 168 of 1994 reversing those of dated 17-2-1994 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 12 of 1993 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders be passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties being plaintiffs filed the original Title Suit being No. 12 of 1993 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet contending inter alia, that the predecessors of the plaintiffs namely Ashraf Ali and Md. Asgar Ali had been owned and possessed the suit land after payment of rent regularly. Subsequently the predecessors of the plaintiffs after filing a Title Suit being No. 1002 of 1865 for declaration of title obtained a, decree. Thereafter, due to arrear of rent for some portion of the disputed property it was put into an auction and one Eresh Chandra Dey auction purchased the land and obtained possession therein. The auction purchaser by two registered kabla deeds dated 04-11-1932 AD transferred the land in favour of the plaintiff No. 1's mother Fazira Khatun. The mother of the plaintiff No. 1 along with the predecessors of the plaintiff Nos. 2-5 one Sayab ullah and Nabab ullah purchased some portion of the suit land by a registered kabla dated 14-6-1956 from one Rakesh Ranjan Ghosh and thereby the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the suit land is not a fishery and in the first part of 1986 AD the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that the suit property has been recorded wrongly in the name of Government as "Dalai Beet". Due to wrong record plaintiff's title to the suit land has been clouded and to dispel the cloud plaintiffs filed the original suit in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant-respondent-petitioner government of Bangladesh is such that the disputed property is a "jalmahal" under the government from the very beginning and the kabla deeds in favour of the plaintiff's predecessors dated 04-11-1932 and 14-6-1956 are collusive, forged and created to grab the property The judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 1002 of 1865 is not for the disputed property and the decreetal land of that suit is not identical with that of the present suit properties. The suit properties are fishery in which neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessors allegedly possessed and the record of right in the name of government has been correctly prepared, as "jalmahal" under the government. 

 4. The learned trial court after taking evidence dismissed the suit on contest vide his judgment and decree dated 17-2-1994 and 24-2-1994 respectively. Being aggrieved the plaintiff-appellant-opposite parties preferred an appeal in the court of learned District Judge, Sylhet being Title Appeal No. 168 of 1994, which was heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet and the learned lower Appellate Court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-1998 and 24-5-1998 respectively allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 11. On careful scrutiny over the papers on record it has come to the notice of the court that in respect of the suit properties there has been a survey by a survey knowing advocate and the learned Advocate Commissioner after holding commission submitted his Report marked as Exhibit-'X'. The learned Advocate Commissioner Mr. Abdul Rashid in his testimony as witness No. 4 states at a stage that he could not relay the land of deed dated 04-11-1932 AD as the plaintiffs could not produce the same before him. Obviously; it is the pleading of plaintiffs that they obtained the disputed property by two kabla deeds of the year 1932 and 1956 and by the kabla deed of the year 1932 they acquired 10 kedars out of suit property and by the remaining deed of the year 1956 they acquired 10 kedars of suit land. The learned trial court during disposal of the original suit opined that the plaintiff no. 1 in his averment states that the area of land is 36/37 kedars. In respect of the identity of the disputed property; on going through the original plaint it is apparent that the plaintiffs in their pleading specifically states to the effect that they acquired the land measuring 10 kedars + 10 kedars = 20 kedars by two registered deeds which was purchased by the mother of the plaintiff no. 1, Fazira Khatun and the predecessor of the remaining plaintiff Nos. 2-5 one Soyabullah and Nababullah. 

 16. I have come across from the impugned judgment and decree of the lower appellate court that the learned Subordinate Judge during assessment of the evidence failed to assess the evidence on record properly in its true perspective and arrived at an erroneous view that the suit land as it appears is specified and identical. The said observation is not consistent with the evidence on records. It is the established principle of civil law that the plaintiff must have to succeed on his own legs. He cannot bank upon weakness of his adversary. The learned trial court during disposal of the original suit rightly opined that the plaintiffs to the suit by credible competent evidence has failed to establish their case rather it has come to the notice of the court that the disputed property is totally unspecified and not identical. The pleading of the plaintiffs is also vague. The learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal not at all reversed the positive findings of the trial court properly in consultation with the evidence on record. In sifting of evidence there has been illegality which cannot be ignored. 

 18. In the result, the Rule have got much substance to succeed. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-1998 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 168 of 1994 reversing those of dated 17-2-1994 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 12 of 1993 is hereby set aside.

parties:
Nur Mohammad ------ Defendant-Appellant- Petitioners
Vs.
Serajul Islam and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondents-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
On an application of the petitioner Nur Mohammad and another under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure the Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 9-9-1997 passed by the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), First Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 28 of 1994 affirming those dated 31-1-1994 passed by the Assistant Judge, Faridganj, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 134 of 1992 should not be set-aside. 

 2. Briefly, the facts of the case, are that the defendant-opposite parties as plaintiffs. instituted Title Suit No. 134 of 1992 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Faridganj, Chandpur for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession contending inter-alia that one Ananda Charan Kuri was the owner of "Ka" schedule property measuring an area of 44 decimals of land. He proposed to sell the same to the plaintiff at a consideration of Taka 1,200 and on receiving Taka 1,030 in different installments from the plaintiff he executed a bainapatra and surrendered the possession of the suit land to the plaintiff. In the meanwhile Ananda Charan being under the bad influence of the defendants executed a ante dated registered Saf kabala deed in the name of defendant No. 1. Thereafter, the plaintiffs brought Title Suit No. 247 of 1969 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Chandpur against Ananda Charan Kuri and the defendant No. 1 for Specific Performance of Contract which was decreed on 30-9-1972 exparte. Against which defendant No. 1 brought Miscellaneous Case for restoration and also brought another Title Suit No. 46 of 1973 for cancellation of the exparte decree the said case though allowed by the trial court but ultimately lost up to the High Court Division. Thereafter, the original Title Suit No. 247 of 1969 for Specific Performance of Contract was put in execution and the plaintiff obtained registered kabala through the court. Defendant No.1 having forcibly entered into "Kha" schedule property and made houses thereon. Hence the suit. 

 5. Against which the defendant-petitioners filed Title Appeal No. 28 of 1994 before the District Judge, Chandpur. The said appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge (Now Joint District Judge), First Court, Chandpur who after hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record dismissed the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court by his judgment and decree dated 9-9-1947. 

 7. Mr Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that both the courts committed error of law in not considering the evidence on record properly. The learned Advocate further submitted that the defendant-petitioners obtained register sale deed from the original owner Ananda Charan Kuri on 10-6-1969 and since then the defendant had been in possession of the suit land but both the courts did not consider the same. The learned Advocate further submitted that the registered deed which was obtained by the defendant-petitioners on 10-6-1969 but the plaintiff obtained decree of Specific Performance of Contract on 30-9-1972 and both the courts did not consider that the plaintiffs could not prove the case of dispossession from the suit land in such a case on the basis of the subsequent deed the decree of khas possession is illegal. The learned Senior Counsel further submitted that simple declaratory suit without any consequential relief against the registered deed dated 10-6-1969 is not maintainable and the plaintiffs cannot get any relief but both the courts did not consider the same. He further submitted that though the defendants contested the earlier suit but in the said suit no title of the parties was decided but both the courts erroneously found that the defendants lost up to the High Court Division which is erroneous findings of the courts below. Thus, he prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 8. On the contrary Mr AB Roy Chowdhury along with Mr Md Kamrul Alam Kamal and Mr Mohammad Hasibuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 4 submitted that both the courts rightly found the case in favour of the plaintiffs and accordingly decreed the suit. The learned further submitted that the concurrent findings of fact that the plaintiff obtained right and title before the registered deed of the defendant which cannot be interfered with. The learned Advocate submitted that both the courts concurrently found that the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants from 28- 6-1977. He further submitted that the defendants as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 75 of 1990 for injunction but could not succeed and the court opined that the defendants failed to prove their title on the basis of the registered deed dated 10-6-1969 but they did not take any further steps against the said findings of the trial court thus the findings of the courts below cannot be interfered with. The learned Advocate further submitted that as per provision of section 48 of the Transfer of Property Act a Transfer operate from the date of execution of the deed although it may have been registered at a later date. In the instant case the petitioners obtained bainanama from the original owner in the year 1954 and accordingly the plaintiffs filed suit for Specific Performance of Contract and obtained deed through execution after the deed of the defendants which should be treated the deed from the date of execution so subsequent transferee cannot get any right and title by the registered deed. Thus, he prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 9. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment, papers and documents as available on the records. The plaintiff obtained bainanama from the original owner Ananda Charan Kuri in the year 1954 but when he came to know that the said Ananda Charan Kuri subsequently on 10-6-1969 executed a registered deed in favour of the defendant he filed suit for Specific Performance of Contract and obtained an exparte decree on 30-9-1972. In the said suit the present petitioner was a defendant along with the transferor Ananda Charan Kuri thereafter the present petitioner filed miscellaneous case for setting aside the exparte decree but ultimately withdrawn the same and filed Other Class Suit No. 46 of 1973 claiming that the exparte decree passed on 30-9- 1972 was not binding upon the plaintiff the present petitioner. Though the petitioner obtained decree in the said suit but ultimately lost up to the High Court Division and admittedly the present petitioner did not take any further step against the said judgment of the High Court Division. Thereafter, the plaintiff- opposite Party on execution obtained the registered deed through court. In the meantime, the present petitioner also filed Title Suit No. 75 of 1990 (Exhibit-2 (gha) for injunction against the present opposite party but ultimately lost, whereas the defendant did not take any further steps against the said order of the trial court. I have carefully examined all the earlier judgment of the courts .The defendant-petitioner though a party to the suit for Specific Performance of Contract but ultimately lost. This court do not consider the right and title and the genuiness of the deed dated 10-6-1969. In Title Suit No. 75 of 1990 the court clearly opined that by the deed dated 10-6-1969 the petitioner did not accrued any right and title. 

 10. It also appears that the courts below did not consider the date of dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land. The plaintiff claimed that he was dispossessed from the suit land on 28-6-1977 but the appellate court opined that the plaintiff failed to prove his dispossession from the suit land on 28-6-1977 opined that the plaintiff though failed to prove the specific date for dispossession from the suit land but he was dispossessed from the said suit land by the defendant. The appellate court also opined that from the judgment of the Title Suit No. 75 of 1999 (Exhibit-2 (Gha) it is clear that the plaintiff was dis- possessed from the suit land by the defendant. 

 11. In the instant case it is to be considered which deed should be prevailed. Section 48 of the Transfer Property Act provides that the deed which was executed earlier which should be prevailed. In the instant case the plaintiff instituted the suit for Specific Performance of Contract being Title Suit No. 247 of 1969 wherein the defendant-petitioner was party along with the original owner Ananda Charan Kuri and in the said suit the plaintiff-opposite party claimed that though the deed was executed in favour of the plaintiff by Ananda Charan Kuri in the year 1954 but the said original owner Ananda Charan Kuri subsequently transferred the suit to the defendant through registered deed dated 10-6-1969 and accordingly after completion of the long litigation obtained the deed through court which clearly proves that the said deed though registered later on but which was operated from the date of execution i.e. 1954. So it is clear that the plaintiff-opposite party obtained right and title from the date of execution of the said Bainanama deed 

 12. Section 48 of the Transfer of Property Act is a priority of rights created transfer wherein the maxim "qui priorest tempore potior est jure" means who is before in time is the better right i.e. the transferor cannot prejudice the right of the transferee by any subsequent denim with the property. On the basis of this maxim the plaintiff has create right from the transferor though the said transferor trying to prejudice the right of the plaintiff by subsequent transfer to the petitioner through registered deed dated 10-6-1969 which cannot be sustained. In the case of Abdus Sauad Khan vs Wajed Ali Fakir reported in 44 DLR 495 it has been observed "there is no provision of law that title on the basis of the subsequent sale deeds will take effect from the date of agreement for sale it possession is delivered in past performance of the agreement." 

 15. In the result, the Rule is discharged. However, without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 9-9-1997 passed by the Subordinate judge (now Joint District Judge), First Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 28 of 1994 affirming those dated 31-1-1994 passed by the Assistant Judge, Faridganj, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 134 of 1992 are hereby upheld.
