full_judgment:
Bangladesh Shilpa Bank, Pabna branch as respondent No.1 appears and contests the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia that the right, title and interest over the land in question already vested in the rspondent-bank on the strength of a certificate issued by a competent Court under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and therefore the respondent-bank being the lawful owner of the land rightly published the auction notice. 

 Mr. Md. Mozibur Rahman Miah, the learned Advocate for the respondent-bank opposes the Rule submitting that the bank has acquired right and title over the land in question by virtue of a certificate issued by the Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in due course of an execution proceedings, and that the writ petitioner resorted under a wrong forum by filing the present writ petition, however, he has remedy in a competent civil Court. 

 Moreover a disputed question of title between the petitioner and the respondent-bank is involved in this writ petition. Apparently the respondent-bank has acquired right and title over the land in question by a certificate issued under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and unless the right and title of the petitioner as he pleaded in the present writ petition, is declared by a competent civil Court in his favour against the decree holder bank as well as the judgment debtor, he can not get any relief only by challenging the auction notice. 

 The petitioner is permitted to take back his original title documents those have been annexed with the writ petition substituting photocopies thereof.

parties:
Waseq Ullah & others ------Appellants
VS
Rezia Khatun and ors ------Respondents
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J : Appeal From Original Decree No. 99 of the 1999 preferred by defendant-appellant. Appeal From Original Decree No.182 of 1999 preferred by plaintiffs and Appeal From Original Decree No.183 of 1999 preferred by other defendants are directed against same judgment and decree dated 12-10-1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Noakhali decreeing Title Suit No.50 of 1990 in respect of 1.80 acres of land out of 2.93 acres of land of plot No.5-10 by adverse possession. 

 2. The plaintiff's case is that, the suit land originally belonged to Goura Chandra Majumder, Horish Chandra Majumder, son of late Ramananda Majumder, Akhil Chandra Majumder, son of late Ram Kania Majumder, Upendra Kumar Majumder, son of late Krishna Chandra Majumder, Raj Chandra Majumder, Girish Chandra Majumder and Sharat Chandra Majumder, sons of late Bhairab Chandra Majumder, Boikuntha Mohan Majumder, Chandra Mohan Majumder, Shashi Mohan Majumder, Proshanna Mohan Majumder, Boshanta Mohan Majumder, Nagendra Mohan Majumder, Brojendra Mohan Majumder, sons of late Golak Chandra Majumder and have been recorded 13½ Anna joma in previous khatian No.75, by registered kabuliyat dated 6th Srabon, 1267 BS the suit land along with other lands of previous khatian No. 31 was given in possession of Goura Chandra i.e. 0.42 acres of land of dag No. 513 and 0.24 acres of land of dag No. 514, in total, 4.61 acres of land, i.e. the land of 'ka' schedule to the suit land. In the plaint the land in west south corner 1.13 acres of land out of 2.93 acres of Plot No. 510 was possessed by the defendant No. 4 forcefully which is kha schedule. The plaintiff joint in the army and he participated in the second world-war and after the war, he left from army and came to his paternal homestead at Ullapara under Begumganj police station where he resides. Later on, he purchased some lands of Baroipara under Ramgonj police station and got pattan of certain lands from Jaminder. The land of 'Ka' schedule i.e. 4.61 acres of land were possessed by the previous tenants and after their death, their heirs while in possession and during riot of 1948 it was not possible for them to reside at Pakistan, they entered into an oral agreement with the plaintiff for selling 'ga' schedule land at a consideration of Taka 2,000 and after receiving most of the settled amount, in 1952 they gave possession of 'ga' schedule land in favour of the plaintiff with undertaking that they would register the saf kabala deed in favorable condition, during one night they left Pakistan and went to India. The plaintiff after getting the land as aforesaid, done some act showing that he is in possession of the aforesaid 'ga' schedule land and there by totally denied the title of the previous owner. Plaintiff's such possession is actually, openly, notoriously, continuously for above than 12 years and thereby got actual and exclusive possession over the suit land. By such invasion of the rights of the 'true owners, gave them a cause of action for recovery of khas possession at once. Plaintiff in fact acquired title by adverse possession which cannot be abolished or ruined. In that way plaintiff is in possession of 'ga' schedule land having title thereto. Plaintiff left for Pakistan on way to London in 1966 and his own persons, Goni Pundit and Joynal Abedin on his behalf, maintained the suit land by producing different kinds of vegetables and also by cultivating in more portion of land. In dag Nos. 514 and 515 i.e. 'ga' schedule land plaintiff constructed homestead and planted different kinds of trees in 1952 and maintained his possession. Plaintiff got connection of electricity line and also sunk tubewell, established cattle and poultry firm, rearing fishes in the pond and cultivated paddy in the land and in this way, he openly possessed the suit land. 

 3. Defendant No.4 being a very cunning person, wanted to grab the suit property and created some false papers and documents in connivance with some other persons in respect of 'ga' schedule land showing these papers, in Certificate Case No. 1960-61 in connection with Case No. 63/63-64, auction purchased the suit land which was confirmed on 27-3-1964. Defendant No.4 thereafter, filed Certificate Miscellaneous Case No. 210/63-64 by his own man and said case was dismissed and thereafter, Muslim Bhuiyan has been shown as auction purchaser of the suit land. All the papers relating to auction are only on papers as never Muslim Bhuiyan got possession of the suit land. Defendant No. 4 got a nadabi deed Muslim Bhuiyan on 25-2-1969 which was registered in connivance with each other and this nadabi deed has been shown in schedule Uma. Defendant No.4 by registered saf kabala deed dated 10-1-1964 purchased some land of 'ga' schedule from defendant No. 6 which is a paper transaction. Till promulgation of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the suit land was not demarcated and no land was recorded in the khatian, only rent roll was prepared for collecting rent which does not show the actual position of the lands and MR Khatian also not been prepared but the fact is plaintiff possessed the suit land from 1952. Defendant No. 4 by his own man, instituted criminal case in Miscellaneous Case No. 6 of 1988 under sections 147/447/379/307/427 of the Penal Code against the sons, relatives and cultivators of the plaintiff and defendant No.4 tried to grab the suit land mentioned in 'ga' schedule. In 'ga' schedule land defendant Nos. 5 to 22 have no title, possession or interest and before promulgation of Defense of Pakistan Rules, 1965, this lands had been in possession of plaintiff and by this time plaintiff got title by adverse possession as he possessed the land for more than 12 years. Defendant Nos. 5 to 22 have no subsisting right, title and interest in the suit land and also in the aforesaid 'ga.' schedule land as vested as enemy property. But defendant No. 4 in connivance with the employees of the vested cell includes 'ga' schedule land in VP Case No. 31/79-80 as enemy property. Plaintiff did not know about all these facts as he was not in Bangladesh. While he came in Bangladesh from abroad, he was advised, by the revenue employee to file an application to the Sub divisional Officer (Sadar) Noakhali for getting lease of 3.48 acres of land i.e. 'ga' schedule land but in that application for lease some mistake as regard Dag Nos. had been taken place and also quantum of land was not properly mentioned, as such, he later on, corrected the same, which is mentioned in 'Cha' schedule to the plaint. Over this application, on 5-3-1979, tahshilder gave report to the Sub Divisional Officer, Sadar, Noakhali, wherein it has been stated that original owners of the suit land, after delivering 'ga' schedule land to the plaintiff, taking advantage of night, left Pakistan to India and V.P authority in 1973 realize lease amount. Plaintiff took lease of the said property without getting any advice from his learned Advocate but in fact by that lease, plaintiff's right, title and possession cannot be extinguished and V.P. Case No.31/79-80 is illegal, fraudulent, collusive and void. 

 5. Defendant No. 4 contested the suit by filing a written statement. It is his case that the suit land originally belonged to Goura Chandra Majumder, Ombika Charan Paul and others. In district settlement Khatian No. 75 the suit land has been recorded in the name of Goura Chandra Majumder and his brother, Horish Chandra Majumder but Harish Chandra Majumder by way of delivery of possession, sold the land in respect of dag Nos. 513 and 514. The name of Goura Chandra Majumder have been recorded in respect of 4.16 decimals of land in Khatian No. 75. During SA survey these lands recorded in the name of the heirs of the original owners MRR Khatian No. 95 has been correctly prepared and published MRR Khatian No. 95 was prepared in the names of the heirs of original owner and it has been admitted by all the parties to the suit. Thereafter, the original owners died leaving brother, Ruhini Kumar, who inherited the property. While Ruhini Kumar was in possession of the suit land, having title there to, died leaving Upendra Kumar Majumder, Horendra Kumar Majumder, who inherited the property. Thereafter, the recorded tenants of MRR Khatian, Roamoni Mohin, Ramesh Chandra, Abani Mohan Majumder died leaving their cousin, Kumudini Kanta Majumder, who inherited the property. In khatian No. 95. In respect of 4.46 decimals of land the names of Ruhini Kumar Majumder, Surendra Nath Majumder. Harendra Kumar Majumder, Kumudini Kanta Majumder and Jogadish Chandra Majumder have been recorded as possessor. The said lands of district survey No. 75 and MRR No. 95, for arrear of rents, were put into auction in Certificate Case No. 15930/1960-61. Having need of cash money, the original orders, by concealing the aforesaid fact, sold certain land of dag Nos. 513 and 514 to this defendant after taking proper consideration money on 10-1-1964. Since then, this defendant is in possession. This defendant having come to know of the aforesaid certificate case, purchased the suit land in the name of Muslim Bhuiyan, his brother-in-law. That auction has been confirmed. Thereafter, this defendant having in need of cash money, sold that suit land through Muslim Bhuiyan to Jaker Ullah and to his brother. Abdul Jalil, Thereafter, Hashmat Ullah, the brother of Jaker Ullah, died .01 decimals of land resold to this defendant. In the land of dag Nos. 513 and 514 of MRR Khatian No.45, this defendant is in possession of 4.59 decimals of land and remaining 23 decimals of land is possessed by Jaker Ullah and others. In respect of Dag No. 513, the case of defendant is that, original owner did not construct any pucca houses but they lived in kancha houses and during cyclone of 1960, the dwelling huts of the original owners were damaged. The original owners sold the suit land to this defendant. After auction, they resides to their respective relative' houses and during liberation, in the middle of 1971, while they left for India, on the way they were killed by Pakistani Army. The "benamder dalil/deed" was executed on 25-2-1969 and it was registered on 15-3-1969 as deed No. 3462 in favour of Muslim Bhuiyan and this is correct. During the middle part of 1964 in Dag No. 510 this defendant constructed a semi pucca house VP Misc. Case No. 31/79-80 was legally instituted and the plaintiff obtained lease from the Government, as such, he cannot demand the suit property. Plaintiff filed VP Appeal No. 8 of 1987 but that was dismissed by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC) Revenue on 3-4-1989. This defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit. 

 1. Are both the TS No. 50/90 and Title Suit No. 46/94 maintainable in its present form? 

 5. Whether original DS recorded tenant and some of their hairs transferred the 'Ga' schedule land at Taka 2,000 and the plaintiff put in to possession of the same taking almost earnest money of the price? 

 7. Whether the title of defendant Nos. 5-22 extinguished or title of defendant Nos. 2-22 was extinguished by the certificate case and sale for rent? 

 8. Is the plaintiff entitled to get a decree that suit is not vested property? 

 10. Is the plaintiff entitled to get declaration that Uma scheduled Nadabi deed and kabala described in Cha schedule null and void? 

 11. Is the plaintiff entitled to get declaration that all the proceedings of VP Misc Case No. 31/79-80 and lease order there by in favour of the plaintiff illegal? 

 12. Is the plaintiff entitled to get declaration of title by way of adverse possession? 

 13. Has the defendant No. 4 of TS No. 50/90 and plaintiff of TS 46/94 right title and possession in the land of TS No. 46/94 and entitled to get relief as prayed for? 

 15. Is the plaintiff of the mother suit entitled to get relief as prayed for? 

 8. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellants, submits that, the issues framed by the learned Judge were decided against the plaintiff but the suit has been partly decreed on admission that this defendant admitted certain portion of the land possessed by the defendant and plaintiff as such the impugned judgment suffers from misreading and non-consideration of evidence on record as the learned Advocate submits that the suit was filed for declaration of title by adverse possession against Government, not against defendant No.4 and it is settled principal of law that against Government, 60 years possession is required for having title by adverse possession as such, the learned Judge at least dismissed the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that, plaintiff cannot below hot and cold at the same breathing as in the plaint he admitted that he filed application for getting lease from the Government now he cannot  turned round to say the suit land is not Government property. Learned Advocate further submits that, plaintiff did not produce any reliable evidence to show that there was any agreement for selling of the suit land by so-called owner as there being no evidence on this score as such, learned Judge committed gross illegality in believing plaintiff case. 

 9. Mr Md Lutfur Rahman Mondal, learned Advocate, appearing for the respondents of FA No. 99 of 1999 and for the appellants of FA No. 182 of 1999 and FA No. 183 of 1999, submits that, plaintiff through oral and documentary evidence has been able to prove that he purchased the suit land from the original owners in 1952 and since then heirs in possession, as such, he acquired title by adverse possession particularly against defendant No. 4 Learned Advocate further submits that, possession of the plaintiff having been proved from 1952 he acquired title against the defendant which the learned judge failed to consider and had the learned Judge consider the case properly then he would decreed the suit. Learned Advocate further submits that, on the ill advise of the employees of the vested property cell plaintiff filed application for getting lease of the suit property but for that reason, the right, title, interest, which plaintiff acquired by uninterrupted possession cannot be washed away which is clearly seen from the application which he filed mistakenly on the advice of the employees of the vested property cell. Learned advocate further submits that, defendant No. 4 from beginning acted surreptitiously in grabbing the suit land as he not only filed criminal case against plaintiff but also put the case land into auction illegally and also purchased the same in the name of his brother-in-law, as such, it is clear that defendant No. 4 was acted against the plaintiff for enjoyment of the suit land. Learned Advocate cited several decisions in support of his submission. Mr Md Lutfur Rahman Mondal, learned Advocate relied on the case of Saifur Rahman vs Haider Shah, 19 DLR (SC) 433 wherein on the question that when execution of a decree within 12 years was presented by resort to fraud upon Court, Supreme Court of Pakistan held that fraud includes deceit and circumvention judgment obtained by fraud is non-existent in eye of law. Learned Advocate next relied on the case of Jeka Dula vs Bai Jivi, AIR 1938 Bombay 37, the case on Specific Performance of Contract, where it has been filed that, a grantor or a lessor cannot be allowed to dispute his own title with either the grantee or the lessee. Learned Advocate then relied on the case of Arun Kumar Pal vs Assistant Custodian of Enemy Property (Land and Building) and ADC (Rev), 1983 BCR 225, where it has been held that, mere prayer for lease of the property from the Deputy Custodian of Enemy Property does not stop a person from challenging the enemy character of the suit property. There is no estoppels against statute. Then learned Advocate relied on the case of Md Ashraf Ali vs Fatigue Chandra Saha, 1983 BLD (AD) 315, where on a case of adverse possession, Appellate Division held that the plaintiffs' claim is against the real owner on the basis of Bonaparte and they were possessing the land for more than the statutory period adversely against him and have perfected their title by such possession against him and not against the defendants. Plaintiffs have not derived title against the defendants by adverse possession but against the real owner. The defendant cannot plead point of limitation as the defendant was not in physical possession. Though the plaintiffs could not prove their bainapatra, their physical possession had titled in their favour against the true owner and the suit was therefore rightly, decreed. 

 10. Learned Advocate then relied on the case of Fazar Ali Tendal vs Fazal Minh, 12 BLD (AD) 203, where it has been held that treatment of documents (i.e. nadabi patra, CS khatian and report of the pleader commissioner) the Appellate Division held that these are not documents of title. Those are considered as supportive evidence of the plaintiffs' claim of title through their kabala. Learned Advocate next relied on the case of Nagendra Chandra Sarker vs Aftabuddin, 15 BLD (AD) 135, where it has been held that, the result, of a criminal case does not affect a civil suit in any way. The civil Court is free to come to its own findings independent of the result of the criminal case. 

 13. Learned Judge on consideration of issue Nos. 1 and 2 held that, the suit is barred by principle of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence as the plaintiff did not pray for adverse possession against the principle-defendants. The suit is barred by law of limitation. On issue No. 3 learned Judge held that "therefore, in view of such testimony as to knowledge of auction purchase and suit nadabi deed and suit kabala since 1979 and 1964 the mother suit is barred by law of limitation". Learned Judge on issue No. 4 on reference to the decision of 47 DLR 524 and 13 DLR 865, held that, 'but in this case 1st part of provision of order 1 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure will come in to play. On the contrary Title Suit No. 46 of 1994 having been brought against the stranger to the suit khatians need not be impleaded other lawful co-sharers as such this suit is bad for defect of parties.' On consideration of issue No. 5 is whether original RS recorded tenant and their heirs transferred the 'ga' schedule land at Taka 2,000 and plaintiff was put into possession, learned Judge found that "none of the PWs corroborated or said anything to this effect. Therefore, plaintiff could not prove his possession since 1948 by virtue of alleged oral contract for sale and payment of alleged consideration money. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not specify the case of looting of original owners homestead nor the date of alleged contract for sale". On consider of issue No. 6 the learned Judge decided it against the plaintiff as PW 3. Abdur Rahim during cross-examination stated that "firstly they had a farm, then homestead admittedly original plaintiff has got 70 x 35 cubic length vide two storied pucca building in the village Ullapara. So, question arise why he would have erected against homestead in the suit land measuring 15 decimals of land. Rather evidence on record convinces us that those are erected on the period stated by the defence in his pleadings". Learned Judge also decided issue No. 7 against plaintiff as 'so it appears that title of the original owner defendant Nos. 5-22 has been extinguished by exhibit Kha, exhibit Ga not and Gha ultimately in favour of defendant. None of them challenged auction sale. It may noted that ostensible auction purchaser Muslim Bhuiyan, sister's husband of defendant No. 4 did not challenge benami purchase of auction'. In deciding issue No. 8 learned Judge found that "it may be noted that is decided by the VP authority itself that the suit property is not vested one and lease order passed in favour of the original plaintiff was duly cancelled at the instance of the defendant on contest. So, it is redundant to pass any decision further to this effect as both sides think that suit property was never vested and non-resident one." Learned Judge decided issue No. 9 as "co-sharers of the suit MRR Khatian challenged the proceedings but the original plaintiff whose name is not available in any paper like RoR nor he paid any rent thereof, during relevant period nor subsequent to the same. No appropriate authority challenged the impugned certificate proceedings. Mere irregularity for non observance of any procedural law or minor anomalies of facts do not render the proceeding null and void as a whole. Stranger like plaintiff has no locus standi to challenge the same. With the certificate sale interest of the original owners extinguished. Moreover, since plaintiff did not take any legal step against the said proceeding within statutory period of limitation since his knowledge in 1979 AD, he has lost right of challenging proceedings of certificate case in question." On issue No. 10, learned Judge inter alia on reference to the several decisions of Indian jurisdiction held that "so, in view of above principle the effect of section 66 is not to make benami transaction illegal and the instant suit is not in between ostensible purchaser and the real purchaser but in between stranger and real purchaser. Therefore, this sort of benami transaction cannot be treated as null and void and same case with subsequent nadabi transaction in between defendant and ostensible purchaser Muslim Bhuiyan, the brother-in-law of the defendant. Stranger like original plaintiff cannot question about the said nadabi deed and kabala described in "Sa" schedule land", In deciding issue No.11, learned Judge held that "in view of preceding discussion plaintiff has lost right to challenge proceedings of VP Misc. Case No. 31/79-80 by which plaintiff brought lease of 3.08 acres of land out of suit land, which is subsequently cancelled at the instance of defendant on contest." In deciding issue No. 12, learned Judge on consideration of deposition of PW 2, Advocate Commissioner's cross examination and also on consideration of deposition of PW 4 Mir Md Abdul and PW 5, is a earth work labourer, held that, 'so, it may safely be presumed that original plaintiff has been possession 1.80 acres of land in plot No.510 adversely before his filing to the application the exhibit Uma openly notoriously for more than 12 years'. In deciding issue No. 13, learned judge on consideration of some judgments and some reports decided in Indian jurisdiction held that "a judgment in criminal case is admissible to show what order was made, who the party to the dispute and what the land in dispute was and who was held entitled to possession. "Learned Judge decided issue No. 14 that "the suit land is not suffered from unspecification and vagueness. And decided issue No. 15 as plaintiff by way of adverse possession is entitled in respect of 1.80 acres of land. 

 14. It appears that the learned Judge held that the suit is barred by limitation, bad for defect of parties, plaintiff's predecessors title was extinguished, plaintiff cannot challenge the auction is favour of defendant, plaintiff's witnesses did not support plaint case, the plaintiff's predecessors names have not been recorded in any khatians, no rent receipt is produced by plaintiff, plaintiff being a stranger has no locus standi to challenge the benami transaction in between defendant and his brother-in-law and after holding as such, the suit ought to be dismissed but the learned Judge decreed the suit in part. Let us see how far the judgment is sustainable in law. 

 15. The suit was filed against defendant No. 1 i.e. Government of Bangladesh for declaration of title by adverse possession. Let us see what the plaintiff wanted to prove. Plaintiff sought for declaration that he got adverse possession in respect of 'ga' schedule land as ga schedule relates to some dwelling viti, and pond with some planted trees. Plaintiff narrated the fact that original owners of the suit land while left the country in 1952 orally sold the suit land to the plaintiff. Let us quote from plaint as:- 

 17. From the deposition, the case of the plaintiff on adverse possession against Government stands totally vague as one cannot see the head and tail of plaintiffs' claim which no one can be gathered either from the plaint or from his deposition. If we consider the plaintiff's entire case make out in plaint and from his deposition then it stands as the Hindu community due to fear of their life in Pakistan, transferred their land to the Muslim like plaintiff and delivered possession. Plaintiff claimed title against the original owners as they transferred the land orally and by adverse possession against the Government. Plaintiff did not make any prayer against his original owner but plaintiff strict his claim of adverse possession against Government. We have already seen the plaint case of oral purchase has not been proved. These is total vagueness on his score. A person cannot forget certain things and one of them is acquiring property, i.e. the date when the contract is made, the date the money transacted, the date the deed registered. Here the case is of purchasing the property orally and plaintiff such state of affairs should particular over the event of transaction. But we find from the plaint and also from deposition of the plaintiff that everything of the plaintiff regarding transfer of the suit land is so much in dark that it cannot be seen as it lost in the darkness. The case of oral purchase stands as unbelievable. 

 19. Now another factor is that plaintiff claim the he purchase the suit property orally as such he cannot assert that he got title by adverse possession as title by adverse possession is to be claimed by a person whose title is to be perfected other than by virtue of a tile deed or a contract to purchase. It is the case of the plaintiff that suit land was declared as enemy property. It is the case of the plaintiff that he mistakenly filed application for getting lease of the property on the advice of the employees of the vested property cell. The advice of the employees of the vested property may be mistakenly, but since application was filed for getting lease, it proved that he accepted the property as enemy property. Now he cannot turned round and sought declaration of title by adverse possession against Bangladesh. The limitation for getting title by adverse possession against Government is 60 years uninterrupted possession. If it assumed the case of the plaintiff that he entered into possession in 1952 from the original owners, but the suit having filed in 1990, as such he did not acquired title by adverse possession against principal defendant i.e. Government of Bangladesh. 

 22. The impugned judgment and decree dated 12-10-1998 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge Artha Rin Adalat, Noakhali decreeing the suit party by declaring title of the plaintiff by advise. Possession in respect of 1.80 acres of land out of 2.93 acres of land of plot No. 510 in Title Suit No. 50 of 1990 is set aside. Title Suit No. 50 of 1990 is dismissed.

caseno:
Civil Revision No. 1074 of 2004 
with 
Civil Rule No. 928 (R) of 2005 
with 
Civil Rule No. 17(R) of 2006.
parties:
Abdus Sattar ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Gazi Golam Mohammad and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. This revisional application under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant-respondent is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31-3-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 41 of 2000 allowing the appeal by reversing the judgment and decree dated 2-3-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 36 of 1994 dismissed the suit. 

 3. The opposite party No.1, Gazi Golam Mahammad, as plaintiff filed Title Suit No: 36 of 1994 in the court of Subordinate Judge, Chandpur for declaration of title in the suit land. 

 4. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land appertaining to an area of 0.05 acres in plot No. 931 under CS khatian No. 242 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 229 and 0.06 acres in both former and present plot No. 931/969 of mouza Dasadi under both District and police station Chandpur has been owning and possessing by Durga Kumar Chakraborty and others from their predecessor namely, Shamkanti Das alias Shamcharan Chakraborty that the plaintiff, namely Gazi Nur Mohammad (now dead) brought Title Suit No. 324 of 1958 in the court of Munsif, first court at Chandqur ( relating to non, suit land) for specific performance of contract, whereupon the decree was passed on 4-4-1961 in favour of the plaintiff with Taka 417.50 as cost; that thereafter said Nur Mohammad obtained registered deed on 11-5-1963 through court: that Nur Mohammad, then filed an execution Case bearing No. 72 of 1963 for realisation of the alleged cost money; that the plaintiff also purchased the land in suit along with other land in auction as highest bidder and also took Bainama on 26-1-1992; that 931 Khatian was mentioned wrongly in that execution case in place of correct CS khatian No. 242 or SA khatian No. 229 and plot No.931-931/969 but the boundary mentioned in auction was intact and that the possession of the land was handed over to plaintiff on 30-4-1992 with performing all formalities of auction sale and thus the case for execution of decree bearing No. 72 of 1963 was disposed of on 31-5-1992 with full satisfaction and since then the plaintiff has been possessing and enjoying its interest by himself as well as by his tenants. It is further stated that the plaintiff namely, GaziNur Mohammad died during pendency of Execution case No. 72 of 1963 and his heirs namely, Hayet-un-nessa and others were substituted in the case; that the defendant refused and threw challenge over the right and status of the plaintiff on the suit land on 16-9-1994 on the basis of a decree in a title suit bearing No. 468 of 1982 and also threatened to dispossess them and for which the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 128 of 1994 for permanent injunction; that the suit was filed in wrong forum for which he finally withdrew the same. It is further stated that the Deputy Commissioner and others on behalf of the government of Bangladesh filed another suit being No. 34 of 1992 praying for declaring the alleged auction and the decree in execution case No. 72 of 1963 as illegal, not binding upon and collusive but the suit was ultimately dismissed. 

 6. It is further stated that the defendant has been threatened by some Nur Islam, Abdul Bepari and Kasim Patari on 30-11-1982 and in order to resist them he filed Title Suit No. 468 of 1982 for permanent injunction and during pendency of that suit; that the defendant was dispossessed from the land as such prayed for mandatory injunction and that the suit was dismissed, on which, an appeal was preferred and the same was allowed and that thereafter the defendant of that suit went to the High Court and filed a Civil Revision which was discharged. 

 7. It is further stated that the plaintiff did not file any case for execution of decree bearing No. 72 of 1963 and no auction took place and that all are paper transactions; that the plaintiff has no right, title and interest in the suit land and the plaintiff filed the suit falsely which is liable to be dismissed. 

 2. Whether the, title of the plaintiff in suit land through auction purchase is to be declared? 

 3. Whether the judgment and decree in title suit No.486 of 1982 be declared as not binding upon the plaintiff? 

 6. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get decree as prayed for? 

 11. The plaintiff filed a certified copy of CS khatian marked Exhibit 1, a copy Of SA khatian marked Exhibit 2, certified copy of judgment of the suit No. 324 of 1958 marked as Exhibit 3, Original registered deed No. 4239 dated 11-5-1963 with respect to title execution case No.7 of 1962 marked as Exhibit 4, Petition for the title execution case No. 72 of 1963 in the Munsif, First Court, Chandpur marked Exhibit-5, Original Boinama as regard auction purchase in said execution case marked Exhibit 6, certified copy of writ of execution marked Exhibit 6(ka), certified copy of the plaint of title suit No. 34 of 1992 marked Exhibit 7(ka), certified copy of the order dated 7-7-1992 of suit marked as Exhibit 7 (kha), information slip as regard title suit No. 468 of 1982 marked Exhibit 8 and certified copy of the judgment of the Additional District Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No.9 in 1995 marked Exhibit 9 in support of his contention. 

 12. On the other hand, defendant No. 1 has submitted certified copy of CS khatian No. 242 marked Exhibit-Ka, certified copy of the SA khatian No. 229 marked as Exhibit ka(1), report dated 21-8-1982 by Tahashilder in VP Case marked as Exhibit- Kha, 2 sheets of DCR as regard rent marked Exhibit-GA, One trade licence marked Exhibit-Gha, certified copy of the judgment and decree in title suit No. 71 of 1985 marked as Exhibit-Oma, certified copy of the order of Civil Revision No. 247 of 1886 (Comilla)/8916 of 1991 (Dhaka) dated 27-3-1994 marked Exhibit-Cha and certified copy of the order dated 19-5-1994 in his case marked Exhibit- Cha(1) in support of his contention. 

 15. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 2-3-2000, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal being No. 41 of 2000 in the court of the learned District Judge, Chandpur and on transfer, the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur who considering the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and decree dated 2-3-2000. 

 16. The respondent being aggrieved RY the impugned judgment and decree dated 31-3-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in title Appeal No. 41 of 2000 as the petitioner filed this revisional application before this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 19. Mr TM Shakil Hossain, the, learned Advocate for the opposite parties, submits. that the representative of government, Deputy Commissioner, Chandqur, filed Title Suit No. 34 of 1992 for canceling the auction sale in that suit; that the Government did not deny that the, suit land and plaintiff's auction purchased land are not same; that as such, the petitioner of the Civil Revision who is merely a lessee of government has no right to raise the question that the suit land is not auction purchased land and that the government did not prefer any revision before the High Court against the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court meaning thereby government has admitted the land in suit as property of opposite party No. 1, as such, the petitioner being a lessee under the government has no interest in the suit land. He further submits that the trial Court though dismissed the suit but after considering the materials on record came to the finding that the defendant No. 1 that is, the present petitioner, has no interest in the land in suit which was affirmed by the learned appellate Court and against that finding, petitioner did not file any cross appeal or objection as such the court in exercising its revisional jurisdiction cannot interfere with the concurrent finding. 

 23. Since the petitioner, Abdul Mannan Mal, deposed as DW 2 in original suit, so it is quite clear that he was aware of the matter. As such the delay cannot be condoned and consequently the Rule being No. 17(R) of 2006 is discharged without any order as to cost. 

 26. It is, therefore, clear that the judgment and decree in original title suit No. 324 of 1958 (Exhibit-3) and their effectiveness and validity remain intact and untouched. 

 27. It is further found that the government represented by Deputy Commissioner, Chandpur filed Title suit No. 34 of 1992 for cancellation of auction sale but the government did not deny that the suit land and the plaintiff auction purchased land is not same, as such, the petitioner of the present revision who is a lessee of the government has no right to raise the question that the suit land is not auction purchased land. 

 30. The moot point for determination is, whether the plaintiff actually got possession of the suit land through auction purchase is admitted that there were some mistakes both in execution case and boinama. But in the boinama there was mentioning of boundary in two sides. The consistent view of our Apex court is that the case of dispute between the plot and khatian, boundary will prevail. Our Appellate Division in the case of Mofizullah Bhuiyan and others vs Sree Narayan Chandra Roy and others reported in 3 MLR (AD) 196 held that when the plaintiffs succeed in proving their title and possession in the suit, land, they are entitled to get a decree for declaration of his title therein. The suit cannot be dismissed merely on the ground of minor variations in the description of the boundaries of the suit land. 

 34. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree dated 31-3-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Chandpur in title Appeal No. 41 of 2000 is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Afia Begum and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Abdul Baset Mia & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
5. The trial Court allowed the prayer for preemption on the finding that the pre-emptees were neither co-sharers by purchase or by inheritance. As against the judgment of the trial Court the pre-emptees went on appeal. The appellate Court allowed the appeal on the finding that land purchased by the pre-emptees father on October 11, 1969 was of SA Khatian No. 1151, that the land of CS Khatian No. 986 has been listed in SA Khatian No. 1151, that the finding of the trial Court as to pre-emptees of not being co-sharers on the ground that there was no mention of the SA khatian in the kabala (Exhibit 'Uma') in the name of the plaintiffs' father is not correct since the land of CS khatian No. 986 has been listed in SA khatian No. 1151, that the pre-emptees as heirs of their father who purchased land of the holding in question on October 11, 1969 are the co- sharers of the holding in question by inheritance and, as such, pre-emptor is not entitled to the relief sought i.e. pre-emptor cannot seek preemption in respect of the transfer that took place on November 21, 1991 in favour of the pre-emptees. 

 9. Leave was granted to consider the contentions that the High Court Division was wrong in holding that after reconveyance there remained nothing to be preempted as title of the land sought to be preempted vested with the original owner and the cause of action for which the case for preemption was filed no longer existed, that as the deed of reconveyance was made during the pendency of the Miscellaneous case for preemption and, as such, the reconveyance so made cannot defeat the right of pre-emptor to preempt the case land, that the proposition of law as laid down in the case of Md Abbas Ali vs Md Osman Ali (minor) and others reported in 37 DLR 324 relied upon by the High Court Division in rejecting the prayer for preemption in case is not reviewed then by the transaction of the said kind the whole purpose of filing of a preemption case will be defeated. 

 11. The state of right of preemption in the background of reconveyance of the land intended to be preempted prior to the filing of the case seeking preemption and reconveyance of the land during pendency of the case filed seeking preemption came up for consideration before this Division as well as before the High Court Division on several occasions. The decision that has been made in the reported cases as regard the state of right of preemption in respect of the land intended to be preempted but reconveyed to the original owner (vendor) and thereupon right, title and interest have vested with him and that on such reconveyance the original owner is possessing the land is that with such reconveyance right of preemption no longer exists. There is also one line of decisions that a transfer followed by a deed of reconveyance would not defeat the right of preemption and that the pre-emptor would take the preemption with the encumbrance of reconveyance. The transaction i.e. reconveyance, pursuant to an agreement for reconveyance said to have been executed at the time of sale would be a clog on preemption provided the reconveyance is not a sham and colourable transaction or, in other words, is not a transaction of the kind sole object whereof is to defeat the right of preemption. The other view is that if the deed of re- conveyance is a genuine one and that on the basis thereof if the pre-emptee reconveyed the land to the original owner (vendor) and the right, title and interest vest in the vendor and the possession of the land sought to be preempted has also gone back to him in that case even though the reconveyance has been made during the pendency of the case seeking preemption the case so filed would become infructuous since with the reconveyance right of preemption ceased to exist. In case of reconveyance either before the filing of the case seeking preemption or at a time when the case seeking preemption is pending the Court would be required to examine whether the transaction is a genuine one or the same is a sham and colourable transaction. If by reconveyance right, title and interest does not vest with the original owner and that the possession of the land also does not go back to the original owner in that case the transaction i.e. reconveyance would be considered a sham and colourable transaction and the right of preemption will exist. The transaction i.e. reconveyance, whether is genuine or a sham and colourable one is to be determined in the background of the evidence brought on record by the parties: If the evidence is in the affirmative i.e. right, title and interest in the land sought to be pre-empted has gone back to the vendor and the land sought to be preempted is possessed by the vendor, in that case there would be no right of pre-emption whether the reconveyance is made before the filing of the case seeking preemption or during the pendency of the case. The contrary of the aforesaid state of the matter would not defeat the right of pre-emption. 

 13. Even if for argument's sake it is accepted that reconveyance having been made during pendency of the case seeking preemption the same could not be a clog for allowing preemption is accepted, then too pre-emptor was not entitled to preempt the land sought to be pre-empted since on consideration of the materials on record last Court of fact found that the pre-emptees were co-sharers by inheritance of the holding land of which sought to be preempted. The High Court Division, on independent consideration of the materials on record, concurred with the finding of the appellate Court that the pre-emptees are the co-sharers of the holding by inheritance long before purchase and the pre-emptor is cosharer by purchase. At the time of purchase sought to be preempted, the pre-emptees were co-sharers of the holding in question by inheritance. The learned Advocate-on-Record could not refer to any material to take exception to the finding of the High Court Division and the Court of appeal that the pre-emptees are co-sharers of the holding land of which sought to be preempted by inheritance at the material time i.e. at the time of sale sought to be preempted.

parties:
Abi Abdullah (Md) and others ------ Petitioners 
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land & ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
6. The petitioners have given a short background of the law relating to diluvion and alluvion of lands. By the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act, No. XXVIII of 1951) the rent-receivers intervening between the Government and the actual occupants of the said land were abolished and such occupants became tenants directly under the Government subject to a ceiling as to the maximum area of land which a tenant could hold. Time to time the law relating to the tenant's right on his diluviated and alluviated land were passed. On 13-7-94 the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 was promulgated substituting in place of the old section 86 with regard to abatement of rent on account of diluvion and determination of right in land re-appearing on account of alluvion. By the said Act, the right, title, interest of the original tenant or his successor-in-interest would subsist in the lands of a holding or portion thereof during the period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appeared in situ within 30 years of their loss instead of 20 years. The respondent No. 1 by the impugned order issued to all the Deputy Commissioners of the Districts including Bhola directed them to take necessary steps for processing the diluvion and alluvion land and that all land already diluviated and alluviated shall vest in the Government and, as such, be recorded in the Khas-khatian of the government. The petitioners are aggrieved by the impugned circular/order because it is not in accordance with the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 and the Revenue authorities in pursuance of the said memo refused to accept rents for the alluviated lands belonging to the petitioners in spite of repeated requests approaches. Hence, the petitioners are constrained to file this writ petition challenging the validity of the impugned order (Annexure-E) and obtained the present Rule. 

 9. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Senior Advocate with Mr AQM Safiullah, Advocate appearing for the writ petitioners, submits that before amendment as per section 86(4) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (EB Act, XXVIII of 1951) the petitioners' ownership subsisted, inasmuch as the lands of the above mouzas reappeared in 1993-94. While the ownership of the petitioners was continuing without any break and they were in exclusive possession,' there came the amendment of section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 on 13-7-94 by the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 (Act XV of 1994). He further submits that the impugned memo dated 29-11-1994 (Annexure-E) issued by the respondent No.1 giving illegal interpretation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 (Act XV of 1994) directing the respondent No. 2, the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola not to give effect to the above Act of 1994 in respect of the lands which have been diluviated and alluviated before 13-7-1994 is wholly illegal, malafide, without jurisdiction, without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. It is further argued by him that section 86(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 clearly envisages that the right, title, interest of the original tenant or his successors-in-interest shall subsist in the lands of a holding or portion thereof during the period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appear in situ within 30 years of their loss and that the impugned memo dated 29-11-94 is contrary to the decision of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh reported in 31 DLR (AD) 195 wherein it was held that the proprietary right of the person to whom the land belonged and during the period of submergence of the land the ownership is not lost but merely suspended and on its re- appearance in its old site the owner gets it back. 

 10. Mrs Quamrunnessa, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondents, has defended the impugned order as being in accordance with law. She argued that the Act of 1994 is not retrospective but prospective and the said Act will be applicable only to diluvion and alluvion of the land after 13th July, 1994. She further submits that the right, title and interest of all lands which had diluviated or alluviated prior to that date, that is 13th July, 1994 will vest in the Government and, would be recorded in the khas khatian. 

 12. The petitioner's case is that by the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1994 (Act XV of 1994) the right, title, interest in their lands lost by diluvion has been restored and on its re-appearance they are entitled to get its allotment subject to ceiling imposed by the Act as tenant of the land. If the impugned order is not interfered with their right of ownership which has been restored by the Act, 1994 would be taken away. It is also submitted that the respondents have misconstrued both the provisions of President's Order No. 135 of 1972 and the Act of 1994 which amended section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950. 

 13. Admittedly, the lands in question were originally owned and possessed by the petitioners and they paid rents upto 1983 and Khatians were prepared in their names. It is further admitted that petitioners lands were washed away and diluviated in 1960-1962 and reappeared in 1974-75 and once again diluviated in 1988 and remained under water till 1992 and ultimately re-appeared or reformed in situ in 1993-94. It is also not denied that the petitioners are still in possession of the said lands. The State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1994 (Act XV of 1994) came into force in July, 1994. By sub-section (2) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by Act XV of 1994 the right, title and interest of the original tenant or his successors in interest shall subsist in the lands of a holding on operation thereof during the period of loss by diluvion if such lands re-appear in situ within 30 years of their loss. Respondents could not show anything that the land in question in the meantime had been recorded in the khas khatian of the Government and allotment was made to anyone else

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1456 of 2001
parties:
Abul Kashem Howlader & ors  ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md Kasem Ali Khan and others  ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title and correction of record of right in respect of suit land stating, inter cilia, that 12 annas share of Kayem Karsha Gour Kishore Howlader was recorded in Khewat No. 41/1 and 4 annas share of the said Kayam Karsha was recorded in Khewat No. 41/1, out of the 12 annas share of the Kayem Karsha as recorded in Khewat No. 41/2, share belonged to Kajem Howlader and 4 annas belonged to Sadan Howlader and the Kayem Karsha was recorded in Khewat No. 41/2 belonged to Samajuddin Howlader out of total quantity of 14.57 acres of land recorded in Khewat No. 41/1, 3.51 acres was khas land and out of total 5.43 acres of land in Khewat No. 41/2, 3.40 acres was the khas land and the remaining land of the respective Khewats were tenanted land which were recorded under khatian Nos. 266 to 270 in the name of tenants. That Kajem Howlader and Sadan Howlader owned and possessed 3.51 acres of land of Khewat No. 41/1 and Somojuddin Howlader possessed 3.40 acres of khas land of Khewat No. 41/2. The said 3.51 acres have been recorded in plot Nos. 2818, 2825, 2828, 2835 and 2844 and the said 3.40 acres of khas land have been recorded in plot Nos. 2842, 2864, 2865 and 2867. That on the death of Kajem Howlader his sons Abdul Kader, Abdul Jabbar, Abdul Wahed and Ahmed Howlader in collusion with the landlords got the entire lands of the aforesaid 2 (two) Khewats auction sold and they purchased the same with their own money and for their own benefit in the benami of Baser Sarder. They also fabricated a Mirash Ijara in (FD) respect of 12 annas share of the entire Kayem Karsha including the tenanted land. That plaintiffs predecessor Khalilur Rahman and his co-sharers went to pay rents when the Tahsilder told them about the auction sale and thereupon a fresh dispute arose between Abdul Kader Howlader and his brothers, on one hand and Khalilur Rahman, on the other hand. Thereupon, Abdul Kader and his brother purchased 12 annas share of the entire Kayem Karsha from the said Baser Sarder in the benami of Abdul Sheikh and Munar Khan by suppression of the facts of Mirash Ijara to Khalilur Rahman and others. And the plaintiffs' predecessor Khalilur Rahman and others purchased the remaining 4 annas share from Baser Sarder and thus came to a settlement inasmuch as the previous position in regard to share in the entire Kayem Karsha remained as it was. After some time, the fraudulent creation of Mirash Ijara became known and thereupon a quarrel arose between Khalilur Rahman and his sharers on one side and Abdul Kader and his brothers on the other side. To have an amicable settlement in the matter, all the parties viz., Abdul Kader and his brother and Khalilur Rahman and his other co-sharers, namely, Hachan Howlader and Yasin Howlader (the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-19) executed and registered a deed of partition dated 25-7-1928. In terms of the said deed of partition Abdul Kader Howlader and his brothers got the khas and tenanted lands of Khewat No. 41/1 and Khalilur Rahman Howlader and Yasin Howlader got the entire khas and tenanted lands of Khewat No. 4½ as usual disregarding the fraudulent Mirash Ijara and fraudulent auction sale and purchase in the name of Baser Sarder at first and in the name of Abdul Shaikh and Munar Khan subsequently by way of fraudulent and benami transaction. The above named benamder Baser Sarder, Abdul Sheik and Munar Khan never possessed any land of the 2(two) Khewats. But subsequently, Abdul Kader's son Hashem Howlader, the defendant No. 20, got the RS and SA Khatians recorded fraudulently in their name by suppression of the terms of partition deed. That subsequently, the defendant Nos. 20 to 51 and their predecessors and the defendant Nos. 59 to 115 brought Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 alleging that RS and SA record of the lands of Khewat Nos. 41/1 and 41/2 are wrong. In that suit Khalilur Rahman the plaintiffs predecessor and the defendants Nos. 1-19 were included as plaintiffs. But, as a matter of fact, the said Khalilur Rahman alias Ibrahim Howlader predecessor of the plaintiff, never signed the power and the plaint; that he did not know anything about the suit; the signatures in the plaint and power were forged. After the death of Khalilur Rahman during pendency of the suit his heirs including the plaintiffs are alleged to have been substituted. But as a matter of fact the plaintiff did not know anything about the suit, nor he signed any vokalatnama or any petition in that suit. The plaintiff was all along serving in Pakistan Air Force and he was posted throughout in West Pakistan from 1952 to 1964 and the plaintiff had all along been living in West Pakistan with his family from the year, 1956 to May, 1964 and during this period, he never came to the then East Pakistan; plaintiff's signatures in any documents of the suit, if there be any, were all forged and fabricated and the plaintiff had no knowledge about the suit. That once plaintiff's father Khalilur Rahman for securing the repayment of a debt, executed a Jaisudi-mortgage of 1.25 of 0.25 bighas of land of his share from the land of Khewat No. 41/2 in favour of Abdul Jabbar, Abdul Wohed, Abdul Kader Ahmed Howlader and Hashem Ali Howlader, the defendant No. 20. Accordingly, possession of the mortgage land was also in their favour and subsequently, Khalilur Rahman repaid the mortgage debt and the Mortgagor returned the mortgage deed with an endorsement to its back and delivered possession of the mortgage land back to Khalilur Rahman. That the direct allegation of the plaintiff is that defendant No. 20. Hashem Ali Howlader is a corrupt and shrewd person and he has forged the name of Khalilur Rahman as the plaintiff in the title suit in collusion and with the help of defendants secured ex parte decree in that suit. Thereafter, Miscellaneous case arose in the name of different persons but ultimately those cases were dismissed and the decree of the title suit remained unchallenged. Subsequently, it transpired that the said defendant No. 20, got a substitution petition filed in the suit in the name of the minor sons of Khalilur Rahman without bringing it to the knowledge of their natural guardian; all these are done by the defendant No. 20 by practicing fraud upon the Court. That thereafter another Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 was fraudulently instituted through defendant No. 61. Mokhtar Ali, and on suppression of all processes by practicing fraud on the Court the suit was dismissed collusively. So in spite of all the rehearing of the cases and the Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 which were fabricated, the decree of the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 remaining unchallenged in some of the above suits and rehearing cases the plaintiff was made a party and the summons were shown served upon him fraudulently although the plaintiff had been living in West Pakistan serving in the Air Force. That it is stated that the original Title Suit No. 18 of 1956 was filed in the First Court of Subordinate Judge and subsequently, the said Title Suit was transferred to the Fourth Court of Subordinate Judge and renumbered as Title Suit No. 49 of 1958; Khalilur Rahman, the plaintiff predecessor or the plaintiff himself never signed any power or plaint nor they authorised anybody else to sign any such paper on their behalf nor the plaintiff even engaged the Lawyer Babu Pabitra Kumar Ghose nor the plaintiff authorised Mohammad Ismail or Saijuddin to present any power on his behalf; all the papers standing in the name of Khalilur Rahman and the plaintiff are forged, fraudulent and collusive. The written statement said to have been filed in the name of defendant Nos. 20-38 in Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 through Hachan Imam Chowdhury, Advocate, is also fraudulent, inasmuch as no contesting defendant could file a written statement of that nature. The plaintiff never engaged Mr Hachan Imam Chowdhury. All these were done fraudulently by the defendant No. 20 and he suppressed everything and kept the plaintiff ignorant about the matter all through. The defendant Nos. 20-115 never possessed the land of the Khewat No. 41/2 measuring 3.73 acres being the suit land which have been recorded in RS Khatian No. 265 and SA Khatian No. 619 and the plaintiff came to know about the impugned decree in the last part of Falgun 1372 BS. Then he procured all the necessary particulars and papers and brought this suit for a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 in the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal is illegal, fraudulent, void ab initio, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 120 and 121 supported the plaintiff's case by filing written statement. The defendant No. 7, 10-13 and 52-56 also supported the plaintiffs case by filing written statement. Defendant Nos. 26-107 contested the case filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and barred by the principles of res judicata. Their further case is that all the statements made in the plaint are false; that summons/notice/process of the Title Suit No. 18 of 1956. Title Suit No. 49 of 1958. Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1959, Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 1959 and Title Suit No. 3 of 1961 were not collusive and fraudulent nor were they suppressed as alleged by the plaintiff. Their further case is that Khalilur Rahman the plaintiff's father signed all the necessary papers of the Title Suit No. 18 of 1956 and the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 and after his death the plaintiff and his brother Ismail, the defendant No. 4 and others file application under their own signature for substitution. None of this signature were forged and fabricated; plaintiff's brother Ismail got the Vokalatnama presented on 21-5-1958 through Saijuddin Howlader, the defendant No. 20 against whom allegations of fraud, collusion and fabrication have been made in the plaint, was then serving in a High School of Bhola and he did not know about the institution of the suit or cases. Ainuddin Sheikh who was defendant No. 4 in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 (defendant No. 19 in the present suit) filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1959 which was dismissed on contest on 13-7-1959. Thereafter, Dhola Bibi defendant No.1 in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 and (now defendant No. 116 in this suit), filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 1959 and it was also dismissed on 23-6-1960. In the said Miscellaneous Case the plaintiff and his brother along with their co-sharers and the defendant Nos. 20-38 together filed a solenama and Ismail; the plaintiff's brother, had also deposed for Dhola Bibi in the said Miscellaneous Case; Mokter Ali who was defendant No. 11 in the Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 (now defendant No. 61 in this suit) filed Title Suit No. 3, of 1961; in that suit the defendant Nos. 20-38 -including the present plaintiff filed a joint written statement for setting aside the decree and plaintiff's brother Ismail deposed in that suit. The defendant No. 20 also filed a separate written statement. But in none of the suits and cases the plaintiff's signatures were forged as alleged in the plaint. The defendant's further case is that plaintiff's allegation that he had all along been in West Pakistan from 1952-1964 is false. Their case is that Baser Sarder purchased the khas and tenanted land of the Khewat Nos. 41/1 and 41/2 and possessed it and thereafter he granted a Mirash Ijara to the extent of 12 annas share to Abdul Kader and others, the predecessors of defendant Nos. 20-44 by vinue of a patta dated 17-10-1911 and thereafter Abdul Sheikh and Munir Khan acquired 12 annas share of khas and tenanted lands of the Kayem Karsha and Khalilur Rahman and others acquired the remaining 4 annas share. It is further alleged that on auction purchasing the Mirash Ijara recorded in Khatian No. 270 for arrears of rent, these defendants got the same merged in the Kayem Karsha and have been possessing as such a land of 6.91, 3.51 in total 10.42 acres appertaining to the khas land of Mirash Ijara as well as Kayem Karsha. These 10.42 acres subsequently increased to 10.60 acres. In short, these defendants have denied the allegation of the plaint and that Baser Sarder, Abdul Shiekh and Munir Khan were benamders. They also denied the deed of partition and they also raised an objection regarding the maintainability of this suit without impleading the heirs of the principal defendants in the suit. They have further denied that Sadan Howlader or his heirs did not possess any land on the basis of kabala from Abdul Shaikh and Munir Khan. 

 5. The defendant Nos. 26-107 preferred an appeal against the said judgment and decree in Title Appeal No. 249 of 1969 and the same was dismissed on 30-7-1977. The appellants thereafter preferred Second Appeal No. 584 of 1978 which has been disposed of as above by judgment and order dated 9-5-2001. 

 6. Mr Akram Hossain Amin, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, submitted that the ex parte decree not being divisible in a suit for declaration of title, the High Court Division erred in law in modifying the judgment and decree be of the trial Court duly affirmed by the appellate Court to the extent that the said ex parte decree be declared as fraudulent against Abul Kashem only and the same is not binding upon him to the exclusion of others. 

 7. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit on contest against defendant Nos. 52, 56, 107 and 26 with costs and against the defendant Nos. 120, 121, 127, 10-30 on contest without costs and ex parte against rest declaring that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 (18/56) dated 6-12-1958 as fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The appeal was dismissed but the High Court Division while maintaining the same found that as Abul Kashem Hawlader was not present in the country during the pendency of the previous suit and the miscellaneous proceeding thereto and hence the impugned judgment and decree is not binding upon him as the same was fraudulently obtained. 

 8. A decree in a suit declaring that the decree is passed in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 dated 6-12-1958 is fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff is not a devisable one and, as such, aforesaid finding of the High Court Division is unwarranted because the decree against other plaintiffs that has been maintained was opposed to law. 

 9. In that view of the matter, the impugned judgment is not sustainable and that the suit is accordingly, decreed on modification declaring the impugned decree passed in Title Suit No. 49 of 1958 on 6-12-1958 as fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

full_judgment:
2. The decree Execution caseNo.1 of 1996 arises out of Civil Petition for leave to appeal no.505 of 1993 and their Lordships of Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh dismissed the appeal on 16.6.1994 thereby affirmed the judgment and decree of the Hon'ble High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh on an Appeal from Appellate Decree No.929 of 1994, allowed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 12.8.1993 and thereby setting aside judgment and decree dated 30.11.1962 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Additional Court of Zilla Khulna passed in Title Appeal No.246 of 1960 reversing the judgment and decree dated 24.8;1960 in Title Suit No.143 of 1952, passed by the learned Munsiff, 2nd Court Bagerhat and the instant Decree Execution Case No.1 of 1995. 

 7. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas with Mr. Sadananda Rana the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the judgment debtor petitioners submit that the original title being No.143 of 1952 was filed for declaration and recovery of possession measuring an area of 55 Bighas of land and it was decreed but the decree holder opposite party nos:l-15 claimed excess land in the decreetal boundary after accretion upto the river totaling to land measuring 125 Bighas of land which is not the part of the decree and the court has gone beyond the original quantum of decreetal land in execution case which caused miscarriage of justice and further submits that he has no objection if an advocate Commissioner is appointed to locate the said 55 decimals of land as per decree of the trial court and it handed over to the Decree holder within Specified date. 

 9. Be that as it may the judgment and decree holder opposite parties are entitled to have the decree execution as obtained in title suit No.143 of 1952 and an execution proceeding seems to be obstructed on the ground that the excess land is going to be handed over. It seems that before filing of this present application the judgment debtor has also preferred similar application before this court which went up to Appellate Division and that was rejected. Therefore under this circumstances the application alleging that excess land is going to be delivered is just a decree to make delay in executing and delivering the possession of the decreetal land. Therefore the executing court must not make further delay in delivery of possession in respect of decreetal land by appointing an Advocate Commissioner after demarcating the boundary in respect of 55 Bighas of land as per schedule within one month from the date of receipt of this order. Accordingly this rule is discharged without any order as to costs.
