caseno: Appeal From Original Decree No. 200 of 1996
parties:
Md Monir Hossain and others
Vs.
Md Shamsul Hoque Mondal and others
full_judgment:
Md. Abdus Salam, J: This appeal at the instance of defendant-appellants is directed against the impugned judgment and decree passed by Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenidah in Title Suit No. 75 of 1994 mainly on the grounds, among others, that in view of the fact and finding of the Subordinate Judge that the power of attorney in question does not contain the counter signature of the Deputy High Commissioner of Pakistan in Calcutta, the said power of attorney allegedly executed by Shyamapada and others in favour of Shahid Dhabak and Ahar Ali is of doubtful origin; that the Subordinate Judge committed error of law by placing the onus of proving the genuineness and regularity of the auction sale upon the defendant' in utter disregard of the provisions of section 114(E) of the Evidence Act which provides for presumption of regularity and legality of all official acts; that the Court below erred in law in not holding that the auction purchaser purchased the suit property before the alleged exchange and took delivery of possession through Court which is proved by the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession; that the Subordinate Judge illegally embarked upon an investigation as to the possession of each plot of land without considering that the writ of delivery of possession followed the kabala deed of the defendant and sufficiently proves possession of the plaintiff in the suit land; that Shaheed Dhabak and Ahar Ali did not come forward before that Court to support the case of the plaintiff in view of the alleged exchange of the suit property and the Court below committed error of law in relying upon the false and concocted story of the plaintiffs that the heirs of Shaheed Dhabak possessed plot Nos. 1209, 668, 669, 677, 678, 678, 655 and 682 as their homestead and that after the death of Ahar Ali his heirs plaintiff Nos. 2-6 have been possessing the khaw schedule land through borgader, even though no borgader came forward to depose in support of this claim and that the Subordinate Judge illegally held that the order dated 25.3.1981 passed by Revenue Authority in Miscellaneous Case No.165/IP/69/70 is not binding upon the plaintiff though the competent authority found upon enquiry that the alleged exchange of the plaintiff and the disputed power of attorney are fake and forged. 

 2. Plaintiff-respondents Shamsul Huq Mondal and others filed Title Suit No. 80 of 1993 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah for declaration of title in the suit  land described in schedule 'Kaw' on the basis of power of attorney described in 'schedule 'Gaw'. 

 3. Defendant No. 1, 3-40 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement date 11.6.95, though the written statement and the verification are signed by only defendant No. 1 Md. Monirul Islam. Defendant No. 45 Deputy Commissioner, Jhenidah on behalf of the Government of Bangladesh did not file any written statement and did not contest the suit. The contesting defendants denied all the material allegations made in the plaint and contended that the suit is not maintainable in its present from and it is barred by limitation and also by constructive resjudicata. It is further contended that the disputed. Ammokternama dated 26.9.62 is not authenticated by any competent Notary Public and not counter-signed by the then Deputy High Commissioner of Pakistan in Calcutta. It is the specific case of the contesting defendant that the suit property was sold by auction in Certificate Case No. 21851/61-62, 21852/61-62 and Certificate Case No. 21853/61-62 and one Amir Hossain and 32 others auction purchased the suit land and they obtained decree in Title Suit No. 223 of 1984 in the Court of Assistant Judge of Mohespur Upazila and the auction purchasers subsequently sold some of the auction purchased land to defendant Nos. 1-40 by Kabala deeds and that the auction purchasers took possession of the land through Court and that the alleged power of attorney and other connected papers of the plaintiff respondents arc forged, fraudulent and not acted upon and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenidah Begum Kabita Khanum conducted trial, examined evidence of both the sides and believed the genuineness of the disputed power of attorney, discussed the law points involved therein and ultimately decreed the suit on contest and declared title of the plaintiff-respondents in the suit land by the impugned judgment dated 4.6.96 and the decree signed on 11.6.96. Thereafter this appeal was preferred by the defendant-appellants. 

 8. We have examined the evidence on record. The original title Suit No. 80 of 1993 was renumbered as Title Suit No. 75 of 1994 by order No. 8 dated 16.7.94 in the 2nd Court Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah. Ext. 1 is the khas Ammokternama in 5 sheets admitted into evidence without any objection. Ext. 1(A) is the disputed power of attorney dated 26.9.62 also admitted into evidence without raising any objection by the defendant appellants at the time of trail. In view of the case law reported in 22 D.L.R. page 858 Sadequr Rahman Chowdhury Vs. Mvi. Abdul Bari, the defendant appellants cannot raise any objection at the time of appeal hearing regarding the disputed power of attorney when the contesting defendants raised no objection against the same disputed power of attorney dated 26.9.62 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah when it was admitted into evidence and marked Ext. 1(A). Moreover, the disputed power of attorney is authenticated by the Deputy Commissioner, Jessore with a certificate that the general power of attorney has been duly stamped and the power of attorney is attested by A.B. Mokherjee Notary Public, Calcutta and counter signed by the then Deputy High Commissioner of Pakistan in Calcutta and it bears the official seal of the Deputy High Commissioner. The Subordinate Judge, Jhenidah rightly observed in the impugned judgment that the presumptive value under section 85 of the Evidence Act is applicable to this disputed power of attorney. The disputed power of attorney was executed on 26.9.62. The East Pakistan Disturbed Persons (Rehabilitation) Ordinance No. 1/1964 was made effective from 30th June, 1964, hence the legal bar mentioned in section 4 and section 6 of Ordinance No. 1 of 1964 is not applicable to the instant power of attorney dated 26.9.62 marked Ext. 1 (A). In this connection the trial Court rightly cited a case law reported in 17 D.L.R. page 451, Chitta Ranjan Sutar Vs. Secretary, Judicial Department, Government of East Pakistan that section 4 and 6 of the Ordinance No. 1 of 1964 place unreasonable restrictions on the right of a citizen to acquire property and the same is violative of the fundamental right 13th and as such they are void and are also discriminatory under Fundamental right 15th. 

 9. In schedule kaw the total area of the suit land has been shown as 21.4.03 acres and this area has been restated as 21.4.03 acres in the valuation statement at the end of the plaint. The Subordinate Judge discussed the documentary and oral evidence on record and came to the finding and decisions that the disputed power of attorney Ext. 1(A) and exchange of the suit property are genuine and the trial Court believed the case of the plain-tiff-respondent and recorded proper reasoning’s in support of its findings and decisions and the trial court decreed the suit in full and declared title of the plaintiff-respondents in the suit property by the impugned judgment and decree; but in page 15 of the original judgment and in the paragraph just before the order portion of the judgment the Subordinate Judge recorded the area of the suit property as 294.58 acres. This area does not correspondent to the total area of the suit property shown in the plaint, schedule kaw and in the valuation statement. Moreover, the total area of the suit property has been shown as 214.03 acres in the decree signed 11.6.96. Hence it is apparent that the area of the suit land has been wrongly typed as 294.58 acres at page 15 of the original judgment. 

 11. In the light of our findings and observations made above in the body of the judgment we do not find any error of law and of fact in the impugned judgment and decree delivered by subordinate Judge, 2nd  Court, Jehnidah in Title Suit No. 75 of 1994. Hence, we do not find any merit in this appeal. The area of the suit property will be 214.03 acres as per plaint and the impugned decree. Only on this point the impugned judgment dated 4.6.96 is modified with 214.03 acres as area of the suit property. The trial Court rightly observed that the Govt. and the relevant Revenue Authority may acquire excess of land excluding 100 bighas after payment of proper compensation to the owner. 

 13. Send down the original case records at once with a copy of this judgment to the learned District Judge, Jhenidah and Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenidah for taking necessary action accordingly.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1158 of 1998
parties:
Akhter Hossain (Md) alias Akhter & others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Shamsuddin Moulvi @ Md Shamsul Huq and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. In a suit for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from interfering with their possession the plaintiffs filed the suit stating, inter alia, that one Fariduddin Ahmed was the owner of 4.07 decimals of land of CS Khatian No. 5 of Mouza Shibrampur who sold the land by different Kabalas dated 15-3-1967 to Nazimuddin Maju Mia, Kashem Mia, Nabi Hossain and Khoda Baksh who were cousins and non-Bengali. During the liberation war of 1971 they were killed. Maju Mia died leaving 3 sons in plaintiff Nos. 1-3, widow in plaintiff No. 4 and daughter in plaintiff No. 5 as his heirs. Kashem Mia died leaving only one son, the proforma defendant No. 6 Mujahid, as his heir. Nabi Hossain, Naimuddin and Khoda Baksh died without any heir. They were all killed during the liberation war of 1971. In this way the plaintiffs and proforma defendant No. 6 Mujahid became the owners by way of inheritance and they are in possession of the suit land along with other lands. The defendants have no title and interest in the suit land and during the liberation war of 1971 the plaintiffs fled away elsewhere and taking this advantage the defendants got the possession of the original title deeds and other papers and created a forged deed in respect of the suit land showing Khoda Baksh as executant of the same. The defendants on the basis of this forged document tried to enter into the suit land on 10-5-1984 and hence the suit for permanent injunction. 

 3. Respondent-defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit denying the allegations in the plaint stating, inter alia, that Khoda Baksh is still alive and that he was in Dhaka during the period from 1971 to 1975 and during this time he did not visit Dinajpur. Taking this advantage Pashir Mohammad and Shohrab of Shiprampur used to possess the suit land illegally and Khoda Baksh came to Dinajpur in the month of April 1976 and recovered the possession of the suit land from Pashir Mohammad and Shohrab. Thereafter Khoda Baksh gave borga of the suit land to Mansur Ali and then returned to Dhaka. Khoda Baksh used to collect the borga money of the suit land from Mansur Ali after coming to Dinajpur. Khoda Baksh subsequently transferred the suit land to Harun-or-Rashid, the son-in-law of defendant No. 1 for a consideration of Taka 12,000 by kabala dated 30-1-1984 and Harun-or-Rashid has been in possession of the suit land through the defendant No. 1 on payment of rent to the Government. Khoda Baksh has his children and that the plaintiffs are not his heirs. Khoda Baksh and Maju Mia are not full brothers. The plaintiffs have no title and possession over the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division erred in discharging the Rule without coming to a finding as regards possession of the suit land in a suit for permanent injunction inasmuch as no complicated question of title is involved in the suit. 

 6. On perusal of the impugned judgment of the High Court Division it appears that the High Court Division found that the Additional District Judge by elaborate discussion of evidence of PWs 1-5 arrived at a finding of fact that the witnesses did not know the suit land and they are also not competent witnesses to prove the factum of possession over the suit land. In view of the claim of title by Harun-or-Rashid from Khoda Baksh by way of purchase by kabala dated 30-1-1984 the Court of appeal below has also disbelieved PWs who contradicted each other as to the existence of sub-plots over the suit land as they did not know the suit land. The Court of appeal below has also found that in the circumstances and findings in the case the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief in this suit for permanent injunction in which the question of title is involved and the plaintiffs as well have failed to prove their possession over the suit land. The finding of fact arrived at by the final Court of fact being based on evidence on record and appreciation thereof could not be assailed before the High Court Division and accordingly, the High Court Division did not find any error of law in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 7. The suit for permanent injunction is essentially a suit for possession. Though the title may be incidentally gone into but in a suit for permanent injunction the Court need not enter into disputed question of title except to the extent as it would help in finding which of the parties have possession. The plaintiff could not bring home their possession in the suit land for a decree for a permanent injunction.

Vs.
Md. Nurul Hoque and others
full_judgment:
Gour Gopal Saha, J: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 14.6.1995 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal No. 285 of 1992 reversing the judgment and decree dated 12.5.1992 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali in Title Suit No. 403 of 1987 sending back the case on remand to trial court. 

 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit in the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali being Title Suit No. 403 of 1987, against opposite parties No. 3-9 for declaration of title in the suit land measuring 1.08 acres described in the schedule of the plaint stating inter alia that Ram Kanai Shil, grand father of the petitioner was the original owner of the suit land by way of settlement from the Zaminder on executing kabuliayt in 1322 B.S. and since then he has been owning and possessing the same on payment of rent to the landlords and living there with the member of his family after constructing dwelling huts therein. It has been alleged that the M.R.R. khatian has been wrongly prepared in the names of the defendants and hence the suit for declaration of title for removing the cloud cast over their title. 

 3. Defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material allegations of the plaint and contended inter alia that the suit as framed is not maintainable in law and it is barred by limitation. It has been contended that the suit land has been rightly recorded in the M.R.R. Khatian in the names of the defendants who own and possess the same in their own right. The plaintiff has no right, title and possession in the suit and the plaintiff filed the suit against the defendants on false and frivolous allegations for illegal gains. 

 5. The plaintiff-petitioner contested the Miscellaneous case by filing written objection denying all its material allegations contending inter alia that the summons was duly served upon the defendant and there is no illegality in the impugned judgment and decree. Miscellaneous Case No. 65 of 1992 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Civil Procedure was ultimately dismissed on 2.11.1992 but defendant No. 1 did not take any further step against the aforesaid order of dismissal before any superior Court as a result of which the ex-part decree passed on 12.5.92 got confirmed. Thereafter the 2 strangers named Nurul Hoque and Mohammad Rafiqullah, who were never parties in the suit filed Title Appeal No. 285 of 1992 before the District Judge, Noakhali against the aforesaid exparte decree dated 12.5.1992 made in Title Suit No. 402 of 1997 contending inter alias that respondent No. 2 Biplab Kumar Shil during his minority inherited the suit property along with others. On attaining majority he transferred 3’15 1⁄2 acres of land, including a portion of the homestead, to them by a registered Kabala dated 26.5.1992 and 

 8. Mr. Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, placed before me the impugned judgment. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge passed the impugned order of remand essentially on the ground of avoiding multiplicity of litigations between the parties. In view of fact that opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 were not parties in the original Title Suit No. 403 of 1987, nor they were parties in Miscellaneous case No. 65 of 1992 under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure there cannot be any justification for sending back the case on remand to the trial Court to give unwanted opportunity to opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 in the name of avoiding multiplicity of suits. The learned Subordinate Judge did not find any illegality or legal infirmity in the impugned judgment passed by the learned trial Court providing justifiable ground for setting it aside. 

 11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and decree dated 14.6.95 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali in Title Appeal no. 285 of 1992 sending the case back on remand to the trial Court on reversing the judgment and decree dated 12.5.92 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Noakhali in Title Suit No. 403 of 1987 are set aside and the decree passed in Title Suit No. 403 of 1987 is hereby maintained.

full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J:- This appeal by leave by defendant No. 2- Government is against the judgment and order dated 27.4.94 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division allowing Appeal from Original Decree No.23 of 1990 thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 23.9.87 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 118 of 1985, in a suit for specific performance of contract. 

 2. Respondent No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 632 of 1982 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate judge, Dhaka impleading the appellant as defendant No.2 praying for a decree for specific performance of contract against defendant No. 1, who is respondent No. 2 in. this appeal alleging that Syed Abdul Hadi was the original owner of the suit property at G/31, Zakir Hossain Road, Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka from whom defendant No. 1. Mahmood Alam purchased the property by a registered deed of sale dated 14-12-62.  The plaintiff-respondent contracted to purchase the property by a deed of agreement for sale from Mahmood Alam 27-1 -71 for a consideration Of 'II. 80,000/- out of which Tk. 20,000/- was paid on the date of agreement as earnest money. Subsequently on 12-12-72, 9-11-74 and 9-12-79 Mahmood Alam took Tk. 20,000/- Tk. 10,000/- and Tk. 10,000/- respectively endorsing receipts thereof on the back page of the agreement. The suit property was listed as an abandoned property and one  Abdul Wahed (defendant No. 4) took allotment thereof Subsequently the Government released the property and directed Abdul Wahed to vacate the same. The plaintiff was confirmed on 1-10-82 that Mahmood Alam would not voluntarily execute and register a sale deed in her favour on receipt of the balance consideration money of Tk. 20,000/-. Hence the suit. 

 6, The High Court Division admitted an application under Order 41 Rule 27 C. P. C. filed by the plaintiff before the High Court Division. The learned Judges admitted in evidence Mahmood Alam's sale deed from the original owner Syed Abdul Hadi and marked it as Ext. 1 being an old document of 30 years. The payment of rent by dakhilas were marked as Exts. 2-8. One Md. Tomiz was examined by the High Court Division as P. W. 2 who allegedly proved the deed of agreement between the plaintiff and Mahmood Alam dated 27-1-71 and it was marked as Ext. 9. 

 7. The learned Judges of the High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record and the application for additional evidence found that the Government released the suit property from the list of abandoned property under Article 15 of P.O.  No. 16 of 1972 and also found that the, deed of agreement stands proved by P. W. 2 who was an attesting witness to the said deed and who apart from proving his signature therein also stated that the executants (Mahmood Alam) put his signature in his presence and that he knew his signature. The High Court Division found that the original title deed of Syed Abdul Hadi, Ext. 1 and the original allotment letter dated 1-1-60 in favour of Syed Abdul Hadi were corning from the custody of the plaintiff and taking these relevant facts into consideration it allowed the appeal and decreed the suit with a direction to defendant No.4 to vacate the suit property.

These Rules at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner is directed against an order passed by Assistant Judge, Beanibazar Upazila on 8-2-88 in Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 1986 rejecting the application under Order 5 rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the original Title Suit No. 265 of 1972 and also the order dated 7-4-88 rejecting the application under section 151 of the Code for restoration of the Miscellaneous Case after setting aside the order dated 8-2-88.
