full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 8-8-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 571 of 2001 in affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 218 of 1991 decreeing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the predecessor-in-interest of the present petitioners No. 1(a)-1(f) one MA Sattar Bhuiyan as plaintiff instituted the original Title Suit being No. 218 of 1991 in the 2nd Court of the learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka for perpetual injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiff in owning and possessing the suit land and also from evicting the plaintiff therefrom, contending inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands originally belonged to one Kadam Mia, Kuran Mia, Nur Khatun, Abdul Malek, Asia Khatun and Amode Ali. One Mazaharul Hoque and others purchased the said land from them by a registered sub-kabala in the year 1965. Thereafter, Mazaharul Hoque and others mutated their names, and obtained separate khatian and used to possess the suit property by payment of rent to the government sheresta regularly. The RS khatian was accordingly prepared in the name of Mazaharul Hoque and others. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that Mazaharul Hoque and others for demarcation of their purchased land filed an application before the then Circle Officer (Rev), Savar on the basis of which a demarcation Case being No. 21/1981-82 was started and upon field measurement the applicants got their purchased land demarcated with specific boundaries. Thereafter, Mazaharul Hoque and others transferred 3.51 acres of land by several transferred deeds in favour of the plaintiff and the number of transfer deeds were thirteen of the year 1990 and since then the plaintiff has possessed the suit property. After purchase, the plaintiff mutated his name in respect of his purchased land and paid rent regularly. The plaintiff has been possessing the suit property by plantation of various trees and growing crops therefrom. While the plaintiff had been owning and possessing the suit property peacefully, the defendant No.1 to the original suit demanded bribe from the plaintiff on different pretext and being refused, the defendant No. 1 threatened the plaintiff with the help of some riotous people. On 25-6-1991 the defendant No.1 along with some terrorist resisted the work of the plaintiff's people on the suit property and they damaged some tree and tried to evict the plaintiff from the said land which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit for permanent injunction. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant-petitioner and others who contested the suit by filing written statement in short is thus that the case of the plaintiff is false, fabricated and mala fide. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiff knowing fully well that the suit property is an abandoned property since 1971 prayed before the Ministry of Agriculture for release of the said property from the list of abandoned property. The Ministry of Agriculture after consultation with the connected papers rejected the prayer of the plaintiff. Subsequently, the local Tahshilder in collusion with the plaintiff illegally released the suit property from the list of abandoned property. The plaintiff also by some illegal influence and exercising undue pressure obtained mutation in respect of the suit property and while it has come to the notice of the government, the government's concerned high official cancelled the mutation order and a proceedings was started in the Anti-corruption Department against that Tahshilder and related Circle Officer. The further case of the defendants in a nutshell is such that the suit property is originally belonged to non-Bengali people who after the independence of Bangladesh left this country for Pakistan leaving the suit property along with their other lands measuring an area of 14.27 acres and accordingly the suit land along with other lands of the aforesaid non-Bengali people has been declared abandoned property and have been enlisted as abandoned property. In the said suit property a project of 'mushroom' cultivation has been started and some hybrid fruit plants also have been planted thereon; by the concerned government machinery and besides this; a high quality training course have been going on there to train up the workers of the government and non-government nursery. One and half crores taka has been invested in the said project. The further case of the government is such that one Anisur Rahman Saju in collusion with some officials of revenue department tried to grab 2.65 acres of land out of 14.27 acres of land and for that reason a case under Anti-corruption Department has been started against that person, in which charge-sheet has already been submitted which is pending for disposal. That the plaintiff along with 250 others armed persons on 25-6-1991 tried to possess the suit property forcibly which is 'Sobhanbag Uddyan Base', but failed at the resistance of the local people and police force. A police case being Savar Police Station Case No. 21 dated 25-6-1991 has been started on that incident. That the plaintiff has got no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land, rather; the defendants have been owning and possessing the suit property for the last 24 years. 

 4. During trial of the original suit the learned trial court after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest by the judgment and order dated 17-10-2001. Being aggrieved the defendant No. 2 i.e. the present petitioner preferred a Title Appeal being No. 571 of 2001 in the court of learned District Judge, Dhaka which was transmitted to the 5th Court of learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka for hearing and disposal and the learned appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 8-8-2004 disallowed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 7. The learned Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-petitioner submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Attorney-General further submits that the judgment and decree passed by the learned courts below is perverse in the eye of law, which is based on misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Deputy Attorney-General (herein after DAG) in his submission submits that the trial court as well as the appellate court were totally misconceived in ignoring that the disputed property is out and out an abandoned property and the government by operation of law has been enlisted the property as abandoned in the year 1972 when the original owners who were non-Bengali people in origin/nationality migrated to Pakistan leaving behind this country, the People's Republic of Bangladesh after its independence. The learned DAG also submits that the papers produced from the side of the plaintiffs are collusive, forged and were not acted upon and that the learned courts below failed to appreciate the actual proposition of law and factual aspects of the case and there has been total non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. That the suit properties is under exclusive possession and control of the government and the government by the concerned Agriculture Department is owning and possessing the suit property which is commonly known as "Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Base". The learned DAG after producing some official documents through supplementary affidavit submits that some important information supported by official papers which are very much essential for disposal of the matter, has been dropped out at the time of filing of the civil revision, which is unintentional and beyond the knowledge of the concerned persons who placed the matter in favour of the petitioners. The learned DAG with regard to this argued that, for proper adjudication into the matter-in-dispute and for ends of justice; all these papers and official documents are very much necessary for consideration of this Court to arrive at a correct decision as to the matter of adjudication between the parties. With regard to this, the learned DAG argued that the property-in-dispute is absolutely an abandoned property and admitting that fact the plaintiff applied before the Secretary concerned of the government for releasing the suit property from the abandoned property's list on 12-11-1990 which has already been exhibited as Exhibit-'Gha' as per Abandoned Property Case No. 02 of 1972 and concerned file which has been lying with the Anti-corruption Department in connection with Kotwali Police Station Case No. 6(3) 87 and that was earlier ceased and the defendant's witness No. 1 in his deposition has mentioned about this. The photocopy of that document (official) was not considered by the trial court, and the same has been kept with the record. The learned DAG argued that after promulgation of the President's Order No. 16/1972, the suit property has been vested in the government under the Abandoned Property (land building and any other property) Rules, 1972 vide Notification dated 8-5-1972 and after that, the concerned Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar (North), Dhaka by his office Memo No. 2404(4) Rev/73 dated 19-5-1973 issued a letter to the Circle Officer (Rev), Savar, Dhaka for handing over charge of the abandoned property of Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery at Savar. The photocopy of the aforesaid memo has been annexed with the supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioner marked as Annexure-'A'. The learned DAG also submits that the concerned Circle Officer (Rev), Savar by his office Memo No. 823/2 dated 30-5-1973 issued a letter to the Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar, (North), Dhaka regarding handing over the possession of "Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery, Savar and its photocopy has been marked as Annexure-'B', and earlier to that, the District Agricultural Officer vide his office Memo No. 912/1(5) dated 11-4-1973 issued a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for handing over the charge of Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery and the Circle Officer (Rev), Savar also issued a letter to the Deputy Commissioner vide his office Memo No. 409/1(6)-SA dated 19-4-1973 for handing over the possession of Sobhan Bagh Horticulture Nursery of Savar and the Photostat copy of the aforesaid letters are marked herewith as Annexure-'C' and 'C-1'. Another letter relating to the handing over of possession issued by the Circle Officer (Rev), Savar vide Memo No. 696/1(3)-SA dated 16.05.1973 in favour of Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar (north), Dhaka is also annexed with the supplementary affidavit marked as Annexure-'D'. The learned DAG during his submission also submits that the all papers relating to mutations of the plaintiff including the DCR and other rent receipts in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party has been cancelled by the concerned authority viz. AC (land) Savar vide his office Memo No. 86 dated 19-2-1998 and there is no record yet has been prepared in favour of the plaintiff and the earlier office order vide Memo No. 86 dated 19-2-1998 is in force till today vide Annexure-'E' and during the present settlement operation the connected B.S. record of the disputed land has been prepared in the name of the government and that record is still in existence. The leaned DAG further submits that, all these papers go to show that the government is possessing the disputed property and the copies of the connected BS khatians are annexed with the supplementary affidavit marked as Annexure-'F' series and the suit property was duly handed over by the connected Tahsildar, Bagdunia Tahshil Office, Savar preparing the lists of articles in favour of the agriculture department, Ministry of Agriculture and the lists of articles are also annexed with the supplementary affidavit marked as Annexure-'G' series and in this way the government is possessing the suit property through Agriculture Department as abandoned property and the Agriculture Department paid the lease money to the government by taking the DCR. The photocopies of the DCRs showing payment of lease money has been marked as Annexure-'H' series. The learned DAG also submits that the vendors of the plaintiff-opposite party were not the Bangladeshi nationals and, as such, they had no legal right to enter into any agreement, sale or execution of a document of transfer in favour of the plaintiff or his predecessor-vendors. The list of abandoned property has been marked as Annexure-'I'. The learned DAG argued that the vendors of the deeds in favour of the plaintiff since were not Bangladeshi citizens, their whereabouts are not known after the war of liberation in the year 1971, and after independence of Bangladesh their names are not included in the voter lists. In support of the aforesaid contention the learned DAG has pointed out the voter lists of the year 1976 which is marked as Annexure-'J'. The learned DAG lastly submits that, all these papers which are purely official makes it clear that the title documents in favour of the plaintiff as alleged are all created spurious papers which have got no legal effect or force to substantiate the prima-facie title and possession of the plaintiff and the so called clearance certificate issued by the Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar, Dhaka in favour of the plaintiff is also a created spurious paper which is forged and not acted upon, inasmuch as; at the relevant time under the government of Bangladesh there was no such officer/office in the name of Sub-divisional Officer, Sadar, Dhaka. The learned Deputy Attorney-General with regard to this, has drawn my attention during his submission that under the District of Dhaka, from the official documents it is apparent that the office of the Concerned SDO was designated in the name of SDO, Sadar (North), Dhaka and in support of this; the learned DAG produce some corresponding letters and documents of the concerned office which has been marked as Annexure-'K'. In support of the contention given by the learned DAG, he has cited some decisions of our Apex Court and the learned Attorney-General with regard to the respective contention of the government and the grounds of the revisional application in his submission specifically argued that the suit as instituted by the plaintiff was not at all maintainable under the purview of section 54 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 since the plaintiff to the suit during trial has hopelessly failed to discharge his onus in proving that he has prima-facie title and exclusive possession in the disputed property, but the learned courts below totally overlooked the said legal aspect of the case and thereby committed gross illegality in deciding the merit of the suit as well as the appeal, which deserve interference of this Court. The learned Attorney-General further submits that the papers produced from the custody of the government inasmuch as; are all official documents; these have a presumption of correctness under the ambit of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872 and the papers which has been submitted along with the supplementary affidavit requires consideration of this Court under the ambit of law as this Court is quite empowered to look into these papers which has falsified the pleading's case of the plaintiff and has enable the court to arrive at a correct decision. The leaned Attorney-General Mr Alom in this regard, has referred some decisions of our Apex Court and lastly submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during passing the judgment and decree since committed gross illegality and not evaluated the evidence on records in its true perspective and not considered the material facts, causing an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in the eye of law and, as such, the Rule has got every merit to succeed. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Attorney-General and the learned Deputy Attorney-General in support of the case of the government, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that, both the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or infirmity, rather; in deciding the fate of the plaintiff's case the courts below rightly assessed the evidence on record and also considered the factual aspects of the, case. The learned Advocate after submitting a counter affidavit on behalf of the opposite parties further submits that the plaintiff to the suit has successfully proved his case by adducing sufficient evidence that in the suit property the plaintiff have prima-facie title and exclusive possession, but the defendants having no manner of right, title, interest and possession therein, illegally threatened the possession of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate also submits that the courts below in their observation and findings rightly arrived at a decision that the property-in-dispute is not an abandoned property or the defendants have no authentic paper to substantiate their claim that the property is abandoned property, and scrutinizing the documentary as well as oral evidence, both the trial and appellate court below concurrently found that the present Opposite parties have title and exclusive possession in the suit land and accordingly decreed the suit and dismissed the appeal, both on contest, respectively. It is submitted by the learned counsel of the opposite parties that the suit property has never been included in the list of abandoned property or published in any official gazette and the petitioners as defendants could never produce any such document to support their claim and that the concerned authority did not serve any notice as per the requirement under Article 7 of the President's Order (PO) No. 16 of 1972 and never took possession of the suit land, which also depicts from the cross-examination of the Defendant's witnesses but the case of the plaintiff that the vendors of the plaintiff purchased the suit property from the S.A. recorded tenants Madan Mia, Kadam Mia and others (Exhibit-7 series) and accordingly they got delivery of possession, and their names were mutated and they paid rent, is proved and that the plaintiff could prove that the vendors of the plaintiff were the owners of the suit land in whose names RS Khatian No.10 and 104 Exibit-7(gha) and 7(umo) were prepared and that they never left this country for Pakistan and they got the suit land demarcated vide সীমানা নির্ধারণী কেইস নং-২১/১৯৮১-৮২ (Exhibit-5), filed in the office of the Revenue Officer, Savar, Dhaka and the Sub Divisional Officer, Dacca Sadar, Dacca vide Memo No. 39 VP Dated 11-1-1982 in reference to AP Clearance Case No. 1/82 (Savar) Issued a Clearance Certificate for mutation of name (Exhibit-8) and that the suit property had not been enlisted or leased out as abandoned property. The leaned Advocate lastly submits that the plaintiff by 13 Kabala Deeds purchased the suit property in 1990 from the RS recorded tenants and accordingly got delivery of possession and also got his name mutated and paid rents (Exhibit-3 series) and when the Defendant No. 1, an officer attached to the Government Sobhanbag Horticulture Centre, Savar tried to extort some illegal gains dishonestly from the plaintiff and when the plaintiff refused to be blackmailed, he started creating impediments and hurdles in the way of the plaintiff's possession in the suit property by using the name of the office and that of the Government and ultimately, the plaintiff initially filed a criminal case followed by the instant Civil Suit in which both the courts below held that the cancellation of the mutation in the name if the plaintiff was illegal and during trial all the plaintiff's witnesses corroborated the plaintiff's possession in the suit land, whereas; the case of the defendants as made out in their written statement was proved to be contradictory to the depositions of their witnesses. The learned Advocate submits that the witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiff during trial of the original suit successfully proved the case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff has title and interest including possession over the disputed property and all the witnesses are competent, trustworthy and reliable, and, as such, courts below rightly relied upon the testimonies of the witnesses as examined from the side of the plaintiff and on the contrary, the witnesses adduced from the side of the defendants to substantiate their case, were totally failed to falsify the case of the plaintiff and prove the case of them (defendants), which is considered rightly by the learned trial court as well as the appellate court and there is no illegality or infirmity including misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of the material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate in support of his contention has referred some decisions of our Apex Court and in his concluding argument submits that the concurrent findings and decisions of both the courts below since not based on any illegality or infirmity, there is no reason to discharge the Rule. 

 9. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates, having gone through the connected documents including the judgment and decree passed by the trial court as well as the appellate court and the connected official papers produced from the side of the petitioners annexed with their supplementary affidavit and the documentary evidences adduced from the sides of both the parties, it transpires that in the original suit, the plaintiff under the ambit of section 54 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 prayed for getting a decree of perpetual injunction for restraining the defendants permanently from entering into the disputed property. 

 10. The relevant law of perpetual injunction as provided in section 54 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 contemplates that in appropriate case the court is empowered to pass a decree of perpetual injunction to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in favour of the applicant, whether expressly or by implication and the court shall be guided by the rules and provisions contained in Chapter-II of this Act. Where it is proved that the applicant has prima-facie title and exclusive possession over the land-in-dispute, in that case only, a decree can be awarded. 

 11. The paramount consideration in a suit for permanent injunction is whether the plaintiff has been successful in proving his exclusive possession. Question of title may be looked into incidentally but decision of title in such a suit is not a guiding principle for holding that the suit is not maintainable without a partition suit. In a suit for permanent injunction the court need not enter into a question on disputed title except to the extent that it would help the court in finding which of the parties have prima-facie title and exclusive possession [Ref. Jobayer Hossain vs Noor Hafez, 56 DLR (AD) 22.] In the instant case as I have come-across that the parties to the suit in order to enable the court to find out the prima facie title and exclusive possession have adduced witnesses in support of their pleadings. 

 13. On meticulous consideration of the evidence on records, I find that both the parties to the suit in order to establish their pleading's case have adduced witnesses. Among them, PW 1 is the plaintiff himself MA Sattar Bhuiyan. This witness in his testimony tried to depose in support of his pleading. At a stage of his deposition he has frankly conceded that on the basis of thirteen sub-kabala 'deeds he has acquired title and interest in the disputed property. The plaintiff has failed to state the CS khatian number of the disputed land and also failed specify the boundaries of the disputed property in his deposition. It is the contention of the plaintiff in his testimony that his property (suit land) is being managed by his caretaker who uses to reside therein in a dwelling hut, but in the plaint; there is no mention about the existence of dwelling but of his caretaker. As to the cause of action of the suit, on perusal of the plaint I find that, it is also not mentioned in the plaint that in what date and time the defendant No. 2 and 3 threatened the plaintiff or his caretaker to dispossess from the disputed property. PW 1 has admitted at a state of his testimony that his mutation has been cancelled by the authority and he filed an appeal before the Divisional Commissioner. The plaintiff as PW 1 also testified that he does not know as to whether the Anticorruption Department has started a case against the concerned Circle Officer (Rev) and Tahashilder. In a reply to a question from the side of the defendants PW 1, the plaintiff admits at a stage of his testimony that he could not file any rent receipt showing his payment of rent for the disputed property after the year 1990 AD. 

 25. DW 1 is Saleh Ahmed, who is Upazila Agriculture Officer, Savar. This witness in his deposition testified that the original owners of the suit properties ware one Haji Abdus Sobhan and his relatives, who during the war of liberation left this country for Pakistan and accordingly under PO 16 of 1972 the suit property has become abandoned property. This witness in his testimony testified about the abandoned property case No. 02 of 1972 and with regard to the papers relating to the taking over and making over possession of the suit property by dint of several official correspondences followed by series of papers. This witness also testified in his testimony that the plaintiff to the suit has got no title, interest and possession in the suit property and the collusive demarcation, mutation, payment of rent which was in favour of the plaintiff, has been cancelled by the appropriate authority of the government. DW 1 in his examination-in-chief corroborates the case of the government and proves the papers filed, which has been marked as Exhibits. 

 (3) A temporary lessee under sub-rule (2) of any abandoned land or building shall not acquire any right or occupancy in such land or building and shall not be entitled to hold over after the expiry of the lease. 

 32. It is a decided matter that, if the dispute involves complicated questions of title, the plaintiff must establish his title by filing a regular suit for declaration of title. A simple suit for permanent injunction should not be allowed to be used as a testing device for ascertainment of title. In this case the plaintiff assails the presumption of the Khatian, a kind of exercise the Court in a simple suit for permanent injunction should ordinarily avoid. [Ref. Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215). Apart from this, going through the evidence on records and the papers produced from the side of the government which have got a presumptive value of correctness it reveals that the case of the plaintiff with regard to the prima facie title and possession is not proved by any tangible, cogent and credible evidence, rather; the Plaintiff's witnesses contradicted the case of the plaintiff obviously in their testimonies and the Plaintiff's witnesses No. 02, 05, and 06 practically has admitted the case of the government. 

 33. In the foregoing narrative, I have every reason to inclined such a view that, the reasoning of both the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal are apparently ill founded and the courts below committed gross illegality in evaluating the oral and documentary evidences in its true perspective and also there has been non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal, causing sufficient merit in this revisional application. Accordingly, I find support in the submission advanced from the side of the learned Attorney-General and the Deputy Attorney-General. 

 34. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 8-8-2004 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 571 of 2001 in affirming the judgment and decree dated 17-10-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.218 of 1991 is hereby set aside, and the original suit be dismissed on contest.

parties:
Mosaraf Hossain Dhali and others ------- Defendant-Respondent-Petitioners
Vs
 Khalilur Rahman Bepari and others ------ Plaintiff-Appellant-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite parties No. 1(ka) 12 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006 and 7-9-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 170 of 2002 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those of dated 6-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 101 of 2001 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 101 of 2001 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur against the defendant-respondent-petitioners and others for a declaration of title with a further declaration that the deed in the name of the defendants No. 29-32 is collusive, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs along with a prayer for recovery of khash possession contending inter alia, that the suit properties appertaining to Mouza Ichli under Chandpur Sadar comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land out of 6.97 acres of land originally belonged to one Loknath and others. Subsequently, one Nurul Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and a Sekander Sheikh in 04 annas share obtained settlement from the original owners Loknath and others. During CS operation the suit land went under water and after its appearance from the bad of the river the Ex-Zaminder filed a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 in which the settlement holders Nurul Islam and Sekandar obtained their respective saham. Thereafter, while Nurul Islam and Sekandar failed to pay the rent the Ex-Zamindar started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and in .Rent Execution Case No. 02 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain. Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land by way of 'boynama' on 10-3-1951. The further case of the present petitioners i.e. the plaintiffs is such that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Mohammad Ali and others by a registered sub-kabala deed dated 21-12-1956 became the owner of the suit land. The auction purchaser Zamir Hossain exhausted his share after his transfer. Thereafter, the SA khatian No. 28 was correctly prepared in the name of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land measuring 3.60 acres. The father of the plaintiff had been owning and possessing the land-in-dispute and after his demise the land was inherited by the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs after erecting their homestead in the suit properties use to possess the same and also paying rent to the government regularly. Out of the total land 42 decimals was recorded in the name of the plaintiff during BS operation and 461/2 decimals went into the khash khatian of the government. It is the case of the plaintiff that the suit land is in the khash land of the government but taking advantage of that the defendants No. 29-32 and 33-36 collusively obtained settlement from the government by kabuliyat dated 22-5-2000. On 20-2-2001 all on a sudden the defendants No. 29-32 dispossessed the plaintiffs from the 'kW schedule land forcibly and erected huts therein. The plaintiffs to the suit thereafter learnt about the settlement of the defendants from the government and after getting certified copy of the kabuliyate on 11-6-2001 filed the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants No. 2-32 and 33-36 after filing separate written statements contended that the land measuring 84.00 acres under Mouza Ichuli of SA plot No. 251 is the khash land of the government and BS khatian has been correctly prepared in the name of the government in its khash kahtian No. 1. The defendants being landless persons prayed for settlement of the land from the government and the government being satisfied by way of registered kabuliyat No. 2481 and 2485 granted settlement in favour of the defendants on 22-5-2000. The further case of the contesting defendants is such the plaintiff No. 4 admitting the title of the government in its khash khatian No. 1 took settlement of 25 decimals of land in Settlement Case No. 178/199-2000. The plaintiff No. 4after taking settlement from the government erecting homestead use to possess the same. It is the case of the defendants that the plaintiffs were never dispossessed from the suit properties since they had no possession therein but only to grab the government property on the basis of false allegations and created forged papers filed the original suit. 

 4. The leaned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 6-10-2002. 

 5. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred a Title Suit being No. 170 of 2002 in the Court of learned District Judge, Chandpur which was transmitted to the 1st Court of learned Joint District Judge, Chandpur for hearing and disposal. The learned appellate court hearing the appeal allowed 'the same by the impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned court of appeal below during disposal of the appeal committed illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the impugned judgment and decree is not a proper judgment of reversal in the eye of law as the learned lower appellate court violating the provisions laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure decided the merit of the appeal arbitrarily in favour of the plaintiffs without reversing the findings and decisions of the trial court adverting evidence therein. The learned Advocate also submits that there has been non-reading and misreading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and the impugned judgment and decree was passed by the Appellate Court in a slipshod manner and not applying it's judicial mind. The learned Advocate submits that the Appellate Court not assessed the evidence on records in its true perspective and evaluated the same causing miscarriage of justice. The learned court during taking decision not at all considered all the papers on records properly and the plaintiffs to the suit during trial utterly failed to discharge their onus in proving their respective case. But the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur without taking it into consideration decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and in fact there is no paper showing the existence of the Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 and that the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs namely Nur Islam and Sekandar obtained their respective saham as alleged comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the impugned judgment and decree is highly defective and it is not at all enforceable as it is not a speaking decree. The plaintiffs' original suit was a suit not for declaration of title, but for a declaration that the kabuliyat in favour of the defendants in respect of settlement is collusive, forged and not acted upon along with further prayer of recovery of khash possession. The learned Appellate Court misconceived the matter from the very beginning and, as such, failed to consider that the plaintiffs were totally failed to prove their possession and dispossession in the disputed property by producing tangible evidence. The learned Advocate submits that the learned Lower Appellate Court also failed to appreciate that, among the plaintiffs the plaintiffs No. 4 and 5 admitting the right, title, interest of the government in the suit property took settlement from the government and the conclusive findings with regard to this from the side of the trial court was not reversed by the appellate court adverting evidence on records. The learned Advocate relying upon the provisions laid down in section 115 of the Evidence Act argued that the plaintiffs are stopped from challenging the title of the Government inasmuch as among them some of the plaintiffs admitting the title of the government in its khash khatian No. 1 obtained settlement by kabuliyate. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs to the suit during trial after adducing sufficient evidence proved their case that the original owners of the disputed properties were Loknath and others and from them one Nurul Islam Sheikh and Sekandar Sheikh in 12 annas and 04 annas share took settlement. The learned Advocate also submits that during CS operation although the land-in-dispute went under water but subsequently it was re-appeared by alleviation and the Ex-Zamindar pursuant to a Partition Suit being No. 65 of 1930 gave the land amicably in favour of their settlement holders Nur Islam and Sekandar Sk. and in fact the partition suit was ended in favour of the Plaintiff's-Predecessors Nur Islam and Sekandar. Subsequently, for arrear of rent a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 was started and in Decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the suit land on 10-3-1951 and from that Zamir Hossain; predecessors of the plaintiffs kabala purchased the land-in-dispute. The learned Advocate also submits that the Lower Appellate Court during deciding the merit of the appeal after proper assessment of evidence and appreciation of law allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below. 

 11. On perusal of the case records; it transpires that the positive contention as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs was such that the land-in-dispute originally belonged to ex-Zamindars namely Loknath and others. From them one Nur Islam Sheikh in 12 annas and one Sekandar Sheikh in 04 annas share took settlement. It is an admitted position that during CS operation the land in dispute went under water of the river. With regard to this; it is the contention of the plaintiffs that while the land-in-dispute reappeared from the bad of the river the ex-Zamindar started a "Touzi Bontan" (Partition Suit) Suit being No. 65 of 1930 and in that suit the settlement holder Nur Islam and Sekandar Sheikh obtained their respective saham in respect of the suit properties. The further pleadings of the plaintiffs were such that the Zaminders for arrears of rent started a Rent Suit being No. 350 of 1950 and obtained a decree. In decree Execution Case No. 2 of 1951 one Zamir Hossain Bhuiyan auction purchased the land by way of "Boynama" on 10-3-1951. From that auction purchaser the predecessors of the plaintiffs obtained the suit land. 

 12. Vis-a-vis; it is the plain case of the contesting defendants that they are the landless cultivators and inasmuch as the property-in-dispute is the khash land of the government they prayed for settlement and the government being satisfied on 22-5-2000 by two registered kabuliyats No. 2481 and 2485 granted settlement in favour of the contesting defendants. It was further contended from the side of the defendants in their pleadings that the plaintiffs had no manner of title, possession and interest in the disputed properties and thereby there is no question of dispossession from the side of the defendants as alleged from the side of the Plaintiff-Opposite parties. 

 18. The other possession witness of the plaintiffs PW 3 Ruhul Amin Bepari who happens to be another relative of the plaintiffs testifies at a stage that he cannot say about the original owners of the suit property from whom the plaintiffs acquired the suit land. 

 21. On the other hand the witness No. 1 of the defendants Md Amir Hossain is a Tahsilder, who deposed on behalf of the government and corroborated the case of the defendants. This witness testified about the settlement khatian in favour of the defendants by way of kabuliyats being No. 2481 and 2485. He also submitted the papers relating to the right, title, and interest of the government with regard to khash khatian No. 1 and the settlement khatian in favour of the plaintiff No. 4 and all these papers has been duly exhibited. 

 25. it is a decided matter that under the ambit of sections 101 and 103 of the Evidence Act it is the incumbent duty upon the plaintiffs to the suit to discharge their onus of proof in proving their respective case but in the instant case as I have come across from the evidence on records that the plaintiffs to the suit could not discharge their onus of proof as observed by the learned trial Judge in his judgment and dismissal decree. The learned lower appellate court at the time of passing the impugned judgment and decree without reversing the conclusive findings of the trial court on the title, possession and dispossession as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs reversed the judgment and decree as a whole which is a clear violation of the provision laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Under this provision of law in case of reversal of the trial court's judgment the Appellate Court is under legal obligation in reversing the findings of the trial court and give bona fide reasons for it's decision on the points for determination and shall have to give reasons therein at its own independent findings. The appellate court must contain definite findings on the question involved and must give reason when reversing the material findings of the trial court [Ref: Mohsena vs Habib, 17 BLD (AD) 47, Abu vs Sharifa, 15 BLD (AD) 91, Nur vs Nur 40 DLR (AD) 175, Abdus vs Jonab (Md) 57 DLR (AD) 112, Profulla vs Nagen, 6 BLC (AD) 1301. 

 27. Besides this; the chain of title since not at all proved from the side of the plaintiffs which is badly required and the possession and dispossession as alleged from their side as not proved by tangible evidence the plaintiffs are not entitled the relief as prayed for. 

 29. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 3-9-2006 and 7-9-2006 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chandpur in Title Appeal No. 170 of 2002 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing those of dated 6-10-2002 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Chandpur in Title Suit No. 101 of 2001 is hereby set aside.

parties:
Mrs. Salma Alam Khan.
Vs.
Mahanagar Traders Ltd. Represented by its Chairman Arjumand Ara.
full_judgment:
Kashefa Hussain, J : Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioner against order no.155 dated 13.01.2013 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 arising out of Title Suit No. 07 of 1996 allowing the application of the defendant under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and condoning the delay of 307 days in filing the application. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule in short are that the petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 277 of 1995 which was transferred and subsequently re-numbered as Title Suit No. 07 of 1996. The suit was filed after complying with due procedure and upon hearing ultimately decreed vide judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010. Thereafter, on 08.02.2011 the defendants filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 under order 9 rule 13 of Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010 paying the prescribed mandatory deposit etc. Primarily the defendant alleged that the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010 was an ex-parte order and ought to be set-aside. The PW-1 and DW-1 deposed in the Miscellaneous Case which was allowed by order dated 13.01.2013 along with condonation of delay of 307 days and thus setting aside the judgment and decree dated 30.03.2010 passed by the Trial Court being aggrieved by the order passed in Miscellaneous Case no. 02 of 2011 allowing the application under order 9 rule 13 of Code of Civil Procedure the plaintiff as petitioner preferred this instant Revisional Application and is hence before us. 

 5. On the other hand learned Advocates Mr. Moinuddin on behalf of the defendant opposite party submits that judgment and order dated 30.03.2010 is actually an ex-parte order and defendants were not present on that particular day before the court and had no knowledge that judgment was going to be passed on that day. He persuades that the use of the term “দোতরফা সুত্রে” is only an inadvertent error on the part of the Trial Court and which is evident from the order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 dated 13.01.2013 allowing the application along with condonation of delay of 307 days and also submits that the original Title Suit was filed in the year 1995 and the suit was dragged on for long 15 years mainly due to various delaying tactics resorted to by the plaintiff. He stresses upon the fact that it is evident from the records that the suit was dismissed several times and that it would be eventually restored repeatedly on various pleas of the plaintiff's. He further persuades that lastly when it was taken up for hearing due to some unavoidable circumstances on the part of the learned Advocate for the defendant which was inadvertent and totally unintentional, the defendant otherwise diligent regarding the case however could not be present in court on that day. He alleges that the defendant had no knowledge of the judgment being passed on 30.03.2010 and which they ultimately learnt later, and finally on 24.01.2011 after receiving knowledge of the judgment filed the Miscellaneous Case No. 02 of 2011 on 08.02.2011, In this context he assails that lie filed the case within 30 days of knowledge of the decree in accordance with the statutory rules. 

 11. Taking all the facts and circumstances into consideration, we arrive at our considered finding that the Trial Court vide its Order no.155 dated 13.01.2013 in Miscellaneous Case No.02 of 11 arising out of Title Suit No. 07 of 1996 correctly allowed the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Cpc. , and, therefore, we do not find any merits in this rule.

full_judgment: 3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that on an application of the defendant No.2 the proprietor of defendant No.1 company, the plaintiff bank opened a Letter of Credit No.K.L.N/L.C/CASH/24/1999 for import of 15000 metric tons of wheat. The imported wheat having been shipped, the shipping documents were negotiated by the foreign supplier and the negotiating bank sent the shipping documents to the Bank. As per terms of the said Letter of Credit, the negotiating bank lodged a claim for payment against the negotiated bill with City Bank N.A., the corresponding bank of the Janata Bank and obtained payment of US$ 20,64,871.50 being the value of the import bill from the Bank. The plaintiff Bank after adjusting the Letter of Credit margin deposited by defendant Nos.1 and 2 against the said import bill lodged PAD No.36 of 1999 in the name of the defendant No.1. The plaintiff Bank requested the above defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to retire the said shipping documents on payment of the balance import bill but the defendants did not come forwarded for payment of the same in spite of several reminders. The plaintiff Bank came to know that defendant No.2 in connivance with the authority and the persons concerned managed to take delivery of the said imported goods without retiring the original shipping documents from the Bank and in this way the outstanding in the PAD Account No.36 of 1999 remained unadjusted. The defendant No.2 promised through letters to repay the said loan and on 25.10.2000 the defendant Nos.2-8 executed personal guarantee and undertaking to pay the dues of the loan account of the defendant No.1 and also deposited the original title deeds of some immovable property. Therefore, the said defendants are liable to repay the outstanding dues in the said PAD Account No.36 of 1999. The mortgaged property is liable to be sold for the realization of the outstanding dues of Tk.12,31,80,431.30 as on 30.04.2003. The defendants were served with final notice dated 17.10.2001 and legal notice dated 06.12.2001 through the learned Advocate of the plaintiff Bank but did not respond and thus the plaintiff bank has been compelled to file the suit.

parties:
General Manager, Madaripur Polly Bidhyut Somity Madaripur ----- Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner 
Versos
Md. Moktaruzzaman ----- Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. I to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 09.05.2013 and 16.05.2013 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Madaripur in Title Appeal No.135 of 2011 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 09.06.2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Madaripur Sadar in Title Suit No.131 of 2004 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order of orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus. the opposite party No.1 instituted the original Title Suit No. 131 of 2004 in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Madaripur Sadar for a declaration that the dismissal order passed by the defendants is illegal, null & void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff contending inter-alia that the plaintiff opposite party joined in Madaripur Polly Bidhyut Somity on 29.12.1984 as line man and he was subsequently promoted to the post of Line Technician. During service the plaintiff was transferred to different stations like kalkini, Gopalgonj, Takerhat jonal office etc. under the district of Madaripur and while he was working in-charge of 'Sreenadi, the defendant No.8 Deputy General Manager, Takerhat jonal Office brought some allegations against the plaintiff and charge was issued directing the plaintiff to submit his reply. Accordingly, the plaintiff submitted his reply and an inquiry committee was formed by the opposite party No.4 President, Rural Electrification Somity, Mostafapur, Police Station and District-Madaripur. Thereafter the inquiry committee submitted their report on 23.10.1998. The plaintiff submitted an application for exonerating him from the liability of charge. But the authority by their order dated 03.11.1998 demoted the plaintiff from the post of line technician to the post of line man, gradel with effect from 01.11.1998 and allowed leave of 39 days with effect from 08.09.1998 to 16.10.1998 and also directed the plaintiff to furnish undertaking. Thereafter the plaintiff subrilitted an application for review of the decision before the authority but failed. The further case of the plaintiff is such that on 12.11.1998 the customers under a damaged transformer of “শ্রীনদী অভিযোগ কেন্দ্র” informed the plaintiff pursuant to a complaint No.81 dated 12.11.1998 about the damage of that transformer & getting that complain the plaintiff going to the place of occurrence inquired into the matter. On 19.11.1998 the Deputy General Manager issued a show-cause notice upon the plaintiff on an allegation that the plaintiff has failed to complete his work and also failed to realize the electric bills from the customers. For the illness of the plaintiffs daughter he could not submit his reply in time and the Deputy General Manager on 07.12.1998 while issued another show-cause notice upon the plaintiff, the plaintiff submitted his written reply. Thereafter the defendants again constituting a second inquiry committee directed the plaintiff to appear before the committee. Besides this; Pursuant to a letter dated 09.02.1999 the defendant No.2 bringing some false allegations suspended the plaintiff from his service. The plaintiff was not allowed to look into his personal file and as such he could not take part in the hearing and thus deprived of getting natural justice. The inquiry committee submitted their report without serving the copy of that to the plaintiff for which the plaintiff could not know the contents of the report. The defendant No.4 without issuance of any rd show-cause notice dismissed the plaintiff from service by his order dated 30.08.1999 which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit. 

 4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 09.06.2011. 

 5. Being aggrieved the defendant No.4 General Manager filed an appeal before the learned District Judge, Madaripur being Title Appeal No.135 of 2011. The learned appellate court hearing the appeal disallowed the same affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 09.05.2013 and 16.05.2013 respectively. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that prior to the original suit the plaintiff-opposite party filed a Writ Petition being No.3849 of 1999 in this court and the Writ Petition was dismissed on 12.02.2002. The learned Advocate further submits that against the judgment and order passed the plaintiff preferred a civil petition for leave to appeal being No.1379 of 2002 but that was also dismissed. The learned Advocate further submits that both the courts below misread and misdirected themselves and erred in law in assessing the evidence on record in its true perspective and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Under the proviso of Rule 44 of Polly Bidhyut Service Code, 1992 an employee of the Polly Bidhyut Somity may file an appeal against the action taken after holding of the inquiry but the plaintiff-opposite party without availing the opportunity instituted the suit. The learned Advocate also submits that without exhausting the proper forum available in the Service Rules the suit was filed in wrong forum and the learned courts below without appreciation of law decided the merit of the suit in favour of the plaintiff illegally. Furthermore, the relief claimed by the plaintiff is not adequate. The learned Advocate argued that the trial court during disposal of the original suit relying upon the weakness of the defendant's witnesses decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff without proper sifting of evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiff. From the admission of the plaintiff in his deposition it is apparent that the notice was served duly upon him and the plaintiff submitted his written reply before the authority as well as before the inquiry Committee. The learned Advocate submits that the plaintiff admitting his guilt before the authority submitted an application for exonerating him and without seeking the relief from the Administrative Tribunal; which was the proper court the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration illegally. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the courts below being guided ; by surmise and conjecture passed their judgments and decree on total non-consideration of material facts inasmuch as in the original plaint the plaintiff admitted frankly that notice was duly served on him and after getting that notice he submitted his reply and appeared before the authority for hearing and the allegation of the plaintiff that the members of the Inquiry Committee was not competent to inquire into the matter as admittedly the members of that committee were probationary officers of Madaripur Polly Bidhyut Somity, is mere an irregularity not illegality. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions the teamed Advocate on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the arguments advanced from the side of the petitioner and submits that in passing the impugned judgment and decree no illegality or irregularity was committed and in deciding the fate of the original suit and it's subsequent appeal there was no misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by dint of which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate further submits that the civil court is, quite empowered to enter into the merit of the suit and look into the illegality and propriety of the matter-in-dispute as jurisdiction of the civil court is not barred by any provisions or the mlevant Rules or Laws or the Rural Electrification Board Ordinance, 1977 (LT of 1977). The learned Advocate in support of his contention referred several decisions of this court and our Apex Court and submits that admittedly the defendant petitioner violating Rule 39 (2) of the Service Code, 1992 of "Polly Bidhyut Somity" constituted the final Inquiry Committee and that committee acted beyond their jurisdiction in giving their proposal for punishment. Besides this; that Committee admittedly obtained written statements of the witnesses and the plaintiff was not rendered any opportunity to cross-examine those witnesses. The learned Advocate also submits that the report along with the proposal of the inquiry committee was not legal. A delinquent-employee have a legal right to cross-examine the witness produced before the Inquiry Committee but in the instant case it is the concurrent findings of both the courts below that the plaintiff was deprived of getting an opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses. The procedure adopted by the inquiry committee and the punishment as suggested by the Committee is against the principle of natural justice and against the decided matter of this court. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the Administrative Tribunal had no jurisdiction to look into the matter as the plaintiff is not public servant or was in the service of the Republic. Lastly; the court of appeal being final court of facts is immune from interference in absence of any sort of illegality or infirmity in deciding the fate of the appeal. 

 14. Under the provisions laid down in section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to try all suits of civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred. Hence, the trial court had every jurisdiction to entertain the original suit and thus committed no wrong. With regard to this, our Apex court in the case of Abdul Ralf and others vs. Abdul Hamid Khan and others reported in 17 DLR(SC) 515 held that the civil court have general jurisdiction to ascertain whether the act of the officers was lawful and bonafide. 

 judgment and decree dated 09.05.2013 and 16.05.2013 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Madaripur in Title Appeal No.135 of 2011 dismissing the appeal affirming the judgment and decree dated 09.06.2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge. Madaripur Sadar in Title Suit No. 131 of 2004 is hereby affirmed.

parties:
Md. Abdus Salam and others
Vs.
Md. Abul Hasem Sarder and others
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.10.2012 and 29.10.2012 respectively passed by the learned District Judge, Satkhira in Title Appeal No. 57 of 2012 allowing the appeal in part modifying the judgment and decree dated 14.05.2012 and 20.05.2012 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Satkhira in Title Suit No. 78 of 2006 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the original Title Suit being No. 78 of 2006 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Satkhira Sadar for declaration of title and further declaration that the S.A. record is wrong with an additional prayer of partition contending inter alia, that the suit properties appertaining to C.S. khatian No.771 of Mouza Madhabkhali under P.S. Satkhira originally belonged, to one Enamul Hoque Biswas comprising an area of 54 decimals of land under whom one Bagan Behara Sarder was a korfa tenant and the under khatian was 773. Due to arrear of rent for non-payment of the same by the korfa tenant Bagan Behara the landlord preferred a rent suit and obtained a decree therein. Thereafter, in decree Execution Case No.221 of 1952 the property was auction-purchased by the landlord and subsequently decided to settle with the land. The plaintiff's father namely Madar Sarder at a salami of Taka 50/- and yearly rental of Taka 5/- took settlement of the property. In favour of the landlord Enamul Hoque Biswas Madar Sarder executed a registered kabuliyat in respect of the land on 25.02.1956. Thereafter; Madar Sarder out of the total 54 decimals of land sold out 10½ decimals of land in favour of the defendant No.5 and delivered possession. Subsequently; by another transfer deed dated 31.10.1966 Madar Sarder transferred 8 decimals of land in favour of one Abdul Khaleque who by a subsequent transfer deed dated 17.12.1990 transferred that 8 decimals of land along with other lands in all 27 decimals in favour of the plaintiffs No. 1 and 2. Madar Sarder died leaving behind four sons Abdus Salam Sarder and others, one daughter Anwara Khatun and wife Meherful bibi. In this way the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land by way of inheritance and their purchase deeds. During S.A. operation due to ailing condition of Madar Sarder his brother Nur Mohammad was entrusted responsibility to record the name of Mather Sarder, but Nur Mohammad Sarder the brother of Madar Sarder recorded his name along with, his relations instead of his brother. The defendants threatened the plaintiffs by virtue of that record and denied to effect partition which constrained the plaintiffs to institute the original suit. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant No.5 who is the opposite party No.1 of the revisional application in short is thus that Bagan Behara Sarder was the korfa tenant under the original owner of the suit property Enamul Hoque Biswas. Due to arrears of rent a Rent Suit was filed by the landlord against Bagan Behara and the landlord obtained decree and in Decree Execution Case No.221 of 1952 the property was auction-purchased by the landlord. Thereafter, while the landlord proposed to settle the land, two brothers Madar Sarder and Nur Mohammad Sardar, son of Bagan Behara Sardar decided to take settlement and accordingly settlement was taken from the joint fund of the family and for joint interest of the family members but the kabuliyat dated 25.02.1956 was executed by the elder brother of the family Madar Sarder. The property was possessed in ejmali by two brothers and their mother and accordingly the S.A. record 602 was prepared in their names. At the demise of the brothers the property was devolved upon the heirs of two brothers. In this way the heirs of Madar Studer by way of inheritance acquired 27 decimals of land. During life time by two sets of kabla deeds Madar Sarder transferred 10½ decimals of land in favour the defendant No.5. The remaining brother Nur Mohammad by a registered kabla dated 09.08.1984 transferred his land in favour of the defendant no.5. The story of acquisition of the land by only one brother namely Madar Sarder is false and to deprive the other brother and his mother this was stated within the pleadings of the plaintiffs out of ill motive. The defendant not being the exclusive owner of 48 decimals of land have been owning and possessing that portion of land and the D.P. khatian accordingly prepared in his name. He has mutated his name and paying rent regularly. The plaintiffs on false allegation filed the suit which is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit on contest vide his judgment and decree dated 14.05.2012. Being aggrieved the defendant No.5 preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 57 of 2012 in the court of learned District Judge, Satkhira and the learned lower Appellate Court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.10.2012 allowed the appeal in part. 

 7. The learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not taking the view that the settlement of the suit land in favour of Madar Sarder is genuine and that was for his own interest and money. The learned Advocate further submits that the kabuliyat which was a registered instrument in favour of the landlord was exclusively executed and registered by Madar Sarder and the learned District Judge have failed to appreciate the facts of the case including documentary evidence which is on records. There is nothing on record to hold such a view that the money for taking settlement was obtained from the joint fund of the joint family as alleged from the side of the contesting defendant. As a member of Muslim community there is no provision in the Mohammadan Law that joint family concept can be considered legal and as such the learned District Judge in taking decision over the pertinent point of the suit holding the view that as a member of a joint family for the interest of others Madar Sarder acquired the property is an error apparent on the face of the record. The learned Advocate also submits that the learned lower appellate court in his findings and observation once held that Madar Sarder as a member of joint family on behalf of his brother and mother and for himself obtained the settlement from the landlord and executed the kabuliyat but he has given a contradictory decision that the kabuliyat dated 25.02.1956 is an ineffective document and by this document nothing was accrued in favour of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate submits that, Exhibit-3 is the kabla deed dated 31.10.1966 by which the two brothers namely Madar Sarder and Nur Mohammad Sarder sold land in favour of one Abdul Khaleque. From this kabla deed it appears that Nur Mohammad sold his land not from, the suit khatian but from different khatian and on the other hand Madar Sarder transferred his land from the suit khatian which proves that the settlement was taken by Madar Sarder himself for his own interest in respect of the disputed property. Besides this; the defendant no.1 who is the son of Nur Mohammad after giving evidence proved the case of the plaintiffs in taking settlement by Madar Sarder alone not with his brother Nur Mohammad which is not properly addressed by the learned appellate court below. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the plaintiffs paid rent in respect of the suit property till 1997 and taking advantage of wrong S.A. record the defendants mutated their names illegality and despite the S.A. record is not the document of title, the same is not properly appreciated by the learned appellate court and in this way the appellate court misdirected himself to the contents of Exhibit-3 the kabla deed dated 31.10.1966 and failed to assess other evidence on records in its true perspective. There is non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party opposing the Rule controverted the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners and submits that the learned appellate court below in deciding the fate of the appeal and in passing the impugned judgment and decree committed no illegality or irregularity. There is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. The learned Advocate further submits that the pattern settlement as alleged from the side of the plaintiffs is not proved as genuine and it was not valid inasmuch as it was not completed by giving rent or salami in favour of the landlord. There is no document showing that the landlord accepted rent or salami from the settlement holder and as such the settlement was not completed and thus it does not confer any right, title, interest in favour of anybody. The learned Advocate further submits that under section 57 of the Mohamadan Law there is a concept of joint family which has been reflected within the decision given by this court in a case law reported in 14 BLD253 and their lordships in the case of Daliluddin Sheikh and others -vs.- Alek Sheikh alias Adul Malek Sheikh and others reported in 3XP(AD)7 held that there is no presumption of joint family in the Muslim Law but it appears that, sometimes after the death of father, all the members of that family use to reside and are in one mess and common income and in that position the property purchased in the name of one member of said family can be considered as property purchased for all. The learned Advocate also submits that earlier the plaintiffs in respect of self-same property and same relief instituted a Title Suit being No. 108 of 1999 which has been marked as Exhibit-"Jha". The suit was between the same parties. That suit was dismissed and two years after that; the present suit is filed by the plaintiffs for the same relief in respect of the same property with an additional prayer for partition and thereby this suit is not maintainable and barred by law. In this context; the learned Advocate referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 182 BLD (AD)54. The learned Advocate submits that admittedly the plaintiff's predecessor Madar Sarder was the elder brother and he had another brother Nur Mohammad by name. From Exhibit-"Gha" it appears that Mader Sardar personally by his presence prepared the S.A. record and subsequent to that; the R.S. record was prepared in the names of two brothers and their mother which is a document on record showing the bonafide of the defendants. It is in evidence that Madar Sarder alone never acquired the land and the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiffs are contradictory with one another and they have hopelessly failed to prove the alleged title and possession over the suit land. By virtue of Exhibit-4 the kabla deed it appears that the two brothers jointly sold out some properties and the case of the defendants is such that in the year 1990 the two sons of Madar Sander plaintiffs No. 1 and 2 purchased some land of the suit holding from Abdul Khaleque and from this document as well as form the examination-in-chief of the plaintiff's witness no.2 it is proved that the plaintiffs are possessing a particular portion of land as decided by the lower appellate court. In this context; the learned appellate court rightly held that in that portion of land the plaintiffs are entitled to get relief since their purchase is not challenged or disproved by any cogent evidence. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the defendants in the year 1984 mutated their names in respect of the suit land and paying rent regularly and the kabla deeds of the defendants dated 10.06.1969 and 02.12.1969 which has been marked as Exhibits-'Gha' and Uma are not challenged by the plaintiffs and as such it is admitted that these kabla deeds were executed by their predecessor Madar Sarder in respect of the suit holding. The learned appellate court in his observation and findings after proper assessment of evidence in its true perspective decided the matter-in-issue rightly in favour of the defendant No. 5 and in passing the impugned judgment and decree there is no infirmity or illegality done for which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

 10. On perusal of the case records it transpires that admittedly the property originally belonged to the landlord Enamul Hoque Biswas and Bagan Behara Sardar was a korfa tenant under the Ex-landlord. It is also an admitted position that there was an under khatian of the concerned C.S. khatian No.771 of suit mouza Madhabkhali and the area of the land was 54 decimals. It is also admitted that for arrears of rent the property was pot to an auction and the landlord Enamul Hoque Biswas auction-purchased the same. In a Rent Execution Case No.221 of 1952 the property which was auction-purchased by the landlord was proposed for settlement. It is the case of the plaintiffs that their predecessor Madar Sarder for his own interest and by his own money took settlement from the Ex-landlord and executed a registered kabuliyat on 25.02.1956. Vis-a-vis; it has been contended from the side of the contesting defendant-opposite party that after the death of Bagan Behara Sarder his two sons Madar Sarder and Nur Mohammad Sarder along with their mother were in a joint family and joint mess and it was decided by the two brothers that they would take settlement and accordingly on behalf of all the elder brother Madar Sarder executed the "kabuliyat" in favour of the landlord. Subsequently, during the S.A. record the elder brother recorded his name with his brother and mother's name in khatian No.602 which was finally published. In the instant case, the pertinent question which is the matter of adjudication is such as to whether the property is acquired alone by Madar Sarder or on behalf of all of the family members left behind Bagan Behara Sarder. It is a fact that the learned trial court during passing his judgment and decree examined six oral witnesses from the sides of the respective parties and decided the pertinent point in favour of the plaintiffs. Subsequently, the lower appellate court decided that the settlement in the name of Madar Sarder never effected and by virtue of that settlement nothing was acquired. Neither Madar Sarder nor Nur Mohammad Sarder nor their mother acquired any portion of land of the suit holding by virtue of the kabuliyat deed dated 25.02.1956 which has been marked as Exhibit-5 and Exhibit-`Ga' respectively from the sides of the respective parties. The proposition of law as cited with the recital of the impugned judgment and decree under the ambit of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act appears to be sound and cogent. Apart from this; the settlement followed by the kabuliyat marked as exhibit-5 was not completed as there is nothing to hold such a view that the Zaminder or the landlord ever obtained any salami or accepted rent from the settlement holder. Besides this; Section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1954 which takes it effect from 16.05.1951 have imposed a legal embargo in giving settlement by the landlord in favour of anybody. It has been properly appreciated by the learned District Judge, Satkhira in his findings. 

 12. On perusal of Exhibit-"Jha" it has come to the notice of this court that prior to this; the, plaintiffs instituted a separate Title Suit being No. 108 of 1999 which was dismissed and that suit was between the same parties in respect of same schedule of land. The present suit which has been preferred after two years of that is for the same relief along with a further relief in getting partition. In this regard; the decision referred to by the learned counsel for the opposite party reported in 1982 BLD (AD) 54 in the case of Kumar Begum Roy v. Panna Debi and others have got much importance in this case. Having regard to this; I like to advert that a fresh suit for achieving the same result by adopting indirect method is not permissible in the eye of law. Law does not allow the plaintiffs to get relief which was sought for in earlier suit between the same parties in respect of the same land which was dismissed earlier. 

 14. Having regard to the facts, circumstance and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the original suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 16. The impugned judgment and decree in part passed by the learned lower appellate court dated 25.10.2012 and 29.10.2012 respectively be set aside. The original suit be also dismissed on contest with costs.
